     LIGHTHOUSE GATE: the "flaps on runner noise" blocker is RETIRED (2026-07-22). It was three problems, not one. (1) TBT + the composite perf score are the only CPU-derived assertions and inflate ~30x on a contended runner (measured 434/435/1343ms in CI vs a median of 14ms locally) — both demoted to `warn`, budget numbers unchanged. (2) The config had no `aggregationMethod`, so LHCI defaulted to `optimistic` = BEST-of-N, which is why CI reported homepage CLS as 0,0,0 while it was deterministically 0.1868 — now `median`, runs 3->5. Expect reported numbers to look WORSE than pre-07-22 history; that is the gate becoming honest. (3) A REAL homepage CLS defect the gate was hiding: the platform fallback font is ~19% wider than Outfit and the hero is centred, so text slid HORIZONTALLY on font swap (nothing moved vertically — the obvious "reflow pushes content down" story was wrong). Fixed with a `size-adjust` metric-matched 'Outfit Fallback' face + a 100vh `.hero__deco-layer` for the decorations: CLS 0.1868 -> 0.0075, LCP unchanged 2709ms, perf 0.86 -> 0.94. Font preload also gets CLS to 0 but costs +377ms LCP (busts the 3000ms budget) — tested, rejected, anti-preload note left in BaseLayout.astro. Full record + deferred items: docs/plans/2026-07-22-lighthouse-gate-honesty-and-homepage-cls.md.      - 🆕 **CLOUDWATCH COST — free-tier alert root-caused and fixed 2026-08-29 (`67de1c18`, `716a6367`).** The alert was `Global-DataScannedBytes` (4.30 of 5 GB) — Logs Insights QUERY scanning, **not** log volume. Ingestion is only ~108 MB/month (2% of its own 5 GB allowance) and storage ~54 MB.
       - **Cause: the metrics collector, not the app.** Six separate Insights queries per run, each re-scanning its whole window = **~764 MB per run** (one 30-day query on the telemetry group scans ~106 MB; the 90-day last-seen scan ~315 MB). Running metrics daily would have cost ~23 GB/month.
       - **Fix: `.claude/skills/beanies-metrics/scripts/cw_cache.mjs`** — one incremental collector replacing all six. Caches a `(day, family, surface) → count` atom in `~/.config/beanies/metrics-cache.json` (every output derives from it) and queries only missing days, normally just today. **Measured 764 MB → 2.0 MB per run (~380x), 40s → 2s**, 148 MB one-time backfill. Output shape unchanged, so `build_dashboard.mjs` needed no edits. `--rebuild` forces a refetch; deleting the cache is always safe.
       - **Ingestion trimmed too** (every logged byte is re-scanned by every future query): `helpful-hints` (33% of all events, ~36/family/day — its watcher is `deep` on activities/members/vacations so any edit re-ran it) now emits on CHANGE plus a heartbeat, with the per-reason trace riding along instead of repeating; `save-status` (27%) always emits transitions into/out of trouble but samples the routine `saving→saved` pair 1-in-20, tagged so the true rate stays recoverable. Both via new `src/services/telemetry/emitPolicy.ts` (`createChangeGate` / `createSampler`, 12 tests).
       - **Deliberately NOT touched:** structured context, success-path events, and `load-perf` (38k events over its 250ms floor from 16 families is real signal about the sync-freeze issue, not noise).
       - **Log retention: every group now 90 days, none unbounded.** `oauth` (10.3 MB) and `registry` (1.4 MB) had NO retention — undeclared in Terraform, so Lambda auto-created them with "Never expire". Both are now declared resources, **imported into state** (a plain apply would fail on "already exists"), applied, and each Lambda `depends_on` its group so AWS cannot create the unbounded one first. `scripts/check-log-retention.mjs` guards it in CI (verified failing in the right direction).
       - ⚠️ **`content_fetch` "drift" was a FALSE ALARM — do not chase it.** An unsourced `terraform plan` renders live secrets as changes, because the secret-bearing `TF_VAR_*` fall back to declared defaults. **Always `source ~/.beanies-tf.env` first**; with it, the repo plans clean ("No changes"). Applying an unsourced plan would OVERWRITE the live secret with a default. Warning added to `infrastructure/README.md`.

     - 🆕 **TRACKER #76 — BIOMETRIC UNLOCK NOW SIGNS THE MEMBER IN. SHIPPED to iOS TestFlight + Google Play OPEN TESTING as 0.12 (2026-08-27, `df725271` + `7e822e99`).** Plan: `docs/plans/2026-08-27-biometric-unlocks-and-signs-in.md` (976 lines, four review passes + a five-reviewer codebase audit + a four-reviewer post-implementation review). A member's password does TWO jobs — decrypt the pod, and identify who is signing in. Biometric only ever replaced the first, so on the commonest path of all (sign out, come back, pod still cached) a device holding a good key was never offered it. The defect was ONE branch in `activateFamilyForBiometric` reasoning that "biometric decrypt would fail" — true, and beside the point. Also: the keystore item is now per member (`${familyId}:${memberId}`) so two beans can share a device; `useBiometricSignIn` is the one shared success tail; `MEMBER_MISMATCH` is the one sentinel; `resolveDeviceKeys` is the single answer to "which keys are here" (`hasRegisteredPasskeys` and `checkHasRegisteredPasskeys` both deleted with their last callers). 5077 tests, type-check + lint clean, iOS source guards green.
       - ✅ **PARTIALLY VERIFIED 2026-08-29: greg confirmed biometric unlock works on his iPhone 14** (0.13R3+). He said he would test more devices. The rest of the matrix below is still owed.

       - 🛑 **NEEDS GREG'S DECISION — on a SHARED device a member can sign in as a DIFFERENT member.** The OS prompt accepts any biometric enrolled on the device and every member's blob holds the same family key, so a child whose fingerprint is enrolled at OS level can pick a parent's bean and get owner permissions (finances, member removal, ownership transfer). Per-member addressing labels identity; it does not separate keys. This is LIVE on both test tracks.      - 🆕 **TRACKER #77 — REMOVING A MEMBER DOES NOT REVOKE THEIR ACCESS. NEW, not started, High.** Began as requirement 11 inside #76 and was split out on 2026-08-27 after an adversarial review found the designed envelope fix closes only ONE of six routes. The other five, each verified: the removed member's phone keeps the raw family key in the OS keystore (`nativeBiometric.ts:265` — no envelope is consulted); `settingsStore.cachedFamilyKeys` holds an unencrypted copy; `signInWithPasskey` never checks the roster; their Google Drive **writer** permission on the `.beanpod` and its parent folder is never revoked (there is NO permission-deletion helper in the codebase); and any invite link they held still works (`InviteKeyPackage` has no memberId, so a token cannot even be attributed to a member). Family-key rotation would fix neither Drive nor invites. ⚠️ The Help Center copy drafted during #76 ("their keys to the pod are destroyed") is NOT TRUE of an envelope-only fix and must not ship in that form.
     - 🔐 **PRE-EXISTING AUTH GAPS found by the #76 security review — each worth its own tracker row, none fixed.** (1) `setPassword` (`authStore.ts:1007`) has NO authorization check: any bean that never set a password can be claimed from the login screen by whoever holds the device — and the picker advertises exactly which beans those are with a "+" badge. (2) The session in localStorage is unsigned and web passkey assertions are never cryptographically verified, so editing one field yields another member's session. (3) PBKDF2 is at 100k iterations guarding the `.beanpod` envelope (current guidance is 600k). (4) iOS keychain items survive app uninstall but the registry that enumerates them does not, so per-member blobs can be orphaned beyond any code path. FIXED and shipped in 0.12: an untrusted sign-out now clears the cached family key (it was deleting the encrypted cache while leaving the key that decrypts it), pinned by tests in `dataClearingSecurity.test.ts`.

         - **How it was found:** CloudWatch, not guesswork. The iPhone was sending 36 telemetry events on build 34 and **not one from the share adapter** — so the adapter never ran, which meant `isPluginAvailable('ShareIntent')` was false, which meant the plugin was invisible to JS.
         - **Why.** Capacitor discovers plugins that ship inside npm PACKAGES on its own. A plugin defined in the **app target** is not discovered — it must be handed to the bridge explicitly in `capacitorDidLoad`. Android had always done the equivalent in `MainActivity.onCreate`; iOS had **no counterpart at all** (the storyboard pointed straight at the stock `CAPBridgeViewController`). `ios/App/App/MainViewController.swift` is now that counterpart.

         - **Why it survived three rounds: it is silent at EVERY layer.** The Swift compiles, the app launches, `isPluginAvailable` answers a plain `false`, and the JS reasonably reads that as an unsupported device. `useShareTargets` then did `if (!adapter.isSupported()) continue` — so a native build with a completely dead share target produced zero events.      2026-08-13 (SESSION 2 — ⭐ GOOGLE TOKEN-CHURN root-caused + fixed + deployed (tracker #62); revoke-breadth empirically resolved BROAD; two live-testing prod deploys): Started from a `/good-morning` where greg reported his Google account "keeps disconnecting" on all surfaces. **(1) ⭐ DIAGNOSED FROM CLOUDWATCH — not PR #61, not usage.** The app minted a new refresh token on every interactive (re)connect and NEVER revoked the one it replaced, on a **single OAuth client_id shared by Drive + Calendar**, so a heavy user accumulates tokens until Google's **100-per-account-per-client FIFO cap** silently revokes the *working* one (`invalid_grant`) → forced re-consent → mints another → self-sustaining loop. The account-mismatch handler auto-force-consenting on every mismatched acquisition was a second churn driver. Investigation doc: `docs/investigations/2026-08-13-google-token-churn-audit.md`. **(2) FULL PIPELINE:** `/beanies-new-issue` → tracker **#62** → `/beanies-pre-plan #62` → `/beanies-plan` (4-pass). Plan: `docs/plans/2026-08-13-google-token-churn-revoke-before-mint.md`. **(3) SHIPPED 5 of 6 commits (the core fix):** a single idempotent revoke helper (`googleRevoke.ts`); revoke-before-mint on Drive consent seams (`performPopupAuth`/`startRedirectAuth`, forceConsent-gated) + Calendar reconnect (guarded so it never kills a co-located live Drive grant); silent self-recovery in the syncStore permanent-expiry subscriber (deferred a macrotask — the callback fires inside the failing `performSilentRefresh` while its dedup is held, so an inline `tryReconnectSilently` deadlocks); sign-out revokes the durable REFRESH token; stopped the account-mismatch auto-consent (warn-once toast); `google-token-lifecycle` telemetry (client + Lambda mirror + the handler-test's THIRD hardcoded allowlist copy — caught only in CI, not the pre-push vitest). **(4) ⭐ REVOKE-BREADTH = BROAD.** Built `scripts/revoke-breadth-check.mjs` (loopback OAuth harness); greg ran it against the real client — revoking one token returned `invalid_grant` on a *separate* sibling. Whole-grant confirmed. Consequence: **removed the durable IndexedDB revoke queue entirely** — under whole-grant revoke a deferred retry is a time-bomb (drains after a replacement mint → kills the current grant). Revoke is now immediate best-effort, no retry (a healthy reconnect resets the whole pool to one anyway). **(5) `/code-review max`** (14 findings) — fixed the reading-independent ones (keepalive on the revoke fetch, 403→transient, fail-safe Drive-share guard, mint-telemetry timing + calendar mints, self-recovery `raceTimeout` bound, sign-out durable-refresh revoke, privacy teardown — later moot when the queue was removed). **(6) iOS "wrong google account" toast** — root-caused to `fetchGoogleUserEmail` returning a token-agnostic module cache: once primed (from the iPhone's persisted provider config, which named the file-owner account `beanies.demo`) it NEVER refetched, so the display/mismatch-toast/bound-account-check froze on the wrong account even after a clean gregsophia sign-in. Fixed by keying the cache to the access token it was verified against (`1245df8f`). **(7) DEPLOYS (`/deploy-prod-auto`):** **0.9.10** (patch, badge-only release note "your Google sign-in now stays connected reliably", web/PWA + **Android production** + iOS TestFlight); **0.9.10R1** (revision, no note, the iOS email-cache fix, same surfaces). **(8) ⚠️ greg's account jammed at the 100-token cap from extensive dual-account (gregsophia + beanies.demo) × 3-surface sign-in/out testing** → all surfaces `invalid_grant`, NO beanies revoke firing (his reconnects are on dead tokens = no-ops, so no whole-grant reset possible). A **TESTING ARTIFACT** (like the save-storm), not a real-user regression — fixed by a Google-console access-clear for both accounts + one clean single-account sign-in. Data was safe throughout (queued offline). **State:** working tree clean, `main` at `48468a2a`; branch `google-token-churn-fix` merged (ff) + deleted. See the Pending block for commit 5 + two follow-up gaps.

     2026-08-13 (SESSION WRAP — one issue taken from a vague concern to shipped-in-prod through the full new-issue → pre-plan → plan → review → deploy chain; the plan's core mechanism was REPLACED mid-flight on greg's push-back): **(1) ⭐ TRACKER #61 — open-cycle redundant loads.** Started from greg's concern that opens were doing double/redundant full loads on a 2-3MB pod. `/beanies-new-issue`: a code trace found **9 distinct redundancies**, and dedupe surfaced #57 (load-progress messaging) as a near-duplicate — greg's call was to SPLIT rather than merge, so #57 is untouched and #61 owns removing the wait while #57 owns communicating it. `/beanies-pre-plan #61` resolved 4 open questions (success = eliminate all provable redundancy without sacrificing data quality; halving is a stretch goal not a gate; audit ships as a committed `docs/investigations/` doc; ships UNGATED). **(2) ⭐ THE MECHANISM CHANGED MID-PLAN.** The 4-pass plan initially compared Drive `modifiedTime` and accepted a bounded 24h divergence window. **greg rejected that** ("if a device diverges, that's a legitimate reason to reload… a one-day divergence will erode trust") — correctly, and forcing "no window at all" exposed that the same bug class existed in TWO more places the mtime design had hidden. Rebuilt around Drive's monotonic **`version` counter** (no clock, no skew, no equal-but-different) captured from the write's own response, making divergence **structurally impossible** rather than merely bounded; backstop cut 24h → **1h** at greg's direction. Passes re-ran (7 total across 2 rounds) and found, among others: the telemetry allowlist lives in `diagnosticContext.ts` with a Lambda mirror so the drafted context keys would have been **silently stripped server-side**; a pre-`await` capture race that would have committed a baseline against a pre-merge doc. **(3) PR 1 SHIPPED + DEPLOYED as 0.9.9R10** (`eb14b7a5`, `e49398bf`, `ca8f1ad9`): `openCycle` per-open counters across all four open paths; `dirty`-gated re-upload (a read-only open was pushing a full 2-3MB file to Drive EVERY time); `changed`-gated re-projection; heads-based snapshot suppression (the `pagehide` flush was re-encrypting the whole projection on every background); deleted the dead `decryptBeanpodPayload`, so `automerge.remoteLoad` finally has exactly one emitter and the metric is trustworthy. **(4) `/code-review max` FOUND TWO REAL DATA BUGS I HAD INTRODUCED** — worth recording because both were invisible to a green suite: (a) gating the save on `dirty` stranded the recurring-dedup's own save, because `reloadAllStores()` calls `cancelPendingSave()` — my own code comment asserted the opposite; (b) `dirty` is heads-derived so it can never be true for an envelope-only change, which silently broke the documented "a passkey enrolled offline rides the next successful save" contract. Also: the reconstruction counter was counting cache MISSES (`time2` emits from a `finally`), `endOpen` had no ownership token so the header Refresh could close the real open's window, and every terminal emitted `open-complete` making the failure rate 0% by construction. Feedback is persisted nowhere else, so everything submitted from an app in that window is LOST. Fixed (`11718da3`): var added to all four lanes; the vite official-build guard now requires it; new `feedbackReporter` gate + boot warning; `workflowEnvParity.test.ts` drift tripwire (verified to fail when broken); `slackPost` returns an outcome; `feedbackSubmit` emits exactly one outcome event per submission (`surface: feedback-submit`, action dispatched|dropped_no_webhook|network_error|build_error) — success logged too so the drop RATE is measurable, which is why this month's loss is unquantifiable. Reuses the allowlisted `action` key: no ALLOWED_CONTEXT_KEYS change. **(2) ⭐ SILENT POD-FORKING — root-caused and fixed (`6d8726eb`, `9ecc4726`; ADR-033; plan `docs/plans/2026-08-10-never-fork-a-family-pod.md`, 4-pass).** A non-owner member on Android silently ended up on a private duplicate of the family `.beanpod`; identical-looking data, noticed only when her to-dos stopped reaching the family. Cause: `establishDurableHomeAfterLoad` treated "I don't own this Drive file" as "mint me a private copy" — but for EVERY non-owner member the family file is owned by the inviter and shared with edit access, so the guard fired for exactly the population it was meant to protect, seeding the copy with the live doc. `installProvider` then repointed the family REGISTRY at the copy, so `attemptSilentConfigHeal` could heal other members onto it. Regression window 2026-07-13 (`6004ad6c`) → 2026-08-10. Fix: `ownedByMe` is no longer consulted on any load path (`capabilities/canEdit` is the writability signal — a NESTED Drive field; a flat read is `undefined` on every healthy file, pinned by a test); `verifyPodAccess` replaces the re-home and MUTATES NOTHING; `reHomeToOwnDrive`/`mintFreshOwnDrive`/`configureSyncFileGoogleDrive` deleted; 7 typed codes → 4 recoveries that ALL point back at the original file; `rebindPodFile` (was `recoverFromMissingFile`) gained the missing `provider.persist` without which a re-pick survived only until the tab closed; CANONICAL_MISMATCH banner is the symptom the incident had no way to surface. **Pointer authority is enforced in the registry LAMBDA, not the client** — the client cannot close the hole because the propagation vector is already deployed on native/cached builds. Authority is `ownerMemberId` (stable UUID), NOT `ownerEmail` (a user-editable profile field that would lock an owner out on an email change); legacy email-only rows upgrade themselves on the owner's next accepted write. Terraform applied + verified end-to-end against the dev table (owner accepted / member refused / owner-after-email-change accepted / member metadata still lands). greg's own row upgraded cleanly to his member id. Prod registry inspected: a stale `6a08e644` "Test" row pointing at greg's real family file (written once on 2026-07-13) was deleted; 9 rows with null `ownerEmail` also have null `createdAt` — they predate the 2026-04-12 commit that added both fields and have been dormant since, deliberately NOT backfilled. **(3) ⚠️ PROD INCIDENT — a crippled build was live on app.beanies.family from 12:24 to ~13:0x SGT.** Found only because feedback tests failed from Chrome but worked in the PWA (which was serving a cached CI bundle). **ROOT CAUSE — my first attribution was WRONG:** it was not a stray local `dist/` sync, it was `translation-sync.yml`'s own `Deploy to PROD` job, which built with a "deliberately reduced subset" of env and ran `aws s3 sync dist/ --delete` over the app bucket. Evidence: run 31355217774's deploy job ran 04:21:43–04:24:15 UTC = 12:24 SGT, matching the S3 timestamps exactly, and the broken bundle's env map matches that job's env list exactly. Effect: NO Slack error webhook, no pod-create ping, no feedback webhook, no analytics, no AI-extract — undoing the preceding proper deploy, and recurring on every translation change. It bypassed the vite official-build guard because that guard only runs when `VITE_BUILD_SHA` is set. Fixed (`3fb12ae2`): the rogue deploy job is DELETED (deploy.yml is the only sanctioned path; deliberately not auto-dispatching it either, since prod deploys are manual by project rule), and `[skip ci]` dropped from the bot commit (it skipped every workflow for that push, so deploy.yml's same-SHA CI gate had nothing to check and `main` was un-deployable until CI was dispatched by hand — which blocked the first restore attempt). Audited every workflow that can write an S3 bucket: only deploy.yml + deploy-web.yml remain. **(4) BUILD-INTEGRITY ALARM (`7c25b28e`).** The dev-build-on-cloud-host guard has existed since June 2026 but only `console.error`d. `reportError` CANNOT page here — a dev build has no error webhook, which IS the condition — so the escalation is server-side: the client emits `logEvent({surface:'boot-integrity', flush:true})` (ingest is reachable in that state) and the telemetry Lambda forwards an allowlisted surface set to Slack from its own env var. Awaited not fire-and-forget (Lambda freezes on return); never throws (the CloudWatch line is the primary artifact and a 500 would make the client retry and duplicate). Note the guard is dead-code-eliminated from CI bundles by design — `build_sha` is inlined, so the branch is statically false; it ships only in the builds that can trigger it (verified: present in the bad dev bundle, absent from three CI bundles). **LIVE AFTER THIS SESSION:** web/Astro on `7c25b28e` (0.9.9R6) — NOTE `3fb12ae2` is CI-only and needs no deploy; registry + telemetry Lambdas applied; Android 0.9.9R6 in Google review; iOS unchanged (awaiting Apple). **Pending block re-validated 2026-08-10: 0 stale items dropped** (all four carried fingerprints re-confirmed open); 7 new items added, the load-bearing one being the deferred two-device convergence check.

The issue's Scope now names hand-verification on greg's actual desktop as an acceptance criterion. **(6) Blog category badges** — `content.config.ts` had `category: z.string()`, so three categories (feature announcement / founder story / memoir) rendered with no badge.      2026-07-24 (SESSION WRAP — earlier session: ⭐ #55 SILENT-REMINDER FIX SHIPPED: Android reminders now sound + vibrate; web PROD + Android 0.9.7 vc18 to closed testing): Live prod = web `713f2ac2` (deploy run `30052704541`), marketing site current, Android `0.9.7` **versionCode 18** on the `alpha` track (run `30052705859`, auto-submitted for Google review). Flow: /good-morning → greg reported reminders firing with NO sound and NO vibration → read the plugin source → single-commit fix → /deploy-prod-auto (web + Android alpha). **(1) GREG CONFIRMED at session start:** #55 Android build is now **GA-APPROVED on Play**, and reminders **fire even after force-kill** (the cold-start regression that silently deleted every armed reminder is verified fixed on-device). Reboot survival not yet tried. **(2) THE SILENT-REMINDER ROOT CAUSE.** On Android O+, sound/vibration are properties of the *channel*, not the notification, and a channel's settings are **frozen at first creation** (every later `createChannel` with the same id is a no-op). Our `reminders` channel was created with only `importance: 4` (HIGH). Reading `@capacitor/local-notifications`'s `NotificationChannelManager.java`: `createChannel` **defaults `vibration` to false and calls `enableVibration(false)` explicitly** — so an omitted flag is an *actively disabled* buzz, not an Android default. Sound: `setSound` runs only if a `sound` is passed, so a fresh HIGH channel keeps the constructor's default notification sound — meaning a truly fresh install would sound-but-not-vibrate, while greg's dev device (which has had the `reminders` channel since an early build) was frozen silent on both. **(3) THE FIX** (`713f2ac2`, `useLocalNotifications.ts`): ship under a NEW channel id `reminders_v2` with `vibration: true`; `deleteChannel({ id: 'reminders' })` on init to retire the frozen one; **leave `sound` UNSET** — any value routes the plugin to `android.resource://…/raw/<name>`, and there is no bundled raw sound, so passing one would MUTE the channel; unset = OS default sound. `buildScheduledNotifications` now targets `reminders_v2`. Two new tests (vibration ON + legacy retire; failing delete doesn't fail the arm). **(4) THE IMMUTABILITY TRAP is why a new id was mandatory** — bumping only `vibration: true` on the same id would have fixed nothing on any device that already had the channel (greg's, every tester's). **(5) NO release note / NO APP_VERSION bump** (greg's call, matching the app-icon precedent): vc18 carries the same `versionName 0.9.7` as the GA build, distinguishable only by versionCode; in-app what's-new bell still reads 2026.07.23. **(6) CLASSIFIER GAP worth remembering:** `scripts/deploy/classify-changes.sh` reported `MOBILE: no` for this change because it only flags native-specific paths (`android/`, capacitor config) — but this is JS that ships *inside* the AAB and is `isNative`-gated, so it reaches users only via a new Android build. Shipped the Android release on greg's explicit instruction despite the `no`. Gates green: type-check, full suite 3995 passed (pre-push), lint, main-ci + security.

     2026-07-22 (SESSION WRAP — later session: Lighthouse gate made honest, homepage CLS fixed + DEPLOYED, LCP hypothesis disproven + reverted): Live prod = marketing site `edcffa31` (deploy-web run `29909007622`); the Vue app and Android are untouched by this session. Flow: /good-morning → STATUS correction → Lighthouse diagnosis → /beanies-plan (4 passes) → implement → /deploy-prod-auto → LCP diagnosis → /beanies-plan (4 passes) → implement → CI measurement → REVERT. **(1) ⭐ THE GATE WAS LYING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and it was three problems, not the one "flakiness" STATUS recorded.** Detail in the LIGHTHOUSE GATE block above. Short version: TBT + perf-score are the only CPU-derived assertions and inflate ~30x on a contended runner (434/435/1343ms in CI vs a median of **14ms** on a quiet machine) → demoted to `warn`, budget numbers unchanged; the config had no `aggregationMethod` so LHCI defaulted to `optimistic` = **best-of-N**, which is why CI reported homepage CLS as `0,0,0` while it was deterministically **0.1868** (~2x budget) → now `median`, runs 3→5. Justifications live in the `lighthouse-ci.yml` header because lighthouserc.json cannot hold comments. ⚠️ Reported numbers now look WORSE than pre-07-22 history — that is the gate becoming honest, do NOT "fix" it. **(2) ⭐ REAL HOMEPAGE CLS DEFECT FIXED AND DEPLOYED — the only user-visible change of the session.** The platform fallback font is ~19% wider than Outfit and the hero is centre-aligned, so on font swap the headline/button/link slid **horizontally** (nothing moved vertically — the obvious "reflow pushes content down" story was wrong, and direct measurement refuted it: every `y` identical, only widths changed). Fixed with a `size-adjust: 95.5%` metric-matched `'Outfit Fallback'` face (`local()` chain of Arial-metric faces so one tuning covers Linux/Windows/macOS) + a `100vh` `.hero__deco-layer` that stops ten decorations riding the hero's content-driven height. **CLS 0.1868 → 0.0075 local, 0.018 on CI; LCP unchanged 2709ms; perf 0.86 → 0.94.** Font preload also reaches CLS 0 but costs **+377ms LCP** (busts the 3000ms budget; `fetchpriority="low"` does not help) — tested, rejected, anti-preload note left in `BaseLayout.astro`. The fallback is honestly named rather than overloading bare `Outfit`, which `discord.astro:35` and `plausible-exclude.astro:25` declare with no `Outfit Variable` and would have silently switched to a system face. **(3) ⚠️ THE LCP FIX FAILED AND WAS REVERTED — read this before retrying.** Detail in the HOMEPAGE LCP block above. Profiled `buildBraid()` at 98% of the beanstalk's startup block (243ms desktop / 894ms at 4x throttle, matching CI's 819ms). Deferred it behind an IntersectionObserver: script eval **858→32ms**, TBT **390→0ms**, the chunk vanished from `bootup-time` — and **LCP moved 3ms** (3162.5→3158.9), while FCP **regressed ~1.7s→~2.6s** (0.89→0.65, tight, not noise; NOT the pending-hide — `visibility:hidden` changed nothing). Reverted `cc03bbad`+`bbc9c4ac` → `64cac410`; component byte-identical to its pre-attempt state, plan kept with the negative result recorded. **LCP is INVARIANT at ~3160ms across three materially different builds** — it is not gated by page work, so the plan's Step 3 (build-time braid precompute) is DEAD (it removes the same work to zero effect). Next attempt must explain the invariant first; my untested hunch is Lantern's simulated critical-path graph pinning it rather than observed timings. **(4) Method note worth keeping:** local measurement misled me **twice** today (claimed LCP was trustworthy from a 0.1% *within-run* spread — it varies 17% across environments; and named the 112KB inline CSS as the LCP suspect — CI shows Parse HTML & CSS is **56ms**). Flow: /frontend-design icon audit → 3 background candidates → greg supplied a Gemini-generated light-background asset → technical audit + repair → full icon-set generation → /deploy-prod-auto. **(1) THE DIAGNOSIS.** The old icon (family-hugging illustration on white) is five characters, five hats and ~50 outline strokes inside a 48px tile — it reduced to a smudge at notification/launcher sizes, and Android's circle mask clipped the two outer kids. It stays in use for onboarding, empty states and the marketing site, where it has room. The father+son mark replaced it — one dominant slate silhouette carries the tile. **(2) THE REAL BUG, in BOTH the old PWA icon and greg's new asset:** the arrow is `#ED4F1D` on a `#FF832B` ground — same hue, separated only by a white sticker keyline, and **sub-pixel white keylines are the first detail lost when the OS downsamples**. Fixed by replacing the ground with a single sky→cream gradient (`#E8F3FC → #FBF7F1 → #FDDDBC`) so the arrow is the only saturated shape. Also removed the hard horizon band (read as two stacked rectangles), filled the baked white rounded-corner wedges for full-bleed, and killed a `#F48939` corner stroke + a stray sparkle. **Artwork itself untouched** — greg's explicit constraint; only the background changed. **(3) 34 FILES from one 1024² master**, generated by a pure-python PNG pipeline (no PIL/ImageMagick on this host — decode/encode/box-resample written by hand; scripts in the session scratchpad, not committed): iOS AppIcon flattened to **opaque RGB** (alpha fails App Store review); 24 Android mipmaps across 6 densities (square, round, + the two adaptive layers); PWA/apple-touch/OG at 192+512 mirrored into `web/`; a **new maskable 512** at 62% wired into the manifest with `purpose: maskable`; and `assets/icon-{only,foreground,background}.png` so a `capacitor-assets` regen reproduces this instead of reverting it. The adaptive foreground is the artwork with the background knocked out **pixel-exactly** (background pixels equal `grad(y)` by construction, so alpha derives by exact comparison) — `ic_launcher.xml` already insets both layers 16.7%, so the launcher masks the gradient and never the beanies. **Retired `public/icons/icon-{192,512}.png`** — they carried the full wordmark, unreadable below 120px; nothing in `src/` referenced them. ⚠️ **greg chose NO release note and NO `APP_VERSION` bump**, so this Android build carries the same `versionName 0.9.6` as yesterday's (distinguishable only by versionCode 14) and the in-app what's-new bell still shows 2026.07.21. ⚠️ **Went straight to production without an internal-track check** — the adaptive icon has never been seen on a real launcher. ⚠️ **CI detour worth remembering:** resolving a rebase conflict in CHANGELOG.md **bypasses the lint-staged prettier hook**, so CI failed on format; the CHANGELOG-only fix commit then **skipped CI entirely** (`main-ci.yml`/`security.yml` both carry `paths-ignore: ['*.md']`), and `deploy.yml`'s gate hard-fails when no CI run exists for HEAD — had to `gh workflow run` both manually. Fixed with greg's chosen **block-early** approach: new `syncStore.canDurablySaveNow()` gate returns `noConnection` (calm "you'll need a connection" copy) BEFORE mutating when a durable save is confidently impossible (no provider, or Drive provider while `navigator.onLine===false`; a local-file provider is never blocked). (2) **unverified rollback** — `restoreCredential` discarded `updateMember`'s return + the region was unguarded, so a failed rollback silently reported "nothing changed" while the local doc held the NEW hash (silent device lockout). Fixed: `restoreCredential` now returns a verified boolean, fully guarded, and emits `critical` + a distinct `rollbackFailed` error ("sign out and back in") on ANY rollback failure (setter throw OR null hash-restore — the latter caught by a unit test during impl). Also: new `syncStore.syncNowDurable(ms): 'saved'|'failed'|'timeout'` three-state save is now the SINGLE core (the old `!!(raceTimeout(...))` `syncNowBounded` folded into a one-line wrapper over it — restores the documented single-home invariant); a post-write `syncNow` reject maps to `'saved'` (the Drive write succeeded, only the metadata write threw → never misreport a durable save as failed, never false-page); convergence re-save + `critical` now fire ONLY on the genuinely-ambiguous `'timeout'` case, not on clean offline failures; reset-modal got a `catch` (no-silent-failures); stale `updateFailed` copy corrected + new `noConnection`/`rollbackFailed`/`unexpected` keys (en+beanie+zh). signin-heal untouched (best-effort).      2026-07-13 (session 2): 🐛→✅ DOC-WORKER DEATH RECOVERY — CODE-COMPLETE ON `main`, NOT YET DEPLOYED (awaiting greg's deploy). /error-review of greg's morning `#beanies-errors` batch (6 alerts across 2 families + 3 device classes: `initAndLoadCache`/`flush`/`getHeads`/`exportEncryptedPayload`/`setKey` timeouts + a desktop `app.onboardingStallTimeout`) — reproduced first-hand: data fails to load in the PWA, force-close+reopen fixes it. ROOT CAUSE (verified in code, NOT a #43 load-speed issue): the client had **no recovery from a worker that goes silent without firing `onerror`** — recovery was wired ONLY to `worker.onerror`; the RPC-timeout path just `pending.delete(cid); throw`, so once the worker is OS-reaped (backgrounded mobile PWA) or FIFO-wedged behind a hung whole-doc op, every subsequent RPC re-posts to the corpse and times out until force-quit. Fix (4-pass /beanies-plan, `docs/plans/2026-07-13-worker-death-recovery.md`, all in `src/services/automerge/worker/`): (1) extracted `recoverDeadWorker()` (shared teardown+drain, no toast); (2) a timeout now recovers the worker + auto-retries ONCE on a fresh respawn for a **fail-safe `RETRYABLE` allowlist** (`mutate`/`initDoc` never retry → no double-applied financial op) — with a `heavyStillInFlight` guard so a light 45s timeout NEVER tears down a legitimately-progressing heavy 120s load (implementation-time catch: the existing two-tier-timeout test flagged this regression), and a single `lostSiblings`-gated consolidating toast so a silent heal can't swallow a concurrent `mutate`'s failure (Pass-4 catch); (3) a no-op `ping` dispatch op + `checkWorkerLiveness()` (5s ceiling); (4) `bootstrap.ts` fires the ping on `visibilitychange`→visible so a background-reaped worker self-heals on resume (kills the force-quit requirement). +9 unit tests; full suite **3806 green**, type-check + lint clean. SEPARATE from Notion #43 (load-speed floor) by design — this recovery fix DEMOTES #43 from data-availability bug to optimization. **⚠️ NEEDS DEPLOY + a version bump** (recommend `0.9.4R11`); no in-app release note needed (reliability fix, CHANGELOG-only). Rollback lever unchanged: revert the `docWorker` flag + redeploy. **✅ DEPLOYED as `0.9.4R11` (commit `5d6b0542`, deploy run success, 2026-07-13); `doc-worker-recovery` telemetry now flowing.**

> ## ⭐ ADR-032 worker migration — LIVE IN PROD (docWorker prod-ON as of 2026-07-07)
>
> **Status: `docWorker` is now flipped prod-ON — the off-main-thread Automerge engine + B1/B2 incremental delta sync run for ALL prod users as of app `0.9.4` (deployed 2026-07-07).** The gradual rollout is complete: greg verified on a real iPhone (two test families, no main-thread freeze, large-doc load faster than before) and the flag was flipped fleet-wide. Rollback = revert the one-line flag in `featureFlags.committed.ts` + redeploy (no data/schema change to undo). **Latest prod = app `0.9.4`.** (Prior: `0.9.3` shipped the iOS redirect-auth race fix + B1/B2; `0.9.2R4` shipped the cross-family data-integrity fix.)
>
> > **✅ Create-family data-integrity fix (DESKTOP-VERIFIED by greg 2026-07-06).** Creating a new family from an active session leaked the previous family's data and could lose the just-created onboarding activity. Root causes + fix in `docs/plans/2026-07-06-create-family-state-teardown.md`; all in `authStore.ts`: (D1/D2) new `resetInMemoryFamilyState()` runs `docClient.reset()`→`initDoc()`→`familyStore.resetState()`→`reloadAllStores()` in `buildOwnerDoc` (clears all ~21 stores + nulls the worker key so pre-pod mutations can't write the old family's cache); (D3) sign-out wrapper renamed `flushPendingSaveWithTimeout`→`forceSaveWithTimeout`, now `saveNow()` unconditionally before `deleteFamilyDatabase` so the freshest edit reaches Drive. greg confirmed no data overlap AND account+activity persist across sign-out.
> >
> > **✅ 10-finding worker-migration hardening** (`docs/plans/2026-07-06-worker-migration-hardening.md`): `onMissing` tri-state, `WorkerCrashError`, `RpcOk.changed`, `openCache`, `persistEnvelopeSafely`, `fireAndForgetMutate`, `collectionRef` — all fixed, suite green.
> >
> > **iOS onboarding loop (2026-07-06, tunnel test) — NOT a migration regression.** An iPhone create-flow loop hit via a `trycloudflare.com` tunnel was diagnosed to `tokenValid=false` after every OAuth redirect return, in OAuth code **byte-identical to `main`** (`createNewFile` never reached). It is the classic iOS-Safari + ephemeral-tunnel ITP/bounce-tracking artifact (token wiped across the cross-site bounce on an unfamiliar domain; consistent with ADR-026). The real `app.beanies.family` domain has first-party standing and is unaffected. **Validate real-iOS onboarding on prod post-deploy**, then flip `docWorker` prod-on gradually. **⚠️ AMENDED 2026-07-07:** the ITP/tunnel explanation was **incomplete**. A separate, real init-ordering race was root-caused (3-agent investigation) and **fixed** on `main`: the first "sign in to an existing family" on iOS failed because the resume/family-list consumers read `isTokenValid()` while `completeRedirectAuth`'s code→token exchange was still in flight (App.vue flips the reactive auth state _before_ it redeems the code) → misclassified as a hard auth failure; the second tap worked (no re-consent). This reproduces on the **real first-party domain** (first-fail → second-success → no-re-consent is the race's fingerprint, distinct from ITP eviction). Fix: a shared memoized `ensureRedirectAuthSettled()` the consumers await first (`docs/plans/2026-07-07-ios-redirect-auth-race.md`). Do NOT re-dismiss a first-attempt iOS sign-in failure as a tunnel quirk.
> >
> > **✅ iOS onboarding + persistence + cross-device sync (inline path) — VERIFIED on real iPhone + 2nd machine (greg, 2026-07-06).** Deploy `1738b1d4` shipped (docWorker prod-off). Confirmed on `app.beanies.family`: fresh account create → sign out → sign in persists; account/activity/member present on a 2nd machine.

> > **✅ iOS worker large-doc timeout — Layer-1 fix IMPLEMENTED + DEPLOYED (`56317341`; shipped in deploy `d60a5c81` / app `0.9.2R3`, 2026-07-06).** greg enabled the worker on his iPhone via the per-browser `localStorage` override and loading his ~2 MB `.beanpod` hit the fixed 45 s RPC ceiling. 4-agent investigation: Automerge WASM `load`/`merge` (~5–15× slower on iOS JSC) + redundant whole-doc work; the fixed uniform 45 s timeout killed a slow-but-progressing load. Fix (`docs/plans/2026-07-06-worker-ios-large-doc-load.md`, 4-pass reviewed): central `HEAVY_METHODS` Set → 120 s bounded ceiling for whole-doc ops (45 s kept for mutations); dropped redundant `Automerge.clone(local)` in `mergeDocs`; delta projection on poll-merge (`projectionDeltasBetween` via `Automerge.diff`, `ProjectionDelta[]|null` + logged full-rebuild fallback); narrowed `postRaw` so the ~2 MB payload isn't main-thread JSON-round-tripped; `pushProjection` telemetry + `mergeClone`→`merge`. +13 worker tests; full suite 3517 green; type-check + lint clean. **NOT a data-safety issue; prod still safe on inline.**
> >
> > **✅ Large-doc load VERIFIED on iPhone (worker override, 2026-07-06):** the ~2 MB file now LOADS (>30 s but completes, no timeout error — the Layer-1 fix works). The 30 s+ is the residual `Automerge.load` floor → Layer 2.
> >
> > **🐛→✅ Cross-family data mixing (round 2) — ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED on `main` (2026-07-06).** Testing the worker on iPhone, greg hit family-data mixing again. 2-agent investigation cleared the Layer-1 delta change and found a **pre-existing, delta-independent** bug (in shared code — affects inline/prod too, for genuine cross-family switches on trusted devices): **Gap 1** — `signOut` on a _trusted_ device never reset the in-memory worker doc (`docClient.reset()` only ran via `deleteFamilyDatabase`, gated `!trusted`), so family A's doc survived sign-out; **Gap 2** — `replaceDocWithCacheRecovery` ignored `initAndLoadCache`'s `{loaded}`, so on a cache MISS (iOS ITP evicts it) it CRDT-merged B's remote into the residual A doc → A∪B persisted + uploaded to B's `.beanpod` (durable). Fix (both gaps, defence-in-depth): `authStore.signOut` now calls `docClient.reset()` unconditionally (keeps the cache DB for trusted fast re-login); `replaceDocWithCacheRecovery` drops the doc on a non-hit so the remote is adopted fresh, never merged into a foreign doc. +3 tests (trusted-device reset; cache-miss dropDoc-before-merge; cache-hit no-drop). Full suite 3520 green; type-check + lint clean. **NOTE:** greg's iPhone test-family B `.beanpod` is already durably polluted from the pre-fix runs — the code fix can't un-merge CRDT data; that test file should be deleted/recreated.

> > 2. **🛑 BLOCKED — do NOT retire dual-publish yet (Notion #44). Instrument the incremental path first.** Investigated 2026-07-09 (session 2) against real CloudWatch telemetry; the OQ4 exit criteria are **unmet on two counts**, and the change as scoped would be unsafe. Findings:
> >
> >    - **The health signal OQ4 names does not exist.** STATUS previously said to watch `missing-deps` telemetry. There is no such event. Every fallback reason in `incrementalTransport.ts` (`missing-deps`, `list-failed`, `read-failed`, `chunk-missing`, `apply-error`) terminates in a bare `console.warn` at `syncService.ts:749` — never `logEvent`, so nothing reaches CloudWatch. The incremental path emits nothing on success either, and `perfTiming.ts`'s `TELEMETRY_FLOOR_MS = 250` means fast chunk applies are invisible by construction. **The incremental path is unobservable in prod, in both directions.**
> >    - **The version stamp OQ4 requires was never built.** The plan (`docs/plans/2026-07-07-worker-incremental-delta-sync.md:160`) gates removal on stamping the writing client's minimum-compatible version into the base envelope/registry, to prove no whole-doc-only client still touches files. Grep for `minCompat`/`minVersion`/`writerVersion` → nothing. Build-SHA telemetry is a weak proxy (only sees clients that report; blind to a stale-service-worker client).
> >    - **What telemetry there is (Jul 7+, fleet of 2–5 families):** 2,793 whole-doc base adopts vs **1** delta-chunk apply; 11 `automerge.saveIncremental`, 1 `automerge.saveBase`. No errors on any sync path. **Do not read this as "deltas are broken"** — 2,785 of the base adopts are one single-device family (`ae92950b`, greg's own), and a single-device family has no peer chunks, so incremental correctly returns `noop` and falls through. The honest read is **the delta path has barely been exercised in production at all.** (Note: `automerge.remoteLoad` is overloaded — it labels both the whole-doc adopt (`applyAndProject.ts:355`, carries a byte count) and the delta-chunk decrypt (`:489`, no byte count). Split them on the byte suffix.)
> >    - **⚠️ The real hazard: pruning is licensed BY the base write.** `pruneOwnChunks` (`incrementalTransport.ts:176`) deletes own-chunks older than `OWN_CHUNK_KEEP = 12`, justified in-comment by _"the base we just wrote is a superset of our own history."_ Remove the base write while `publishIncremental` still prunes → the change-log discards chunks whose only durable home was the base. **That is permanent data loss on a user's `.beanpod`, not a degraded-sync bug.** Three other things hang off the same write: `recordPersistedBytes(fileContent)` one line below feeds the `beanpodSizeKb` registry signal (shipped `0.9.5`); the `outcome: 'fallback'` branch assumes the base carries missing deps; the mixed-fleet reconcile assumes the base is current.
> >
> >    - **✅ NOT a data-loss risk TODAY (verified 2026-07-09).** The pruning precondition is genuinely enforced in shipped code — the hazard above is strictly conditional on _removing_ the base write. Chain checked link-by-link: (a) `publishIncremental` has exactly **one** call site (`syncService.ts:858`), seven lines after `await currentProvider.write(fileContent)`; (b) that `write` is awaited and its rejection propagates to `doSave`'s outer `catch`, so a failed base write can never reach `pruneOwnChunks` (the permission-denied path returns even earlier); (c) `pruneOwnChunks` only deletes chunks matching **this device's own** `actorId` with `seq < publishSeq - 12`, whose content is by definition already inside the whole-doc base just written — another device's chunks are never touched; (d) chunks are an accelerator, never a sole home — every delta failure returns `fallback` and the caller re-runs the unchanged whole-doc merge. The line-176 comment is an accurate statement of a real, currently-enforced precondition. **OQ4 deletes that precondition while leaving the code that depends on it.**
> >    - **🐛 NEW FINDING — chunks accumulate without bound → filed as Notion #46 "Beanpod change files accumulate without limit in the user's Google Drive" (Bug, Normal, `Not started`). Independent of #44; worth fixing regardless.** `Automerge.load`/`init` are called with **no explicit actor** (`docOps.ts:47,258`, `applyAndProject.ts:260`), so Automerge mints a **fresh random `actorId` every session**. `pruneOwnChunks` prunes only its own `actorId`, and `publishSeq` resets to 0 each session — so a device **never prunes the chunks it wrote in any previous session**, and no other device will either (each prunes only its own). `OWN_CHUNK_KEEP = 12` bounds only the _current_ session. The `changes/` folder in the user's Drive grows forever. (Corollary: the header comment's "names are never reused" is true, but via the rotating `actorId`, **not** the monotonic seq — if `actorId` were ever pinned across sessions, `publishSeq` restarting at 0 would silently **overwrite** existing chunk names. Do not pin the actor without also persisting `publishSeq`.)
> >    - **🐛 NEW FINDING — every fresh session's first pull re-reads the entire chunk history.** `pullIncremental` treats any name not in the **in-memory** `fetched` set as fresh, and `fetched` starts empty (`newTransportSession()`). So each new session's first poll lists + downloads **every chunk ever written by every device**, then applies them. Automerge's apply is idempotent so it stays _correct_, but the cost grows monotonically with the (unbounded, per above) folder. On a long-lived family this gets slow, and it **plausibly contributes to why the delta path looks so unexercised in telemetry** — the whole-doc base adopt may simply be winning. This sharpens the sequencing below: instrumenting first is the only way to see whether this is already biting real users.
> >
> >    **Sequenced fix (do in order):** (1) **instrument** — route the fallback reasons through `logEvent` (surface `incremental-sync`) and count chunk applies/publishes unconditionally, below the perf floor; small + safe, ships standalone. (2) Add the **writer-version stamp** per OQ4. (3) **Let it run** until there's real multi-device delta traffic to look at. (4) **Then** retire the base write, reworking `pruneOwnChunks` in the same change. Step (1) is the natural next commit → `/beanies-plan`. **Also update the Notion #44 removal criteria** to say "instrument, _then_ watch" — the current wording implies a signal that was never wired up, which is what nearly sent this session in the wrong direction. Rollback lever for the whole worker remains: revert the flag in `featureFlags.committed.ts` + redeploy.

> ### What this migration is
>
> Move the Automerge doc + persistence pipeline OFF the main thread into a Web Worker (fixes the load-freeze; ADR-032 + `docs/plans/2026-07-05-automerge-web-worker.md` + `docs/plans/2026-07-05-worker-migration-cutover-tasks-4-6.md`). Main thread keeps a read-only reactive `projection`; stores read it sync, write via async `docClient` RPC. Shipped behind a `docWorker` kill-switch (**dev-on / prod-off**, so prod runs the inline fallback until flipped). **Transparent to users — no re-login; `.beanpod` V4 / encryption / cache DB all unchanged.**

> ## 🔬 Drive reconnect loop — INSTRUMENTED + DEPLOYED (app `0.9.4R6`); root cause STRONGLY suspected, not yet confirmed
>
> **DEPLOYED 2026-07-09 23:44 UTC** — commit `7e0e0b85`, deploy run `29058070034`. Telemetry Lambda applied via terraform (`module.telemetry` only; a single in-place `source_code_hash` update, zero other resource changes; deployed `CodeSha256` verified byte-for-byte against the local zip). Live bundle confirmed carrying `build_sha 7e0e0b85`, `APP_VERSION 0.9.4R6`, and the `silent-refresh:*` discriminator. No in-app release note, per greg.
>
> **⭐ LEADING HYPOTHESIS (2026-07-10): the OAuth consent-screen scopes were dropped.** Google Cloud audit logs show **two `UpdateClientWithMask` events by `gparker97@gmail.com` on 2026-07-06** (07:44:52Z, 08:31:39Z). The **first token failure is 2026-07-06 12:29:19Z** — hours later, the same day. That is **a full day BEFORE the `docWorker` prod-ON flip (2026-07-07)**, which exonerates the ADR-032 worker migration by clock rather than by argument. `drive.file` + `userinfo.email` were found missing from the consent screen on 2026-07-09 and re-added; **no toast on any device in the 6+ hours since**. Best-fit mechanism: while `drive.file` was unregistered, Google kept _issuing_ refresh tokens for the grant but invalidated them shortly after — which explains `invalid_grant` (rather than "no token"), the recurrence after every re-consent, and the recovery on re-adding the scopes.
>
> **NOT the mechanism Gemini proposed** ("Google refuses to issue a refresh token, leaving only a 1-hour access token"). Refuted by the logs: no `auth-no-refresh-token` alert ever fired despite repeated interactive reconnects, and the calendar errors read `Token has been expired or revoked` — a token that was issued, then killed.
>
> **⏳ CONFIRMATION PENDING — hold 2026-07-16/17.** greg re-consented 2026-07-09. If that token is still alive past the 7-day mark, no expiry clock is in play and the scope story stands. If a toast reappears, the now-deployed telemetry reports `refresh_token_age_ms` on the _first_ occurrence. Record the value here either way.
>
> **Symptom:** the orange "Google session expired" toast on almost every tab open / PWA resume, across all browsers, from ~2026-07-06.
>
> **What is proven.** Google returns `400 invalid_grant — "Token has been expired or revoked"` for the refresh token, while the grant **remains listed** in the user's linked apps. The client's behaviour is correct: it clears the dead token and stops retrying. The empty `beanies-file-handles/handles` store is a _consequence_ of Google's rejection, not a cause. Ruled out by evidence, not argument: the ADR-032 worker migration (different IndexedDB database, untouched since 2026-05-22); `googleAccountAssertion` (never fired — no `[accountAssertion]` line in the console log); Testing-mode 7-day expiry (app is `In production`, branding + data access verified, sensitive calendar scope approved); an unregistered `drive.file` scope (re-consent showed no unverified-app warning); a Google password change (greg confirms none).
>
> **Root cause remains UNKNOWN.** Leading candidate: Google's ~100-refresh-tokens-per-user-per-client cap silently evicting oldest-first (the app mints a new token on every reconnect via `prompt=consent` and never revokes the one it displaces — do NOT "fix" that by weakening consent or adding revoke calls; see the plan's Caveats).
>
> **Why it hid for a week.** `scheduleColdStartReconnectEscalation` suppressed its Slack alert on `hadRefreshToken === false`, commented "there is no bug to investigate". But the permanent branch _clears_ the token, so every refresh after the first also reports `false` — the by-design case and a live revocation were indistinguishable. Only `offline-queue-flush` ever paged, biasing the sample. That is how the 2026-07-08 `/error-review` reached its confidently-wrong "testing-mode 7-day expiry" conclusion (now corrected in this file and in its plan).
>
> **Shipped (3 commits, `28cac2fb` → `c35f5206` → `b417343b`; full suite 3700 green, type-check + lint clean; NOT pushed, NOT deployed):**
>
> 1. **Telemetry un-blinded** — `SilentRefreshReason` (`no-token-stored` | `revoked` | `exhausted`) backed by a session-scoped latch that survives the token being cleared, surfaced as `error_code: silent-refresh:*` on the already-allowlisted key (no `ALLOWED_CONTEXT_KEYS` / Lambda-mirror / app-store-declaration change). Suppression now keys on the genuinely by-design case only. **`refresh_token_age_ms` finally reaches Slack on the revocation path.**
> 2. **Calendar refresh storm fixed** — `createGoogleTokenProvider` cached only successes, so one dead grant produced _hundreds_ of `POST /oauth/google/refresh` 400s per page load (every queued `eventExists`/`insertEvent`/`deleteEvent` re-asked independently). Added per-connection in-flight dedupe + a permanent-failure latch, consolidated the duplicated `isPermanentRefreshFailure` predicate into `services/google/refreshFailure.ts`, and wired `invalidateConnection` into `calendarSyncStore.reconnect()` — **without that call the latch would brick calendar sync until a page reload.** `runPooled` gained an opt-in `shouldAbort`.
> 3. **Boot-adjacent flushes gated on auth readiness** — `tryFlush('visible'|'startup')` now awaits `whenRedirectAuthSettled()`; `online`/`token-acquired` deliberately are not.
>
> **⭐ NEXT ACTION — this is a measurement, not a code task.** Push + deploy, then wait for the next revocation and read **`refresh_token_age_ms`** from `#beanies-errors`. It discriminates: a consistent **~7 days** ⇒ an expiry clock; **scattered ages** ⇒ cap eviction; **all tokens dying on one date** ⇒ a Google-side security event. greg re-consented 2026-07-09 after re-adding the `drive.file` + `userinfo.email` scopes that had vanished from the consent screen, so that token's lifetime is already a live experiment. Record the value here before proposing any further fix.
>
> **Also open (deliberately not done):** (a) `errorReporter.ts:259` injects `severity` into the telemetry context to keep the firehose "filterable", but `severity` is not allowlisted — it has been silently stripped from **every** report ever sent; fixing it means widening the allowlist (3-place coupled change incl. app-store privacy declarations) — greg's call. (b) **Drive and Calendar share one OAuth client**, so a consent-screen scope edit made for Calendar can take Drive persistence down for every user (this session produced direct evidence: `drive.file` had disappeared from the consent screen). Splitting them is a real design decision with migration cost — raise once the root cause is known.
>
> Plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-09-drive-refresh-token-telemetry-and-calendar-storm.md`. Lesson: `docs/lessons.md` → "Get the cheapest discriminating observation before proposing a mechanism".

(1) ⭐ **#65 built end-to-end** (`46f1c79a`): the #61 open-guard's durable baseline row now also carries a fingerprint of the heads **Drive holds** at that revision, so an open can tell the local doc has moved past the file (the force-kill-before-flush case) and decline to skip — falling through to the existing read+merge+re-push. An open with nothing pending still skips (`reads=0 writes=0`), so the #61 win is intact. The load-bearing rule: the fingerprint is ALWAYS derived from Drive's own bytes — `mergeRemoteEnvelope` returns `remoteHeads` from the **unmigrated** decrypted remote, the write terminus uses the heads of the serialized payload, and anything unprovable records `null` and degrades to a read. `commitRemoteBaseline(driveHeads)` takes it as a **required** parameter so a future terminus cannot over-claim by omission. The row payload stays **opaque to the worker** — `remoteBaseline.ts` owns the codec as pure functions, so the whole legacy/corrupt-row ladder is table-tested with no fake IDB. Legacy pre-#65 rows decode to an unknown fingerprint, decline once, then get rewritten — no migration. (2) **The 4-pass plan discipline earned its keep**: passes 2, 3 and 4 EACH caught an over-claim bug of the same class as #65 itself (snapshotting `currentDoc` heads; using `dirty === false` as proof, which the adopt branch hardcodes; and carrying heads from `initAndLoadCache`, which `reloadAllStores`' `cancelPendingSave` turns into a silent false-skip). (3) **`/code-review max` found 15 findings; 11 fixed** — the worst was the write terminus lacking `?? null`, where a worker double without `heads` threw **after** a successful upload and reported a landed save as failed (advancing the save-failure escalation ladder). Also: the re-probe branch pairing a post-write (possibly peer) revision with our heads; the guard probe needing `probe: true` not just `quiet` (else a wedged-but-live worker is torn down and sibling RPCs drained, incl. a user `mutate`); the worker-respawn rehydrator discarding the baseline row and defeating the worker's deliberate clear on a recovered load; the adopt branch hardcoding `dirty: false` while `migrateDoc` can move the doc (stranding the migration delta unsynced forever); `disconnect()` leaving a stale baseline; and the legacy-row decode being a `JSON.parse` sniff rather than a `ver:` recognizer. > **Previous update:** 2026-08-15 (**⭐ RECURRING-OCCURRENCE DATA LOSS — root-caused, fixed, and shipped as `0.9.10R7` to web + Astro + Play open testing + TestFlight.** greg reported that editing a recurring activity occurrence (changing only the pickup person, never the date) moved the session to another date or made it vanish. Investigation found **not one bug but three independent roots producing eight failure modes**, two proven data loss and one financial. **(1) ROOT A — a create payload reused as an update payload.** `ActivityModal.onEdit` seeded the form's `date` from `activity.date` (the SERIES START) while the banner above it showed `props.occurrenceDate` (the clicked day) — the modal displayed two different dates and the user only ever saw one — and `buildPayload()` emitted `date` unconditionally, so an untouched date was written on every save. Proven by execution: clicking the 2026-04-01 occurrence of a series starting 2026-03-04 put the override on **03-04** with `originalOccurrenceDate: 04-01`, so the clicked slot was suppressed (vanished) and the copy landed on the series start overlapping the first instance. **(2) ROOT B — `materializeOverride`/`splitActivity` trusted their callers.** `...overrides` was spread AFTER the parent strip, so the form's `recurrenceEndDate` leaked onto the one-off child — and `expandRecurring` applies the end-date cut BEFORE the `switch (recurrence)`, pruning `recurrence:'none'` children. Proven: a series ending 03-31 with its 03-11 session moved to 04-07 rendered **0 occurrences on both dates** — total loss. The same spread cloned `linkedRecurringItemId`; since a child is `recurrence:'none'`, `isOneTimePayment` was true, so the fee sync **rewrote the family's monthly payment into a one-off** — editing OR cancelling one session of a paid class stopped the recurring fee. **(3) ROOT C — `confirmReschedule` never preserved `originalOccurrenceDate` on a child**, so a moved session's occurrence key drifted, un-suppressing the master's slot (duplicate), colliding on Google instances, and stranding restores. **Masked by Root A** — fixing A alone would have shipped a duplicating-session bug, so A and C had to land together. **(4) SAME CLASS IN RECURRING TRANSACTIONS:** `this-and-future` overwrote `splitRecurringItem`'s correct `startDate` with the template-seeded form value (and carried `lastProcessedDate`, suppressing materialisation); and **"delete this and all future" wrote `recurrenceEndDate`, a field that does not exist on `RecurringItem`** (an `as any` hid it), so `recurringProcessor` — which only reads `endDate` — never end-dated the series and regenerated every deleted instalment. A user cancelling a bill watched it come back. **(5) FIXES:** a shared `diffPayload` so forms emit only what changed; the store made safe REGARDLESS of caller (`OVERRIDE_INVALID_KEYS` re-forced after the caller's overrides, fee ownership TRANSFERRED on split rather than stripped, completions filtered + re-dated rather than dropped, idempotency per `(parent, occurrence)`); delete/split/truncate cascades for override children; `not_found` recovery in `applyExceptionUpsert`; and a multi-weekday date-move refusal (that move is genuinely inexpressible, so it explains instead of corrupting). Legacy corruption self-heals with no migration — a leaked `recurrenceEndDate` is ignored on read, a leaked `linkedRecurringItemId` is cleared on contact. **(6) ⚠️ PROCESS — THE FIRST PASS INTRODUCED EIGHT REGRESSIONS, TWO FINANCIAL.** `/code-review max` caught them all before anything shipped; the worst was adding `linkedRecurringItemId` to the strip list, which removed the id but kept `payFromAccountId`/`feeAmount`, so a split **minted a SECOND fee item while the original kept running — billed twice, forever** (verified by execution). A second review round found 3 more, including a test I wrote that could not fail against a `lessons.md` rule I wrote in the same change. Both rounds fixed. Three new rules in `docs/lessons.md`: check what a field GATES before stripping it; a blanket strip is the same anti-pattern as a blanket write; mocking the collaborator hides the regression that collaborator would have caught. **(7) COVERAGE:** 5 new test files for surfaces that had NONE (`useActivityScopeEdit`, `ActivityModal`, `diffPayload`, `recurringItemFields`, the regression suite) — **21 of 22 regression tests fail on pre-fix `main`**. The E2E specs were structurally incapable of catching this (series started tomorrow + `.first()`, so template start == clicked occurrence); both now click the SECOND occurrence via an indexed `openEditModal`, with `recurringSeriesStartStr()` guaranteeing two occurrences render in-month. **(8) TELEMETRY:** 8 new `recur_*` context keys, allowlisted in `diagnosticContext.ts` + the Lambda mirror + its pinned drift test, and declared in all three store-privacy surfaces. **greg repaired the few affected activities in his own prod pod by hand — the production-data question is CLOSED.** Plan: `docs/plans/2026-08-15-recurring-occurrence-edit-data-loss.md`. **(9) SECOND DEPLOY THE SAME DAY → `0.9.10R8` (web + Play open testing + TestFlight; Astro skipped, `WEB: no`). No release note — greg's call; recorded in `CHANGELOG.md` only.** greg reported from a phone screenshot that the clash badge was eating the event title on the mobile week view ("Softball batting cage" → "Softball ba…"). Cause was structural, not cosmetic: `ClashIndicator`'s `chip` variant rendered the clashing calendar's NAME in a tinted pill, the pill wrapper is `flex-shrink-0` and the title is not, so the title absorbed all the compression. It was also stacking THREE emphasis devices (tint + semibold + orange mark) beside a dark-slate title, so the accent was inverting the hierarchy it should support. Fixed by retiring the `chip` variant entirely — the grid signals with the mark, the drawer explains with the name (it already shows it in full alongside "This is OK" / "Reschedule…"). Deliberately NOT a shrinkable label: a name compressed to "greg…" costs nearly the same title space and communicates nothing. Acknowledged clashes went 70% → 40% opacity, because once both states share a shape opacity carries the whole distinction. Four call sites simplified (`WeeklyCalendarView`, `DayTimeline`, `ActivityListCard`, `MonthChip`); `variant` prop removed rather than left as a dead branch. Mockup approved before implementation: `docs/mockups/clash-indicator-restraint-2026-08-15.html`. **⚠️ SELF-CAUGHT TEST TRAP:** the first version of `ClashIndicator.test.ts` passed 6/7 against the PRE-fix component, because it asserted against the default variant (already mark-only) while the bug only ever appeared when a call site passed `variant="chip"` — the exact "write the test so the right and wrong answers are different values" trap added to `docs/lessons.md` (rule 4) earlier the same day. Rewritten to pass `variant: 'chip'` explicitly; now 3/7 fail on the old component. Caught by running the stash-check rather than trusting green.)

(2) **False "we couldn't save your pod" on iPhone Drive setup → auto-heal.** The first Drive write right after the full-page OAuth redirect can throw a 401/TokenExpired on a freshly-returned token (WebKit bounce-tracking clears the refresh cookie across the cross-origin redirect) even though the `.beanpod` stub already exists; the critical error dumped the user to the storage picker and a manual re-tap adopted the stub. `ResumePodSetup.finalizePod` now silently re-acquires a token and retries the write ONCE (reason==='write' only — 'verify' sets `partialFileId` and would rename the stub to `.corrupt-<ts>`). **A `/code-review` caught a pre-existing CRITICAL data-loss on this path:** a failed create-write leaves its envelope (encrypted under a now-discarded family key) in the offline queue → a non-auth-gated `token-acquired`/`online`/`startup` flush could later overwrite the good pod and brick decryption — fixed at root: `createNewFile` now `clearQueue()` on any create failure. (3) **⭐ Stuck-zoom on iPhone (setup + onboarding + every form) — root-caused (after TWO wrong guesses) to iOS auto-zoom-on-focus of sub-16px controls.** Native form controls are `font-size:100%` (inherit), and the wizard/onboarding sit under `text-sm` ancestors, so `BaseInput`/`BaseSelect`/`BaseCombobox` fields rendered 14px → iOS zooms on focus and won't zoom back (only a force-quit recovers). The first two attempts (AppDelegate zoom-reset on OAuth return; then onboarding-only field bumps) were BOTH wrong — native OAuth opens in a SEPARATE SFSafariViewController so the app webview is never zoomed, and the trigger is in-app field focus. Fixed app-wide via a full sweep: `BaseInput`/`BaseSelect`/`BaseTextarea` pinned to `text-base` + `BaseCombobox`'s two inputs; a **global `@layer base` floor** `input:not(...),select,textarea { font-size: max(1rem, 1em) }` (only ever RAISES — never caps larger controls, catches inherit-only + future); the ~20 remaining raw controls carrying an explicit `text-sm`/`text-xs` bumped to `text-base`; plus the onboarding `.ob-*` classes + an `AmountInput` `max(1rem, …)` clamp. rem-based so Large reading mode still scales; NO `user-scalable=no`/`maximum-scale` (preserves pinch-zoom + WCAG 1.4.4). AppDelegate reverted to stock. (4) **End-of-wizard "couldn't save the beanpod" → retry.** `SetupProgressModal` step 3 called `syncNow` twice with no token reconnect between tries, so a transient token expiry failed both and "Continue" only SKIPPED the save; now it silently reconnects + retries once. Extracted `reconnectForWriteRetry` into `driveTokenRecovery` (shared by `finalizePod` + `SetupProgressModal`, DRY). **greg confirmed on-device on R6 that the zoom is fixed.** Filed tracker issues **#63** (deep links open the installed app first — App Links/Universal Links, then PWA, then browser) and **#64** (add beanies as a mobile share-target feeding shared images/PDFs into magic beans). **NEXT: greg to record the App-Review demo video on R6 + reply to Apple's Guideline 2.1 "Information Needed" in Resolution Center** (Notes + demo account `beaniesdemo@gmail.com` + screen-recording shot list already drafted this session; ASC record version → 0.9.10R6). Android beta (open testing) auto-submitted for review each deploy.)

Regression window 2026-07-13 → 2026-08-10. (3) **⚠️ Production served a crippled build for ~40 minutes** — root cause was NOT a stray local sync (my first attribution, wrong) but `translation-sync.yml`'s own `Deploy to PROD` job, which built with a reduced env subset and `aws s3 sync --delete`'d over the app bucket, killing the Slack error webhook, pod-create ping, feedback delivery, analytics and AI-extract, and undoing the preceding proper deploy. > - **E2E suite fixed — green on chromium + webkit** (red since `b1a842fe`, 2026-06-26). Verified chromium 21/21 locally on a **fresh** server; both browsers green on CI (run 28347418021). **Trap logged** (`docs/lessons.md` #15): a stale warm dev server reused via `reuseExistingServer` served OLD code and gave a false-green locally, sending the first diagnosis down a wrong "contention" path — always repro against a fresh server.

> ## ✅ DONE EARLIER 2026-06-29 (AM)
>
> - **Deep-link cold-start fix — DEPLOYED** (`754de773` fix + `d9457157` release note; deploy run green, release `2026.06.28`, minor/bell-badge per greg). Root cause: deep-link handlers (e.g. Google Calendar → `/activities?activity=<id>`) read the query param on mount **before** the store hydrated, missed the lookup, but cleared the param anyway — so the item never opened on a cold start. Fix: new `src/composables/useDeepLinkParam.ts` — only clears the param **after a successful open**, and **retries when the backing store hydrates**. Revisit only if the watchdog misbehaves.
  >
  > ### What was root-caused (the ITP hypothesis below was WRONG)
  >
  > Three independent telemetry captures (a `#beanies-errors` Slack alert + two CloudWatch runs after the telemetry Lambda was updated) proved: at the exact instant of failure the device reports **`web_storage: ls=true,ss=true`** — storage WORKS; only the values written BEFORE the redirect vanish. greg confirmed it reproduces in a **plain Safari tab** with **"Prevent Cross-Site Tracking" OFF**. Root cause: **WebKit bounce-tracking protection clears the initiating site's script-writable storage across the cross-site OAuth bounce** (`app → accounts.google.com → app`), independently of the ITP toggle. So `sessionStorage['beanies_redirect_auth']` (codeVerifier + returnPath) and the round-2 create-resume password — all written pre-bounce — were gone on return, cascading into: recovery screen → second password → what's-new pop → silent "counting beans" hang → misleading "Private Browsing" toast.
  >
  > ### What the fix does (committed in `04f18785`; plan `docs/plans/2026-06-20-ios-oauth-bounce-state-param.md`; ADR-026 amendment)
  >
  > Enabled by two facts: the OAuth proxy is a **confidential client** (holds `client_secret`, so PKCE is defense-in-depth, not load-bearing) and ADR-026 already deems the web redirect CSRF-safe (same-origin top-level nav).
  >
  > - **Carry routing through the OAuth `state` param** (new `src/services/google/redirectState.ts` — `encode/decodeRedirectState`, validates same-origin `returnPath` + exact-match version). Survives the bounce because it rides in the URL, not storage.
  > - **Drop the web PKCE verifier**; the Lambda's `code_verifier` is now optional (`infrastructure/lambda/oauth/index.mjs` + SPEC + tests — ALWAYS still attaches `client_secret`).
  > - **Thread a REQUIRED `mode` (`create`/`join`/`reconnect`) through all FIVE `startRedirectAuth` call sites** (`connectStorage`, `syncStore`, `useGoogleReconnect`, `usePickBeanpodFile`, `SettingsPage` → `LoadPodView`) — compiler-enforced coverage.
  > - **Remove the round-2 password stash; single clean password re-entry** via the existing `identity` phase (`resumePaths.ts`/`CreatePodView.vue`/`ResumePodSetup.vue`).
  > - **`OAuthCallbackPage.vue`** reads `state` from the URL (new → legacy → lost ladder); accurate copy (no "Private Browsing").
  > - **Init watchdog** (`App.vue` `INIT_TIMEOUTS`, 35s → existing recovery overlay + `app.onboardingStallTimeout`); **no what's-new auto-open mid-onboarding** (`useNotifications.ts`).
  > - **Native path UNCHANGED.** One-release legacy `beanies_redirect_auth` fallback guarded by a **dated CI tripwire** (`legacyRedirectTransport.tripwire.test.ts`, fails after **2026-09-30** to force cleanup).
  >

The telemetry Lambda was also deployed (Terraform) so `web_storage`/`breadcrumbs` survive ingest. Plan `docs/plans/2026-06-20-iphone-onboarding-observability.md`. This is what let us capture the `ls=true,ss=true` evidence that disproved ITP.

Workflow: live-schema read → classify Bug/Feature → **subagent-backed proportional research** (codebase/commits/docs + web) to fill every field → **always-on duplicate check** → confirm the 4 control fields (Priority, generate mockup?, github issue, Feature gated?) → **full preview with provenance** for explicit approval → create a `Not started` row (Raised By greg) → report new `#ID` + **offer** `/beanies-pre-plan` (never auto-chains). Never hardcodes select options (reads them live). **Validated via 3 dry-run evals** (calendar feature / sync-toast bug / data-export feature), with-skill vs no-skill baseline, all 6 runs writing NOTHING to Notion: **100% pass-rate with the skill vs 67% baseline (+0.33)**. > **(1) #36 — Session-epoch guard for Google token acquisition (`177163bb`; plan `a1d34eee`; NOT deployed; `npm run validate` green, 3240 tests).** Closes a pre-existing concurrency race in `googleAuth.ts`: a token acquisition in flight when the user signs out could resolve AFTER teardown cleared session state, writing a "zombie" credential into the just-cleared (or next) session and mirroring it into the beanpod. A module-level `sessionEpoch` is bumped at each semantic teardown (`clearGoogleSessionState`, `revokeToken`), which also now clear the redirect-intent sessionStorage keys so an abandoned redirect can't bridge a reload. Each of the **four acquisition seams** (silent auth-code, popup, silent refresh, redirect completion) snapshots the epoch at entry and discards via `isSessionStillCurrent` (best-effort access-token revoke + `info`-level `auth-epoch-discard` log) when the epoch advanced. `notifyTokenAcquired` gained an `expectedEpoch` arg as a **single-chokepoint backstop**: a stale epoch logs `error`-level `auth-epoch-leak` and returns before any side effect, so a future un-guarded seam is observable/test-asserted. `driveTokenRecovery.restoreLocalFromDoc` is guarded at the one store+prime boundary (neither the local IDB write nor the in-memory prime runs on a stale epoch). Followed the 4-pass `/beanies-plan` (`docs/plans/2026-06-14-session-epoch-guard-google-token.md`). Ships ungated, no GitHub issue. **Notion #36 → Done.**
>

> **⭐ READ FIRST NEXT SESSION — the #34 pivot (this is where we pick up).** Live test by greg: created a beanies activity at a time his connected Google calendar was already busy. The event synced fine (visible side-by-side in Google) but **no clash indicator appeared in beanies.** Investigation found two issues, the second of which is the important one:
>
> - **(a) Surface gap (easy).** `ClashIndicator` is only mounted on `ActivityListCard`, and that component is used in exactly ONE place — `DayAgendaSidebar.vue`. The month grid (`MonthChip`), week view (`WeeklyCalendarView`) and day view (`DailyCalendarView`/`DayTimeline`) render their own event markup and have NO indicator. So nothing shows on the calendar grid where greg was looking. The plan listed those surfaces; only the list card got wired.
> - **(b) Self-clash design flaw (the real one).** beanies pushes the activity to the SAME calendar we then free/busy-query, as an opaque (busy) event — so an activity's own synced event registers as "busy" at its exact time → every synced activity would self-clash. Worse, Google's free/busy MERGES overlapping busy blocks, so once a beanies event and a real event touch they're one indistinguishable interval — can't be separated after the fact, and subtraction creates false negatives.
> - **AGREED PIVOT (greg's proposal, validated):** the "we can't read events" invariant was never real — `calendar.events.owned` (held for the #32 push) already grants READ ("see, create, change, delete events on owned calendars"). So `calendar.freebusy` never reduced our capability; it was a narrower-claim scope. **New design:** use `events.list` with a **partial-response `fields=items(id,recurringEventId,start,end,status,transparency)`** so PII (summary/description/location/attendees) never crosses the wire; identify beanies' OWN events by `deterministicEventId(activity.id)` (we already mint these — match `id`/`recurringEventId`, no marker, **no #32 push change, no migration**); a clash = a non-beanies, non-transparent, non-cancelled event overlapping the activity. This solves self-clash AND merging, **keeps events opaque** (no "mark genuinely-busy events as free" hack — greg rejected that), and lets us **DROP `calendar.freebusy` entirely** (one fewer sensitive scope; simpler consent + Google verification). Privacy claim shifts from "API physically can't return content" to "we only request times; content never reaches us" — honest + auditable via the `fields` param, and the strong claim was already untrue given events.owned.
>

Keyword table got a shallow, collision-free fill for the motivating School gaps (`field_trip` incl. New `CATEGORY_OPTIONS_TEXT` constant is hardcoded identically in all three copies (the `.mjs` copies can't import the TS taxonomy); a new client-only sync test (`extractionPromptCategory.test.ts`) derives the expected literal from `getActivityCategoriesGrouped()` and fails CI if the taxonomy and the prompt list ever diverge.
