> **The load-bearing architecture (the 4-pass review earned its keep):** travel segments are **nested array items** inside `doc.vacations[*].{travelSegments,accommodations,transportation}[]`, not a flat top-level collection — so the photo pipeline's `attachPhotoToEntity` + GC `collectReferencedPhotoIds` (which assume `doc[collection][entityId].photoIds`) would have silently no-op'd the attach AND GC-deleted every segment attachment as an orphan. Fix: **`photoStore` registry `Set<string>` → `Map<name, {attach, collect}>` hooks** (default flat hooks preserve every existing collection; the old hardcoded `avatarPhotoId` GC branch is **retired** into explicit avatar hooks). **A throwing `collect` hook now fail-safe-aborts the GC sweep** (never widens the delete set — the single highest-consequence path). New `src/services/photos/photoCollectionHooks.ts` (vacation nested attach/collect via a `vacationId/segmentId` composite key + `console.warn` on id-drift; avatar hooks). `App.vue` registers `vacations` + the avatar-shaped `familyMembers` hooks (Pass 4 caught that a wrong familyMembers registration would wipe every avatar — GC has no grace for orphans).
>
> **PDF + UI.** `addPhoto` PDF passthrough (skip compression, raw blob, `application/pdf`, `0×0`, original `fileName` carried through the offline queue too). `attachmentKind()` is the single source of truth for image-vs-PDF (no scattered mime checks). New `DocumentTile.vue` boarding-pass stub; `PhotoViewer` PDF branch uses `getBlobUrl` (the lh3 image CDN can't serve PDF bytes — Pass 4 blocker) + inline `<iframe>` + "Open in new tab"; `PhotoIndicator` gained an `icon` prop (📎); `PhotoAttachments` `allowDocuments` opt-in (default false — activities/recipes/etc. unaffected). `usePhotos` `accept: 'imagesAndPdf'` with a 10 MB cap + `%PDF` magic-byte check + distinct oversize toast. New `vacationStore.updateSegmentPhotoIds` owns the segment merge. Wired into the 3 edit drawers, the 3 wizard steps, and the timeline (📎 count chip + thumbnail strip → read-only lightbox). i18n en+beanie+zh; `travel-plans-and-vacations` Help article updated.

> **(1) Native + PWA Google Drive sign-in via redirect transport — SHIPPED & VALIDATED.** The pod-load path used a popup OAuth transport that can't complete in the native WebView / installed PWA (blank tab → 120s timeout). Unified the load flow on the existing system-browser/redirect transport (`beginDriveAuthRedirectIfNeeded` + `?resume=load-drive`), so after consent the app re-opens the Drive file list and decrypts automatically. A follow-on CORS failure on the OAuth proxy was traced to the WebView document origin: `capacitor.config.ts` now serves the bundle under `https://app.beanies.family` (`server.hostname`), which is already CORS-allowlisted; `https://localhost` + a `native_redirect_uris` var were also added to the proxy (terraform-applied, greg-authorized). greg confirmed native sign-in works end-to-end.
>
> **(2) Native biometric (passkey) — investigated to a definitive conclusion; DEFERRED to the Play-signed build.** Two transports were tried and the root cause is now pinned:
>
> - **WebView-WebAuthn — dead end (abandoned).** `WebSettingsCompat.setWebAuthenticationSupport`: `FOR_APP` → opaque `CreateCredentialUnknownException`; `FOR_BROWSER` → hard native Chromium WebView crash (`JniAndroid$UncaughtExceptionException`) the instant `navigator.credentials.create()` ran. (`a30fa0c` on `main` shipped this approach; it is now superseded.)
> - **`@capgo/capacitor-passkey` plugin shim — the right path; reaches Google's native FIDO flow.** `autoShimWebAuthn()` (native-only, installed in `main.ts`) routes the app's existing `navigator.credentials` calls to the Android Credential Manager. The plugin successfully reaches Google's own FIDO `RegistrationActivity` with the crypto/PRF stack unchanged — proving the WebView↔Credential-Manager bridge was the blocker, not the device, account, RP, or assetlinks.
> - **Final wall: GMS `[50152] "RP ID cannot be validated"` on the sideloaded DEBUG build.** Despite: signing cert **confirmed `19:E4:…`** (`adb shell pm get-app-links family.beanies.app` → `Signatures: [19:E4…]` + `beanies.family: verified`), and the `app.beanies.family` assetlinks (`get_login_creds` + `19:E4`) **validated by Google's own checker** (`linked:true`). This is the known, murky on-device Digital-Asset-Links failure that affects **sideloaded debug builds** specifically.
> - **Decision (greg):** defer native biometric to the **Play-signed internal-testing build**, where (a) the real **Play App Signing** cert goes in the assetlinks, (b) GMS DAL validation for passkey creation is materially more reliable for Play-distributed apps, and (c) it has to be validated anyway for store launch. Nothing is blocked: native works today with **password sign-in**, and **PWA/browser biometric is unchanged**. iOS biometric is also deferred — the plugin currently returns empty `clientExtensionResults` (no PRF) and no iOS build exists yet.
> - **Foundation kept in `main`** (ready to validate on the Play build, no rework): plugin shim + `capacitor.config.ts` origin/RP config, `getRpId()` seam in `passkeyService.ts` (native → `app.beanies.family`, web → origin host, unchanged), `public/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (`get_login_creds`, live), CI unique `versionCode` + build-SHA stamping, bare `MainActivity` (WebView WebAuthn removed), and `residentKey:'preferred'` on native.
>
> **Watch / next (Play milestone):** on the first **Mobile — Android release (Play)** internal-testing build — add the Play App Signing SHA-256 to `public/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (keep the debug `19:E4` too), then re-test native biometric registration → unlock. If it works, tune native registration to a **single** create attempt (the current 3-attempt progressive fallback re-prompts the chooser, which is fine for web/OEM quirks but poor native UX). If `50152` persists even Play-signed, gate the native biometric offer behind a flag until resolved.

> **(B) Google Drive refresh-token persistence fix — all platforms (ADR-028).** Plan: `docs/plans/2026-05-20-google-refresh-token-persistence-fix.md` (`/beanies-plan` 4-pass). Diagnosed via the now-live firehose: greg's Android-PWA `offline-queue-flush` events showed `silent_refresh_had_refresh_token:false` every restart. Two compounding bugs: (1) the refresh token was orphaned under `__pending__` — the redirect reconnect's `completeRedirectAuth` (App.vue Step 2b) stores there before the family is bound, and nothing migrated it on a plain reconnect/cold-boot; (2) reconnect used `prompt=select_account`, so Google never re-issued a refresh token. Fix: `startRedirectAuth` ALWAYS `prompt=consent` (single place — every redirect caller is an offline-access flow; no per-call-site flag); popup reconnect site forces consent; `migratePendingRefreshToken` gained an empty-family guard (never clobber) and `initializeAuth` calls it on every bind — so an orphaned token self-heals onto the family key on the next cold boot (incl. already-affected devices); removed the now-redundant explicit `syncStore` migrate calls (single source of truth); added `auth-no-refresh-token` report + `auth-init` firehose events. Only `googleAuth.ts` has substantive logic changes (+ 1-line `useGoogleReconnect` popup edit + `syncStore` removals). Desktop unaffected (popup binds family before storing). 71 googleAuth tests + 5 useGoogleReconnect tests green.

> **(B) LoginPage TDZ + redundant zombie-state alert suppression** (`91ca366`, Vue prod `502ebab`). Two issues from production onboarding error alerts on 2026-05-18 morning. (1) Boeder-family Android Chrome user hit a `vue-render` ReferenceError on LoginPage: classic temporal-dead-zone self-reference. `const stopResumeWatch = watchEffect(() => { ...; stopResumeWatch(); })` — when all conditions are immediately true at mount (post-router-guard redirect to `/welcome?resume=setup`), the first synchronous watchEffect run hits `stopResumeWatch()` before the const assignment completes. Vue's error boundary caught it so the user could still complete pod creation, but the render aborted mid-effect and the error fired to Slack. Fixed by `let stopResumeWatch: WatchStopHandle = () => {}` then assigning — first synchronous run safely calls the no-op, then the assignment completes for any later reactive re-run. Regression test in `src/pages/__tests__/LoginPage.tdz.test.ts` mounts LoginPage with all conditions immediately true and asserts no throw + lands on resume-setup view. (2) `app.onboardingZombieState` alerts were firing redundantly on PWA cold reload while the user was already at `/welcome?resume=setup` (recovery flow working as designed). Moved the `reportError` inside the `if (!onResumeScreen)` branch so the alert only fires when redirection is actually needed — router-guard alert stays unchanged for "navigating TO a protected route in zombie state" (the genuine signal).

> **(C) Photo upload reliability — queue-fallback + binding sync + lightbox footer** (4 commits: `40b50ff`, `caed355`, `56866e9`, `502ebab`, Vue prod `502ebab`). Triggered by greg's `couldn't upload photo. please try again.` alert on his Android Chrome on 2g, plus standing UX feedback about photos appearing to vanish when the drawer is closed mid-upload. Three layered fixes. (1) **Queue-fallback on transient online failures** (`40b50ff`): `photoStore.addPhoto` wraps `finalizeUpload` in try/catch with a new `isTransientUploadError(e)` classifier (NetworkError / TypeError(Failed to fetch) / AbortError / Drive 5xx / 429); on transient throw, falls back to `enqueueUpload` (the existing offline queue infra — same flushHandler) so the photo isn't lost on flaky-but-online networks. New `QueueWriteFailedError` class for the rare case where the queue itself can't persist (IndexedDB quota / private mode). Return type changed to discriminated `{ photoId, status: 'completed' | 'queued' }`. Avatar path is parallel infra and would need queue payload extension — flagged as out of scope follow-up. (2) **Photos appear on drawer reopen** (`caed355` + `56866e9`): the real bug greg's repro hit. `BaseSidePanel` uses `v-if="open"` so closing the drawer unmounts `PhotoAttachments` mid-upload; the async `store.addPhoto` continues and writes the photoId directly into `entity.photoIds` via `attachPhotoToEntity` (good); but `usePhotos.add`'s follow-up `options.updatePhotoIds(merged)` emit hits the unmounted component as a no-op, so `usePhotoEntityBinding`'s local `photoIds` ref stays stale. Worse: the parent (`FamilyPlannerPage`) captures `editingActivity.value = target` at click-time so `props.activity` is a plain object snapshot that doesn't reactively update when the doc changes. Worse still: entity stores (activityStore et al.) hold static `ref<Entity[]>` arrays that only refresh on explicit `load*()` calls — they don't subscribe to `docVersion`. Three layers of staleness, single fix: new `photoStore.photoIdsFor(collection, entityId)` reactive helper that reads photoIds straight from the live Automerge doc and subscribes to `docVersion`. Wired into all five photo-bearing modals (ActivityModal, ActivityViewEditModal, MilestoneFormModal, MedicationFormModal, RecipeFormModal). Realigned to BeanieFormModal's convention: 🗑️ icon-only red-tinted square left + 📥 icon-only slate-tinted square next + gradient-orange "Close" primary right (`flex-1`). > **(E) Reload-loop fix — break the path1b-load-failed cycle + reporter hardening** (`527f9ce`, Vue prod `527f9ce`). Ritterbusch family hit a tight init → fail-load → safeRouterReplace('/welcome') → guard cancels (type=16) → window.location.replace fallback → reload → repeat cycle, generating 40+ error alerts in 30 seconds. Root cause: `ALREADY_AUTH_REDIRECT_FROM` guard in `src/router/index.ts:309-319` redirects /welcome → /nook for signed-in users with `podCreated: true`. App.vue path 1b ("loadFromFile failed for non-password reasons") tried to send them to /welcome, guard bounced them back, window.location.replace forced a full reload, and the cycle repeated. Three fixes: (1) App.vue path 1b no longer redirects — falls through to the post-init health check which sets `initError` and surfaces the existing recovery overlay (user can Reload or Clear Data). No redirect = no guard fight = no loop. (2) Defence-in-depth: `safeRouterReplace` now counts attempts per target in sessionStorage and aborts after `SAFE_REPLACE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` consecutive cancellation-and-fallback cycles, surfacing the recovery overlay instead. Reports `app.loadFamilyData.replaceLoopDetected`. Counter resets on successful navigation. (3) errorReporter now persists its 60s dedup window across reloads via sessionStorage (`__er_bucket_*` keys) — the existing in-memory bucket map dies on every page reload, so reload-loop floods evaded layer-1 dedup entirely. Layer-2 sessionStorage keyed by (surface, normalized-message) — identical errors fired across reloads in the same tab coalesce to a single Slack alert per 60s. The Ritterbusch flood would have been ~2 alerts instead of 40+.

> **Earlier 2026-05-14 (session 1, mid-morning. Calendar swipe animation shipped** — a UX polish on the existing horizontal-swipe gesture on the Planner's day/week/month surfaces. Previously: swipe past threshold → `nextDay()`/`nextWeek()`/`nextMonth()` fired and Vue flashed in the new content with zero motion. Now: an iOS-Calendar-style two-phase slide. New composable `src/composables/useCalendarSlide.ts` layered on top of the existing `useHorizontalSwipe` (which keeps owning gesture detection — its 13-test contract untouched). Behaviour: (a) live drag — element follows the finger via `translate3d(dx, 0, 0)`, motion past the 60px commit threshold is rubber-banded with coefficient 0.45 so it resists infinite pulling; (b) commit (released past threshold) — Web Animations API runs phase A (current `dx` → `−sign×width`, 220ms, easing `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` — Apple's system page-transition curve), then calls `onNext`/`onPrev` (Vue re-renders), instantly snaps to `+sign×width`, then phase B (off-screen edge → 0, 320ms); content swap happens while the element is off-screen so the user perceives one continuous slide; (c) cancel (released below threshold or pointercancel) — single 220ms ease back to 0; (d) `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` short-circuits the whole thing to instant content swap, no drag preview — matches the pre-animation behaviour exactly; (e) re-entrancy — `enabled` ref flips false during the commit animation so a second swipe can't fire mid-flight (wired through `useHorizontalSwipe`'s existing `enabled` parameter via a `computed`). Two implementation details: (1) `useHorizontalSwipe`'s terminal `onProgress(0)` (fires at end of every gesture, committed or cancelled) is disambiguated by a synchronous `committing` flag set inside `onSwipeLeft`/`onSwipeRight` (which fire before `onProgress(0)` in `onPointerUp`); when true, the composable's `onProgress` handler skips the spring-back. (2) Phase B waits one `requestAnimationFrame` after the synchronous swap so Vue's just-triggered re-render lands before the inbound animation kicks off — otherwise the new content can flash with the old layout for one frame. Wired into all three planner views — `DailyCalendarView.vue` / `WeeklyCalendarView.vue` / `CalendarGrid.vue` — each a 4-line swap (import + call + a `will-change: transform` hint added alongside the existing `touch-action: pan-y` for GPU compositing). 10 new unit tests (`src/composables/__tests__/useCalendarSlide.test.ts`) covering direction, drag preview, rubber-band damping, commit animation sequence, re-entrancy lockout, and the reduced-motion path. **Out of scope (documented in the plan)**: live peek of destination content during drag (the iOS Calendar "carousel of three" pattern — would require lifting `referenceDate` out of each view); animating prev/next button taps (greg's request was specifically about swipe); vertical-axis swipe between views. `npm run validate` clean (0 errors, 2213 unit tests pass, build 15.85s). Plan: `docs/plans/2026-05-14-calendar-swipe-animation.md`. **Not yet deployed — awaiting greg's verification on real hardware** (the slide-out/slide-in pacing is hard to assess from a desktop browser; intentional swipe-on-iPhone preview before shipping to prod). No commits yet either; staged as working-tree changes.)

Triaged GENUINE: both fetches in `src/services/google/oauthProxy.ts` (`exchangeCodeForTokens` for popup/redirect token exchange, `refreshAccessToken` for silent refresh) called `fetch()` with **no network timeout**. On iOS Safari over flaky cellular / Wi-Fi handover, `fetch` can hang for minutes or never resolve — and because `attemptSilentRefresh` deduplicates concurrent callers via `pendingSilentRefresh`, a single hung fetch pinned every subsequent caller to the same dead promise. The 4s cold-start defer still fired the reconnect banner, but clicking Reconnect ran `completeRedirectAuth()` → another untimedout `exchangeCodeForTokens` fetch → app init wedged at `isInitializing=true` so the full-screen spinner never dismissed. The 2026-05-08 silent-refresh hardening (`8152872`) lowered the failure-counter threshold 3 → 2 and made escalation faster — that didn't cause the hang, it just exposed it earlier, matching greg's observation that reconnect prompts had been "happening much more than before." Fix: new `fetchWithTimeout(url, init, timeoutMs = 15_000)` helper using `AbortController`. Both fetches go through it. Timeout error message includes the substring "silent refresh failed" so `isAuthTransientSyncError` (`syncStore.ts:290-292`) routes the failure as auth-transient → reconnect-banner path keeps working AND wake-event recovery hooks fire. Defense-in-depth: `App.vue:512` wraps the `completeRedirectAuth()` call in a 20s `Promise.race` so init can never wedge even if a future code path adds another awaited fetch. Three new unit tests pin the timeout behaviour. Vue prod deploy `25603971921` (~1m 45s: gate 3s + build 1m18s + S3+CloudFront 22s). New noise-list entry `oauth-proxy-fetch-hang` added to `reference_known_noise.md` so future triages cross-reference. **Test status throughout**: 2061 → 2064 unit tests passing (+3 from oauthProxy timeout tests); type-check + lint + build clean across all 10 commits. **Other-terminal commits**: none today. **Pending into next session**: telemetry watch on the OAuth-fetch fix (next `cold-start-reconnect-escalation` alert, if any, will end with "OAuth proxy fetch timed out after 15000ms" — clean signal that proxy/network is bottlenecked, not our code; alerts with the old shape would mean the timeout didn't catch); Mother's Day weekend amplification active TODAY (Day 10 of 14 of aloe vera launch — Quora answer Sun 8-10 PM SGT + 2nd Substack Note); rest of pending block validated and trimmed below.)

Added `400` to the `Caveat:wght@` segment of `index.html`. (b) After URL fix the title still rendered Outfit because of a deeper bug: `src/style.css:421-425` had a global `h1, h2, h3 { font-family: Outfit, sans-serif }` rule **outside** any `@layer`. In CSS cascade-layer ordering, unlayered styles beat layered styles regardless of selector specificity — so the unlayered element rule won over Tailwind v4's `@layer utilities` `.font-caveat { ... }` even though class selectors normally beat element selectors. Wrapped the heading rule in `@layer base { ... }` so utility classes can override per element. (c) Defense-in-depth: added explicit `font-medium` on the title h2, family-name subtitle, page-header subtitle, and bean-polaroid caption — weight 500 was already loaded so works even on PWA-cached old assets. **(3) CSS structural audit (deferred)** — greg asked for a quick pass on whether the same cascade-layer trap lurks elsewhere; identified four findings: (a) THREE more unlayered element-selector groups in `style.css` ready to bite us next time someone applies a utility on those elements — `html, body { ... }` (lines 400-418, body font-family + bg + color literal), `input[type='date'], input[type='time'] { ... }` (479-502, font-family + accent-color + picker indicator styling), `select.beanies-input { ... }` (469); (b) parallel color-token systems — `packages/brand/theme.css` defines `--color-primary-500`/etc as Tailwind v4 scale; `src/style.css` defines `--color-primary` (no scale, legacy) — same hexes, components reference whichever was current when written, divergence risk if anyone updates one without the other; (c) `body` hardcodes `font-family: Inter, system-ui, ...` instead of `var(--font-inter)` (token defined in brand but not used here); (d) `!important` patterns: `NookVacationCard.vue:103,107` + `onboarding-shared.css:423,429,440,449` are fighting scoped styles in shared components (right fix: expose CSS variables on those components), `GoalsPage.vue:873` has unexplained `!important` on a progress gradient, `style.css:360 .dark .nook-card-dark { background: ... !important }` could become a `dark:bg-*` utility. Worked around in `96b7b93` by removing the redundant inline override (the value matched the CSS-default `.scrap-washi { --washi-color: ... }` from `style.css`, so the override was a no-op). Plugin bug itself unfixed; flagged for tomorrow's CSS session. **Test status**: 2040 unit tests passing across both pre-push runs (1985 → 2040 from milestones / scrapbook / family-timeline test additions in `eb03538`); type-check + lint + build clean on `96b7b93`. **Other-terminal commits**: none today. **Evening session (~21:00 SG, commit `b240f6e`)** — greg surfaced TWO production bugs. **(A) Sync silent-refresh escalation gap**: greg added a milestone on his iOS PWA, hard-reloaded desktop several times, didn't see the data — and noted the indeterminate `BackgroundSyncBar` never appeared on reload. Settings → Family Data showed a "data file not connected" card; one tap on his email via the reconnect popup brought everything back. Diagnosed: silent-refresh path was failing for transient reasons (proxy hiccup / refresh-token-not-loaded race / network jitter beyond the ~4.5s 3-attempt retry budget), classified as `auth-transient` in `backgroundSyncFromFile` (the toast is suppressed on that kind because the _design assumption_ was that `setupTokenExpiryHandler` would escalate). But the auth layer ONLY escalates to `permanentFailureCallbacks` (which fires `showGoogleReconnect = true`) on a definitive `invalid_grant` — see `googleAuth.ts:614-636`. Any other persistent failure mode silently exhausted retries and returned `null` with no UI signal. The "tap email once" reconnect succeeded because `useGoogleReconnect.reconnect` falls through silent-refresh → `attemptSilentAuthCode` (silent iframe, `prompt=none`, uses Google session cookies) → `performPopupAuth` (popup with `prompt=select_account`, also session-cookie based) — those paths are independent of the refresh-token+proxy chain that was broken. Fix: new module-level `consecutiveSilentRefreshFailures` counter in `googleAuth.ts` increments on each retry-exhausted `attemptSilentRefresh` call and fires `permanentFailureCallbacks` exactly when the counter crosses `SILENT_REFRESH_FAILURE_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD = 3` (uses `===` not `>=` so subsequent failures past threshold don't re-fire). Resets on any successful token acquisition via `notifyTokenAcquired` (covers silent + popup + redirect + silent auth-code paths via single point) and on `clearTokenState`. With file polling firing every 10s + ~4.5s retry budget per call, the banner now surfaces within ~30-45s of the system being stuck. Existing `onTokenAcquired` self-heal in syncStore (lines 1779-1799) auto-clears the surface when a later refresh succeeds, so a recovered transient blip doesn't leave a stale banner. Also factored the inline `forEach` from the `invalid_grant` branch into a `firePermanentFailureCallbacks()` helper. Three test changes in `googleAuth.test.ts`: renamed existing "fires onTokenPermanentlyExpired ONLY on invalid_grant" → "fires immediately on invalid_grant — but NOT on a single retry-exhausted transient failure" (assertion still holds — one retry-exhausted call is counter=1, below threshold); added "escalates to onTokenPermanentlyExpired after N consecutive retry-exhausted failures" (12 transient throws across 4 calls, fake timers + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(5000)` to skip 4.5s backoffs without triggering the ~55min `scheduleAutoRefresh` setTimeout); added "resets the consecutive-failure counter on a successful refresh" (2 fail → 1 success → 2 fail; counter goes 1, 2, 0, 1, 2 — no callback fires). Also added `vi.useRealTimers()` to afterEach as a fake-timer-leak safety net. Replaced `mockImplementation` with queued `mockImplementationOnce` calls because the former persists across `vi.resetModules` and was polluting `clearGoogleSessionState` / `onTokenAcquired` / `migratePendingRefreshToken` tests downstream. **(B) Scrapbook horizontal overflow**: greg reported the `/pod/scrapbook` PWA panned horizontally on mobile to reveal a strip of background — only this page, no other. Root cause: every entry card in `EveryoneSpread.vue` and `BeanSpread.vue` carries an inline `transform: rotate(±X deg)` for the tilt aesthetic. Rotated elements don't change their flow width but DO extend their visual bounding box past their grid cell; the body's `scrollWidth` includes that visual extent, so the browser allowed horizontal panning to reveal it. Other pages don't tilt content, which is why this was scrapbook-only. Fix: added `overflow-x: clip` (NOT `hidden`) to `.scrapbook-paper` in `src/style.css:574`. `clip` clips visually without creating a horizontal scroll context — preserves the sticky AppHeader and any future sticky descendants. **Test status**: 2042 / 2042 unit tests passing (+2 from auth escalation), type-check clean. **Vue prod deploy `25500883230`**: 1m 42s end-to-end (CI/Security verify 4s · build 1m 15s · S3+CloudFront 23s). **Astro deploy**: skipped (no marketing-site files changed). **Other-terminal commits**: none.)

> **Earlier 2026-05-03 update (Sunday late-night — three-fix follow-up session triggered by greg pasting a Slack `#beanies-errors` alert from his Android Chrome PWA: `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../FamilyNookPage-DZK3iJ0T.js` while opening the app on mobile (desktop unaffected). Three Vue prod deploys spread across the session; final commit `df395df`. **(1) PWA self-heal for stale-chunk crashes after deploy** (commit `b19a106`, deploy run `25272066664`, build 1m6s + deploy 22s): pre-existing structural bug surfaced for the first time. The PWA's workbox precaches `index.html` per `vite-plugin-pwa` config, and that HTML references content-hashed chunk filenames (e.g. `FamilyNookPage-DZK3iJ0T.js`). After every prod deploy those filenames rotate; users still on a previously-precached `index.html` 404 on every lazy `import()` → "oh no, the beans spilled" overlay → the overlay's "Reload" button was a soft `window.location.reload()` that the SW just intercepted and re-served the same stale HTML, leaving users looping until the SW updated on its own (often hours, depending on `registerType: 'prompt'` + when the user dismissed/accepted the update banner). Five-part fix in one PR: new `src/utils/hardReload.ts` recovery primitive (SW `update()` → `SKIP_WAITING` → `caches.delete()` for all caches → `location.replace()`); `router.onError` matches chunk-load message shapes (Chrome / Firefox / Safari variants) and calls `hardReload()` automatically with a `sessionStorage` loop guard cleared by `afterEach` so future deploys can recover too; `vite:preloadError` window listener catches the modulepreload variant; chunk-load failures filtered out of `unhandledrejection` so they stop spamming `#beanies-errors`; error-overlay Reload + Sign Out & Clear Data both call `hardReload()` instead of soft `location.reload()`; AppHeader refresh icon surfaces "A new version is ready / Reload Now" action toast when `safeServiceWorkerUpdate` detects a waiting SW worker (kept the routine refresh path data-only, didn't promote the icon to always-hard-reload). New `Known noise patterns` memory entry documents the now-filtered signature so future triages start from the known list. **(2) Auth-transient toast suppression** (commit `e74f6b5`, deploy run `25276899596`, build 1m11s + deploy 21s): caught after the first deploy when greg tested the reload-icon flow with an expired Google token + failed silent refresh. Two layers were producing competing user-facing signals for the same auth-transient state — the auth layer (per the recent `e5fee92` self-heal fix) intentionally stays quiet on transient silent-refresh failures and only escalates to a Google reconnect banner on `invalid_grant`, but the sync layer was setting `backgroundSyncError = 'Could not refresh data from cloud'` on every failed read, which `BackgroundSyncBar`'s watcher promoted to a loud warning toast. Result: every reload-icon tap (and every auto-poll cycle) fired the toast even though the auth layer was correctly handling the situation. Classified `backgroundSyncError` by kind (`auth-transient` / `decrypt` / `network`) — sync state still flips so success-toast gating in `AppHeader.handleRefreshAll` works (no false success), but `BackgroundSyncBar` skips the toast when kind is `auth-transient`. Auth layer keeps owning the user-facing escalation. Detection regex matches the `silent refresh failed` substring shared by both `TokenExpiredError` shapes. **(3) Activity modal-stack fix** (commit `df395df`, deploy run `25276899596` — same workflow as #2): caught after E2E ran on the second deploy push. The recurring webkit-only "Activity with monthly fee creates recurring item" flake hit again (3rd hard-fail recurrence — 2026-04-16 / 04-22 / 04-30 / 05-03). Documented in `E2E_HEALTH.md` as `(c) flake` three times running but actually a real ordering bug all along. Root cause finally found: in `FamilyPlannerPage.handleSave`, the create branch opened `CreatedConfirmModal` BEFORE closing `ActivityModal` — so for one tick both `<BaseModal>` instances were in the DOM with `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"`. WebKit's a11y/focus engine, under CI contention, would stall the second modal's visibility for >15s while the first was still teleported in. Reordered: `showModal.value = false` first, `await nextTick()` to let Vue flush the v-if removal, then open the confirm dialog. `E2E_HEALTH.md` updated with the diagnosis + reclassified the prior three (c) entries as the same latent ordering bug (`(a) → (b)`). `TransactionsPage.handleTransactionSave` follows the same close-then-open pattern but without `nextTick`; left as-is since it hasn't flaked, apply the same pattern preemptively if it surfaces. **E2E follow-up — webkit AccountCategoryPicker subtype rendering** (NOT yet fixed, see Pending block): the modal-stack fix removed the symptom that test was failing on but exposed a different webkit-only blocker earlier in the same flow — `cross-entity.spec.ts:347` now hard-fails at `AccountsPage.selectAccountType('checking')` waiting for the `🏦 Checking` subtype button to render. Same shape as 2026-04-30 (`AccountCategoryPicker.vue:126` conditional `v-if="expandedCat()!.subtypes"` lags on webkit-CI under contention). Three other webkit tests passed on retry as flakes hitting the same subtype path. Chromium 21/21 green throughout. Deploy gate (CI + Security) is green so this doesn't block prod — but the activity-monthly-fee test will keep hard-failing on webkit until the v-if is restructured. Suggested fix shape: replace conditional v-if rendering with always-rendered + `v-show`, OR pre-mount the subtype group via `<KeepAlive>`. **Tests/build status**: 1932 unit tests pass throughout the session (was 1920 → +12 from the inter-session owner-role ship that landed mid-session); type-check + lint clean; build clean. **Other-terminal commits merged via rebase\*\*: greg made three commits on a parallel session (`602fcbf` activity categories tidy, `bb5e674` owner role refactor, `3f881a3` evening status wrap) — both my pushes hit fetch-first rebases; CHANGELOG.md merge conflict resolved both times by keeping all entries.)

Renamed `Fun` → `Party` (group label only, contents unchanged); added new `Entertainment` group with 8 items — Movie 🎬, Show / Musical 🎭, Concert 🎵, Theme Park 🎢, Sporting Event 🏟️, Museum 🏛️, Festival / Fair 🎪, Other Entertainment ✨ — using a rose/pink palette distinct from existing groups. All eight new entertainment activities map to the existing `entertainment` expense category in `activityCategoryToExpenseCategory()` so logging "$45 for Friday movie" pre-fills the right expense bucket. Travel-banner copy at the top of the activity drawer also tightened: `vacation.planningATrip` "Make It a Family Vacation!" → "Add a Travel Plan!" (closer match to what tapping it actually does — opens the trip planner, not commits to a vacation). 11 translation keys updated/added; `npm run translate` regenerated Chinese cleanly with 1 stale key removed. **Owner role refactor end-to-end** (commit `bb5e674`): triggered by greg looking at his prod pod (Parker Meng Beanies, one of the earliest prod families) and seeing zero Owner pills on any card — confirmed via the chip text he could read off the cards: he was "Admin", everyone else "Member", nobody had `role === 'owner'`. Three connected problems addressed in one PR per CLAUDE.md sustainability principles (DRY/elegance/no-silent-failures/multi-pass review). **(1) Missing-Owner self-heal**: `applyDefaults()` in `familyMemberRepository.ts` was backfilling six fields but not `role`, so legacy/migrated records with a stripped owner had no defensive heal — `role` came back as `undefined`, the `currentRole !== 'owner'` check trivially passed, and the dropdown rendered "Member" instead of the Owner pill. Fix: `applyDefaults()` now backfills `role: member.role ?? 'member'`, and a new `normalizeRoles()` helper runs on every load (idempotent, single `changeDoc()` per write batch) — ensures exactly one Owner exists by promoting the earliest-created human (preferring the `requiresPassword === false` family-creator seat) if none, demoting later owners if multiple, and migrating legacy `admin` rows to `member` while persisting `canManagePod = true` so existing admins keep their effective permission survives the rule change. canManagePod default in applyDefaults narrowed from `(role === 'owner' || role === 'admin')` to `(role === 'owner')` only — safe because normalize stamps the flag explicitly before the rule has effect. Fast-path early return when no writes are needed (no-op on subsequent loads). reportError fires on the no-owner-promoted case so we capture how often the heal triggers in the wild. **(2) Card cleanup**: `MemberRoleManager.vue` deleted entirely (37 LOC + the only consumer was BeanCard.vue:250). Owner identity is now a Heritage Orange 👑 crown overlaid on the owner's avatar (top-right corner, 36% size, white ring, mirrors BeanieAvatar's existing bottom-right filter-badge mechanics — single additive `ownerBadge?: boolean` prop with a code comment explaining the slot/prop evolution path when a second per-avatar badge is needed). Non-owner cards show no role chip at all — frees the name row entirely. Granular permission editing (canManagePod / canViewFinances / canEditActivities) is unchanged: it still lives in the existing pencil-icon `FamilyMemberModal.vue`, where it always was. Dead `updateMemberRole()` action also removed from familyStore (no callers after Stage 2). **(3) Transfer Pod Ownership flow**: new Settings → Transfer Pod Ownership tile (gated to `isOwner === true`) opens a three-step `BeanieFormModal` — single host modal, no nested overlay stacking. Step 1 picks an adult human via `<FamilyChipPicker>` (extended with one additive `members?: FamilyMember[]` prop so caller can pass an adults-minus-current-owner list without coupling the picker to new filter logic). Step 2 re-authenticates via new `<ReauthChallenge>` component at `src/components/auth/` — passkey-first via `authenticateWithPasskey()`, falls back to `<PasswordModal>` with `verifyPassword()` against the owner's stored hash. Edge case (no passkey + no password) shows a clear "Set a password in Settings → Security first" recovery prompt and reports the case so we know if it ever fires. Cancellation drops back to choice (silent — passkey-cancellation is established noise per ADR). Step 3 confirms with danger-styled "Transfer Ownership" button. The store action `transferOwnership(toMemberId)` does the demote + promote in a **single atomic `changeDoc()` callback** so Automerge sees one transaction (no partial-failure reconciliation code needed). In-place `members.value.map(...)` update follows the existing `updateMember()` pattern (faster than full re-fetch + re-walk through applyDefaults). New `authStore.updateCurrentUserRole()` keeps the session role in sync if the outgoing or incoming owner is the current authenticated user — UI re-renders with the new state without a reload. Registry `UserFamilyMapping.familyRole` write **deliberately skipped**: `grep -rn familyRole` confirmed it's written at signup but never read anywhere — writing dead data adds complexity for zero gain; tracked as separate cleanup tech debt. `<ReauthChallenge>` extracted as reusable since three foreseeable callers exist (transfer ownership, future delete-pod, future leave-pod) — clear contract (`open` + `member` props, `verified`/`cancelled` events). 12 new unit tests cover normalizeRoles (one-owner no-op, two-owners demote, no-owner promote-creator, no-owner promote-fallback, admin migration with canManagePod preserved, changeDoc throw resilience, empty list) and transferOwnership (happy path, pet target rejection, same-owner rejection, ghost target rejection, authStore role sync). All 1932 unit tests pass; type-check + lint clean. **Plan archived**: `docs/plans/2026-05-03-owner-role-refactor.md` — multi-pass review applied (DRY pass identified `<ReauthChallenge>` extraction + `members?` prop reuse + `BeanieAvatar.ownerBadge` prop reuse over building new components; sustainability pass killed nested-modal stacking design + `useConfirm` overlay + dead-code carry; correctness pass replaced full re-fetch with in-place map). **Both ships deployed in one Vue prod workflow** (run `25273999158`, build 1m4s + deploy 22s) via `/deploy-prod-auto-skip-ci` — `classify-changes.sh` saw both `602fcbf` and `bb5e674` as pending since the morning's `e74f6b5` deploy. > **Earlier 2026-05-01 update (evening):** auth-reliability follow-up session, two deploys, two surgical fixes that close real symptoms greg hit in production. **Picker error disambiguation + Slack alerting for all join-flow errors** (commit `9360701`, Vue prod deploy `25218765602`, build 1m8s + deploy 22s): triggered by greg testing onboarding for a stuck user (Xu Family / `elaine1.galao@gmail.com` on iPhone iOS 18.7 / Safari 26.3) — the user kept hitting `PICKER_SCRIPT_LOAD_FAILED` after successful OAuth, and greg reproduced the _same_ error on his Android Chrome 147 by scanning her invite link and signing in to her Google account on consent. Audit found three connected issues: (1) the `reason: 'script'` value was overloaded across 5 distinct underlying failure modes — config missing, script-tag load fail, picker construction throw (most likely "google.picker is undefined" post-load), auth-chain throw, plus the existing iframe/timeout paths — all collapsed to one opaque code with the `(e as Error).message` logged to console and dropped on the floor. (2) Worse, picker errors _never reached `#beanies-errors`_ — only 1 of 8 `currentError.value = ...` sites in `useJoinFlow.ts` called `reportError`, and it wasn't the picker one. We'd been debugging from user-copy-pasted diagnostic blobs the whole time. (3) The `scriptPromise` was cached at module scope and never reset on `onerror`, so the "Retry" button on a failed picker called `loadPickerScript` → returned the same rejected promise forever without ever attempting another fetch. Fix shipped: widened `PickBeanpodFileResult.failed.reason` to `'config' | 'load' | 'open' | 'auth' | 'iframe' | 'timeout'` with an optional `message` carrying the captured exception text through to the diagnostic blob; new `recordError` helper in `useJoinFlow` consolidates all 8 error sites into one source of truth that ALWAYS fires `reportError` with the captured detail in the message body; `scriptPromise = null` reset on `script.onerror`; force-consent on the `'needs-pick'` fallthrough path in `runCloudFlow` so the picker doesn't silently re-use a wrong-account silent token; structural cleanup of `usePickBeanpodFile.pick`'s try-block to narrow it to only the auth chain (since `pickBeanpodFile` always-resolves by contract — making the auth-vs-picker boundary visible in code prevents future drift). The 5-reason taxonomy maps cleanly onto the existing 3 picker codes (no new error codes, no new i18n strings, no new components, no view changes). 1908 → 1916 unit tests pass; type-check + lint clean. **Silent Google token refresh self-healing across reload + tab wake** (commit `e5fee92`, Vue prod deploy `25220481552`, build 1m + deploy 22s): triggered by greg seeing the yellow reconnect toast 3× today after multi-hour inactivity AND right after tapping the "get fresh beans" banner — every reconnect succeeded via the manual flow, proving the refresh token in IndexedDB was valid and the system just wasn't doing the silent refresh it should have. Three-track audit (`expiryCallbacks` trigger chain, refresh-token persistence/restore, Drive-sync auth + 401 handling) found five contributing issues, all addressed in one fix: (1) `getValidTokenSilent()` was firing the banner from inside its own catch path on ANY silent-refresh failure including transients (network blip, 5xx, mid-SW activation), so callers had no chance to retry before the user saw it. (2) Module-level `setTimeout` for auto-refresh dies on full page reload AND is throttled while the tab is hidden — no `visibilitychange` listener proactively re-validated the token on focus. (3) Banner had no self-healing path — once up, stayed up even when a later silent refresh succeeded. (4) Single-attempt wake refresh in `attemptSilentReconnect`. (5) Already-correct `invalid_grant` short-circuit (kept). Fix: split callbacks into expiry (transient-eligible, no banner) vs `onTokenPermanentlyExpired` (`invalid_grant` only — the banner's sole legitimate trigger); new `installAuthWakeListener` registered from `initializeAuth` proactively calls `attemptSilentRefresh` on `visibilitychange` AND once at install when the token expires within ~2 minutes (covers cold boot / SW reload); `syncStore.setupTokenExpiryHandler` now subscribes `handleGoogleReconnected` to `onTokenAcquired` so any successful silent refresh auto-clears the banner; `MAX_ATTEMPTS` bumped 2 → 3 with stepped backoff `[1500, 3000]` ms. Net effect: the toast appears only when Google has actually revoked the refresh token (`invalid_grant`), never on transient failures, tab-wake, or SW reload. New `__resetWakeListenerForTesting` export prevents stale-listener accumulation across `vi.resetModules()` boundaries. 1908 → 1916 unit tests pass; type-check + lint clean. **Plans archived**: `docs/plans/2026-05-01-silent-token-refresh-reliability.md` (today's session). The earlier picker-error plan from this morning is preserved in the `in-the-past-we-compressed-spindle.md` ephemeral plan-mode file (not migrated to `docs/plans/` because the deploy skill needed plan-mode-exit timing that interfered with the canonical archive flow). **What to watch over the next 24-48h**: `#beanies-errors` channel for any new `join-flow:PICKER_*` reports — they'll now carry the captured exception text in the Slack message body, giving us the input for any Phase 2 targeted fix (most likely candidate: `picker_construct` with `google.picker is undefined` → add a post-condition check + one-shot retry in `loadPickerLibrary`). Greg should also see the reconnect toast disappear from his daily experience unless his Google account actually revokes the grant.)

Four commits, two Vue prod deploys, one terraform apply. **OAuth Lambda hardened** (commit `9cc8f60`, deployed via `terraform apply`): four CORS-hygiene improvements informed by external self-hoster Sam Ledoux's reference implementation — `Vary: Origin` on every CORS response (closes the cache-poisons-wrong-origin window), `Cache-Control: no-store` on every response (token exchanges are credentials, no intermediary should cache), defense-in-depth `403 forbidden_origin` for POSTs whose Origin header isn't allowlisted (browser CORS only blocks the response read, not the request itself, so without this an attacker page could have the proxy execute requests against Google server-side), and `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` dropped in favor of auto-derive from `CORS_ORIGIN` as `<origin>/oauth/callback` for each origin (single source of truth, one less env var for self-hosters, matches SPA's hardcoded callback path at `src/services/google/googleAuth.ts:119`). 8 new test cases (29 total, all passing). Verified prod's terraform `cors_origins` default lists exactly the same 4 origins as the old hardcoded array — zero behavior change for cloud users. Greg confirmed Drive sign-in works in prod after apply. **Migadu apex TXT records codified** (commit `6450be7`): caught during the OAuth Lambda's `terraform plan` — two TXT strings on the apex record set (`hosted-email-verify=8uetlptp` Migadu domain verify + `v=spf1 include:spf.migadu.com -all` SPF) had been added manually outside Terraform when greg set up Migadu, so the plan wanted to delete them as drift. All chip labels + step titles respect beanie-mode lowercase (every visible string flows through `t()` with `en`/`beanie` variants — no Title Case carrying forward into the new wizard). **Architecture wins shipped alongside**: (1) `BaseCombobox` dropdown now teleports to `<body>` with edge-aware fixed positioning (computed via `getBoundingClientRect()`, flips upward when near viewport bottom, listens to scroll/resize for re-anchoring) — benefits every combobox usage in the project, not just onboarding; eliminates the "dropdown clipped at modal edge" failure mode universally. Greg validated bean-tap navigation in dev before deploy after a meaningful course-correction: initial implementation pushed a synthetic `history.pushState` marker on stack open (via the new `useBackGestureClose` composable) so the platform back gesture would close the stack — but the marker raced with `router.push` from bean taps, causing the destination URL to be popped past back to where the stack was opened (visible symptom: every bean tap "reloaded" /nook). Bean tap is now plain `router.push` — identical to the original flat navbar. The composable + its 7 unit tests stay in the repo for the future `useQuickAdd` refactor (PR 2). **Pending / Next Session**: (1) PR 2 — refactor `BaseModal` and `MobileHamburgerMenu` to consume `useEscapeClose` + `useBodyScrollLock` (~75 lines of inline duplication to remove across 2 files); single-purpose cleanup PR with isolated regression risk. (2) Manual VoiceOver smoke on iOS Safari for the v3 nav (Tab cycle, `aria-expanded` announcements, focus restoration on close) — JSDOM can't simulate Tab traversal so this is the only a11y check not yet unit-asserted. > **Earlier 2026-04-27 update:**
> **Last updated:** 2026-04-27 (late afternoon — eliminated the unsolicited Google popup after deploys and during background sync. Three Drive code paths (`googleAuth.getValidToken`, `googleDriveProvider.read`, `googleDriveProvider.write`) fell through to `requestAccessToken()` on silent-refresh failure — opening a popup synchronously without a user gesture, which is what greg was seeing as "asked to re-authenticate after every deploy". Root cause: brief network turbulence during SW activation makes the post-reload silent refresh fail occasionally; the old code interpreted that as "open a popup right now" instead of "show a reconnect banner and wait for a click". New `getValidTokenSilent()` is the silent-only path used by all background Drive operations; on failure it throws `TokenExpiredError` AND fires the existing `onTokenExpired` callback so syncStore surfaces the existing reconnect banner. Original `getValidToken` (popup-fallback) retained for genuinely user-gesture-triggered call sites only (Settings reconnect, invite share). Failed writes queue via existing offline flush and replay on reconnect — zero data loss. Tests updated: 26 provider tests now assert no-popup behavior + offline-queue + TokenExpiredError surfacing. 1632 unit tests pass; type-check + lint clean.)

> **Earlier 2026-04-27 update:**
> **Last updated:** 2026-04-27 (afternoon — fixed the "PWA shows yesterday's data" bug end-to-end. New `useToday()` composable is the single reactive source of truth for the local day, owning the only `visibilitychange` + `pageshow` listeners + a self-rearming midnight `setTimeout` (DST-safe via fresh `new Date(y, m, d+1, 0, 0, 0)` per arm). New `useStaleTabRefresh()` watches that composable's reactive state and runs a heavy refresh on day-change OR long-absence (>5 min) wake: `reloadAllStores → processRecurringItems → updateRatesIfStale + attemptSilentReconnect (parallel) → reloadIfFileChanged`. Per-step error classification with explicit `[useStaleTabRefresh]`-prefixed logs — critical step (reloadAllStores) toasts the user via `error.backgroundRefreshFailed.{title,help}` and aborts downstream; non-critical steps log + continue. App.vue removed its own `visibilitychange` registration; save-on-hide is now a single `watch(useToday().isVisible)`. `attemptSilentReconnect` extracted from App.vue to `src/utils/silentReconnect.ts` with the bare `catch {}` replaced by a logged warning. Eighteen call sites swept to read `today` from the composable. Replaces and rewrites `docs/plans/2026-04-10-stale-tab-refresh.md` in place. Modal date-default edge case (open at 23:59, save at 00:01) tracked separately as #187 — silent UX mutation is worse than the bug. 26 new unit tests (12 `useToday`, 14 `useStaleTabRefresh` including error-classification cases for every step). Full suite green: 1630 tests pass, type-check + lint clean.)

Root cause: `useGoogleReconnect.reconnect()` calls `requestAccessToken()` which opens a popup, and standalone PWAs (Chrome on Android, Edge, etc.) can't bridge popup→postMessage back to the installed-app window — the popup either fails to open or lands in a different browser context, so the auth flow hung forever and the catch returned a silent false. Fix: `shouldUseRedirectAuth()` now returns true for standalone PWAs (matchMedia `display-mode: standalone` OR navigator.standalone === true) in addition to iOS Safari; `useGoogleReconnect.reconnect()` honors it and routes through `startRedirectAuth(returnPath)` when detected — page navigates to Google, returns to the same path, and a new `completeRedirectAuth` call in App.vue's onMounted (after auth init, before family resolve, wrapped in try/catch so failures never block app boot) consumes the pending OAuth code so the next Drive operation picks up the fresh token automatically. Also surfaces failure feedback that was swallowed before: `reconnectError` is now `string | null` (was bool) and the SettingsPage Family Data section renders the actual error message when reconnect fails for any non-redirect reason. Existing v-if checks against reconnectError continue to work since both null and bool false coerce identically. Test mock for `useGoogleReconnect` updated with the two new exports + new test covering the standalone-PWA branch (5/5 pass, 1510 total). **Hotfix #5 — recovery action for "file not found"** (`504ffb7`, deploy run `24935912288` 1m29s ✅): greg's running PWA showed the red "your data file was not found" banner after sign-out + clear data + sign-in; reconnect button now worked but didn't help because `handleGoogleReconnected()` short-circuits when `driveFileNotFound=true` (line 1412) — the existing recovery is "fresh token", which doesn't fix a missing per-file scope grant. Root cause: `signOut()` in `authStore.ts:490` awaits `flushPendingSave()` before clearing auth, and that calls `save()` which writes to Drive. > **Updated by:** Claude (2026-04-25 evening session — fixed two onboarding bugs that were poisoning the new-user funnel for any invitee on an iPhone. Reported by greg's wife mid-test of a fresh invite from a Google-Drive-backed pod. **Bug 1 — iOS Safari "popups are blocked" right after QR scan**: the join page (`src/components/login/JoinPodView.vue`) fired Google OAuth on `onMounted` via `attemptFileLoad` → `syncStore.loadFromGoogleDrive` → `requestAccessToken` → `window.open`. Safari (and every iOS WebKit browser) blocks `window.open` outside the synchronous call stack of a user gesture, so the popup is denied 100% of the time on iPhone. The existing redirect-auth fallback (`startRedirectAuth` at `googleAuth.ts:558-577`) was wired only into the manual `handlePickFromDrive` click handler, not into the auto-load path on mount. **Fix**: added two helpers to `src/services/google/googleAuth.ts` — `shouldUseRedirectAuth()` (detects iPhone/iPad/iPod by UA + iPadOS-as-Mac via `maxTouchPoints > 1`) and `tryGetSilentToken()` (returns cached token via `isTokenValid`, falls through to `attemptSilentRefresh`, returns null if interactive auth is required — never pops UI). `attemptFileLoad` now uses `tryGetSilentToken()` before touching `loadFromGoogleDrive`; without a token it sets `cloudLoadFailed.value = true` + `needsManualFileLoad.value = true` and surfaces the "Pick from Drive" CTA. The CTA's click handler (`handlePickFromDrive`) now checks `shouldUseRedirectAuth()` first and goes straight to full-page `startRedirectAuth(returnPath)` on iOS — popup attempt skipped entirely. Belt-and-braces: the popup-blocked catch fallback is still in place for any platform that slips through. **Side bonus**: when the invite URL carries `fileId=<driveFileId>` (which it does for Drive-backed invites — see `MeetTheBeansPage.vue:159`), the post-auth flow prefers auto-loading by fileId over forcing the user through the Picker — only falls back to Picker if the auto-load fails. **Bug 2 — "that folder doesn't have a pod inside" false negative**: introduced 5 days earlier in commit `a21cf08` when the join flow switched from picking the `.beanpod` file to picking the `beanies.family` folder (intended fix for joiners' photo access; subsequently obsoleted by the public-link + CDN approach for photos). The folder-pick triggers `findBeanpodInFolder` (`driveService.ts:530`) which queries `'<folderId>' in parents and name contains '.beanpod'` — but under the `drive.file` OAuth scope, picking a shared folder does NOT grant API list-access to files owned by another user, so the query returns 0 results even when the `.beanpod` is visibly inside the folder via the Drive UI. **Fix**: reverted the join flow to picking the `.beanpod` file directly via `pickBeanpodFile` (`drivePicker.ts:145`, kept around through the folder transition). File-pick grants direct `drive.file` access to the chosen file, which works correctly for files shared by another user. Removed the misleading `@deprecated` note on `pickBeanpodFile`. Photos remain reachable independently via the public-link + CDN approach already in place — no scope change needed. **Files touched**: `src/components/login/JoinPodView.vue` (swap `pickBeanpodFolder` → `pickBeanpodFile`; gate auto-load behind `tryGetSilentToken`; route iOS through `startRedirectAuth`; prefer fileId auto-load over Picker after auth; redirect-completion path no longer forces Picker when fileId is in URL), `src/services/google/googleAuth.ts` (add `shouldUseRedirectAuth` + `tryGetSilentToken` exports), `src/services/google/drivePicker.ts` (un-deprecate `pickBeanpodFile`, replace doc with rationale). **Dead code left in repo**: `pickBeanpodFolder` + `findBeanpodInFolder` + `NoBeanpodInFolderError` + the `noBeanpodInFolder` translation key are now unused in production but kept (their tests still pass; they may be useful if photo-access architecture changes again). Cleanup is a low-priority follow-up. **Verified**: `npm run type-check` clean; `npm run lint` no new warnings on changed files; 80/80 unit tests in `src/services/google/` pass; pre-push hook ran the full 1509-test suite green. **Deploy**: Vue `deploy.yml` run `24930704417` 1m32s ✅ (build 1m04s + S3+CloudFront 21s) shipped on commit `a8f1a24`. Skip-gate used (CI + Security still running in background — small surgical change, validated locally). Marketing site untouched (no `web/` changes). **Validation needed**: real-device test on iPhone Safari with a fresh invite link — scan QR, expect "Pick from Drive" CTA (not popup error) → tap → full-page redirect to Google → return to /join → file auto-loads by fileId. **Earlier 2026-04-25 afternoon session** still also covered the design-only mockup work below.)

> - **🐛 Bug: "Switch Google account" → empty warning modal that keeps coming back.** Reported by greg after deploy of `41da938`. Repro: Settings → Family Data → click **Switch Google account** → Google's account chooser dialog appears → close it without picking an account → an empty warning modal appears → dismiss it → it keeps coming back. Two distinct failures fused: **(a)** the modal is empty, suggesting either the title/message translation keys (`settings.familyData.switchAccount` / `settings.familyData.switchAccountFailed`) aren't resolving correctly in the `useConfirm` alert state, or `useConfirm`/`ConfirmModal` doesn't render passed translation keys at all on this code path; **(b)** the modal re-appears on dismiss, suggesting a re-trigger loop — most likely candidate is `armAccountSwitch()` + `clearGoogleSessionState()` running before consent (so the flag stays armed AND the in-memory token is wiped), then a subsequent silent-refresh / sync attempt either re-enters the cleared-state path or some watcher refires the handler. **Investigation start points**: `src/pages/SettingsPage.vue` `handleSwitchGoogleAccount` (the catch block + showAlert call); `src/composables/useConfirm.ts` (how the alert state renders translation keys); whether `useConfirm.ts:48` `confirm()` reuses module-level `state` and could be re-triggered by reactive rerender of the Settings page after auth state clears; whether `syncStore.driveFileNotFound` or `syncStore.showGoogleReconnect` flips after the cleared state and triggers the SaveFailureBanner / its modal. **Quick test**: try replacing `showAlert` with a plain `console.warn` on cancel and see if (i) the loop disappears (then it's the modal causing the loop somehow) or (ii) the loop persists with no UI (then it's an auth-state-driven re-trigger). Likely-cheapest fix: don't `armAccountSwitch()` + `clearGoogleSessionState()` until _after_ the user has confirmed account selection in Google's chooser — i.e. let `requestAccessToken` complete first, THEN flip state. Adjust `handleSwitchGoogleAccount` accordingly. The whole switch-account flow is a low-traffic deliberate action; assertion + cleanup-on-signout do the load-bearing work for the actual reported bug. Not P0 but worth fixing before the next prod-impacting account-stickiness reproduces.

**Mixed-version caveats (documented, accepted — native update ships in same window):**
(a) ≤0.13 clients can't open KIT-BORN envelopes (throw "No wrapped keys" unless a
passphrase is set); (b) PIN-only members read as UNCLAIMED on ≤0.13 clients
(re-invitable, excluded from transfer, un-provable on pre-0.13 native); (c) old
clients ignore `lk=1` and dead-end a device link in the unclaimed-only join. Copy on
the mint card + join set-pin step says "the other device needs beanies 0.14 or later".

### ⭐ 2. #65/#61 — re-validate the open-guard fix in prod (the 24h window is now OPEN) ⭐

**State (corrected 2026-08-19):** #65 is **LIVE in prod**. The 08-18 deploy ran on `70f03983`, which has `46f1c79a` as an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms) — the old "NOT deployed / step 1: deploy" text below was wrong. `PERFORMANCE.md` §10's after-column was likewise already filled (`025e0c67`), so steps 1-2 of the plan below are DONE.

**VALIDATION RESULT — the BAD case fired.** CloudWatch `open-cycle`, 2026-08-17 00:00Z → 2026-08-19, n=24 across R8/R9/R10: **zero** `unchanged-revision-in-window` on R10 (R9 had 3, at `rec=1 reads=0 writes=0`), and `baseline-heads-unknown` on the same client 19.4h apart (03:23:17, 03:23:19, 22:46:55) instead of decaying within the hour. Full table + evidence in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` §10.

**ROOT CAUSE (found, NOT fixed).** Every cold-open/sign-in call site calls `loadFromFile()` with no options, so `merging` is false (`syncStore.ts:845`) and the open takes the **replace** branch, which leaves `driveHeads = null` (`syncStore.ts:936`). Terminus 1 then calls `commitRemoteBaseline(null)` unconditionally (`syncStore.ts:986`), persisting `headsFp: null` and — because the commit is last-write-wins (C10b) — **clobbering** any good fingerprint `doSave`'s terminus 3 had recorded. The next open therefore trips `baseline-heads-unknown` (`syncService.ts:719`) forever. #61's skip is inert in prod.

**FIX — IMPLEMENTED AND DEPLOYED (2026-08-19, `0.9.10R11`).** `replaceDocWithCacheRecovery` already calls `mergeRemoteEnvelope` and discards `remoteHeads` (`syncStore.ts:790`). Return it and feed terminus 1. The branch's justifying comment — "our doc is knowably AHEAD of Drive, so no fingerprint may be claimed" — is the bug: the fingerprint records what **Drive** holds, and being ahead is what #65's own `unpushedLocalChangesCheck` already reports as `unpushed-local-changes`. Done: `replaceDocWithCacheRecovery` now returns `remoteHeads` and terminus 1 commits it on both branches. Regression test `src/stores/__tests__/syncStore.openBaselineTerminus.test.ts` (4 cases) — confirmed RED against the old code with exactly the diagnosed value (`null` for the drive heads) and green after. Full suite 4456 green, type-check + lint 0 errors.

**STILL TO DO — the fix is DEPLOYED (`2c7ae834`, shipped in `0.9.10R11`, and again in `0.9.11` which went to prod 2026-08-19 07:41Z) but UNVALIDATED. The 24h window is now OPEN — this is actionable immediately.** Re-run the `open-cycle` query and confirm organic `unchanged-revision-in-window` at `rec=1 reads=0` reappears, and that `baseline-heads-unknown` decays within the hour instead of persisting.

**Note on the R10 `unpushed-local-changes` event** (Android, family `…cda0c344`, 10:59Z): it reports `writes=0`, which deserves an explanation given #65 exists to re-push on exactly that path. May simply be that the write lands after the terminus emits. Unverified.

**The risk this validation exists to catch.** #65 adds a second barrier in front of #61's skip. If the Drive-heads fingerprint is not being recorded correctly at the four termini, EVERY open declines to skip and the #61 win (`rec=2 reads=1` → `rec=1 reads=0`, shipped yesterday as `0.9.10R9`) silently evaporates. That failure is **invisible to tests and produces no error** — it looks like slower opens and more Drive reads. It is only detectable in telemetry.

**greg — what you need to do, in order:**

1. **Deploy.** `/deploy-prod-auto` (web/PWA + Android + iOS TestFlight). Nothing below can be checked before this.
2. **Capture the #61 after-numbers FIRST, before the #65 deploy skews them.** ⚠️ If `PERFORMANCE.md` §10's after-column is still empty (it is — local-only figures so far), take that reading from `0.9.10R9` data **now**. Once R10 is live the population is mixed and the like-for-like comparison against the PR-1 baseline (`rec=2 reads=1`) is gone for good.
3. **Use the app normally for a day** on at least two devices. Open, edit, background, reopen. The interesting states need real usage.
4. **Then pull `open-cycle` from CloudWatch** and hand the numbers back — the next session validates against them.

**The CloudWatch query — `surface = "open-cycle"`, last 24h, grouped by `error_code`:**

```
fields @timestamp, context.error_code as reason, context.rec as rec, context.reads as reads, context.writes as writes, message
| filter surface = "open-cycle"
| stats count(*) as n by reason
| sort n desc
```

**What GOOD looks like (the change is working):**

| `reason`                        | Expected                                                              | Meaning                                                     |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unchanged-revision-in-window`  | **the clear majority of repeat opens**, with `rec=1 reads=0 writes=0` | the #61 skip is still firing — THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS |
| `baseline-heads-unknown`        | a burst on deploy day, then **decays to ~0 within ~1h**               | the legacy-row upgrade cohort, one-shot and self-clearing   |
| `unpushed-local-changes`        | **rare** — only after a real force-kill/crash                         | the bug #65 fixes, actually firing                          |
| `trust-expired` / `no-baseline` | unchanged from R9                                                     | daily-user cold opens                                       |

**What BAD looks like — report any of these immediately:**

- **`unchanged-revision-in-window` collapses vs. the R9 baseline** → the fingerprint isn't being recorded; #61's win is gone. This is the primary regression and the whole reason for this validation.
- **`baseline-heads-unknown` stays flat/high past ~1h** → a terminus is never recording a fingerprint (suspect the replace/recovery branches or a `commitRemoteBaseline(null)` path).
- **`heads-probe-failed` appears at all beyond a trickle** → the worker probe is failing; check `surface = "sync-change-detect"`, `action = "heads-probe-failed"` for the stack.
- **`open-fail-open` (warn) rate rises** → note that `unpushed-local-changes` and `baseline-heads-unknown` are deliberately classified CLEAN, so a rise means genuine uncertainty, not #65 noise.

**Second query — the probe's own failures (new this change):**

```
fields @timestamp, message, context.error_code, error.name, error.message
| filter surface = "sync-change-detect" and context.action = "heads-probe-failed"
| sort @timestamp desc
```

**On-device repro to close the acceptance criterion** (needs two devices; only you can do this): edit something → force-kill the app within ~1-2s, before the save flushes → reopen within the hour on an otherwise-unchanged file → the edit should reach Drive **on that open** (second device sees it, or the `.beanpod`'s Drive `version` advances). Pre-#65 it would have waited for the next edit or trust expiry.

**Known telemetry gap (do not misread the numbers):** `endOpen` early-returns when there is no open token, and header **Refresh** + the deferred config-heal both re-enter `backgroundSyncFromFile` **tokenless** — so guard reasons from those paths emit NOTHING. The counts above are true-app-open only, and undercount by the share of tokenless entries. This is pre-existing (#61-era), not introduced by #65. Filed below as a follow-up.

**Two review findings deliberately NOT fixed** (both `/code-review max`, 2026-08-18):

- **Tokenless open-cycle emission** (above). Fixing it means changing what `open-cycle` COUNTS — it would stop meaning "app opens" — which would break the like-for-like #61 before/after comparison greg has not yet captured. Decide AFTER step 2. Likely fix: a separate surface for refresh/heal rather than widening `open-cycle`.
- Lower-severity items listed in the review output (orphaned JSDoc above `unpushedLocalChangesCheck`, a stale "only revision + checkedAt are persisted" comment at `syncService.ts:93`, `commitPendingBaseline`'s unchecked `a.payload as string` allowing `undefined` to destroy a valid row, `headsFingerprint` order-sensitivity, and untyped `commitRemoteBaseline` in `__mocks__/syncService.ts` which defeats the "compiler forces every terminus" property in the store-test realm). None are correctness-critical; worth a cleanup pass.

> - **Notion #49 — encrypt data sent to the AI provider (High).** Gate 3. Today `managedProvider.ts` POSTs the document as plaintext to our own Lambda, which builds the chat body and calls Tinfoil with our key, so **our server can read the user's document**. Research (recorded on the row) settled the shape: EHBP is a body-level HPKE layer (RFC 9180) that works through a _blind_ proxy — Tinfoil's own documented pattern — and the browser verifier is now ~50KB of pure TS (`tinfoil@1.1.7`), not the old 80MB WASM. Estimated 3-4 days. **One spike first:** does `inference.tinfoil.sh` serve CORS on `/.well-known/hpke-keys` and `/.well-known/tinfoil-attestation`? If not, relay both through our Lambda (safe — the attestation is hardware-signed and binds the HPKE key). This gates a public Play Store privacy claim.

**🟡 `#beanies-errors` watch for `app.chunkRecoveryFailed` (post-`d86e797`, deployed 2026-05-13):**

- `App.vue`'s init catch fires this when `isChunkLoadError(err) === true` AND the bounded-retry counter has already exhausted (3 silent hardReloads across all three callsites — `App.vue` catch / `router.onError` / `main.ts:vite:preloadError`). Includes `route_path` + the error message + the `attempts` count in the context. Cleared automatically on a successful boot via App.vue's post-init health check.
- **Baseline expectation: silent in steady state.** If it fires for any user/device, the layered fix (regex, SW unregister, CDN no-cache, old-chunk retention, bounded counter) isn't enough for that device class and we'd want to add another layer (likely: auto-trigger the "Sign out & clear data" path after N attempts instead of just showing the overlay). The very first deploy after a user's last load is the highest-risk window — if it's going to fire, that's where.

**🟡 `app.onboardingZombieState` pattern-watch (passive — no action unless a family stays stuck):**

- Fires ONCE per OAuth-redirect-return per page-load in the zombie state. The single alert per round-trip is expected — it's the safety net working. Pattern signals: (a) the same `family_id` firing multiple times across hours/days → a user is genuinely stuck on the resume-setup screen and may need a nudge; (b) the alert firing with `route_path` other than `/welcome` or `/welcome?resume=setup` → the router guard caught it on an SPA nav (e.g. `/activities`) which means they were trying to use the app while their session was zombie'd. (c) The `family_email` context being null in the Slack message (shown as "(not yet authenticated)") is a minor format oddity — it doesn't mean the user isn't authenticated; just that the family context wasn't initialized when the alert fired. Worth a small follow-up to backfill from `authStore.currentUser.email` if `family_email` is unset.

**🟢 (future, low-priority) Seed family settings from globalSettings on pod creation:**

- Surfaced by the 2026-05-16 `persistDualSetting` pre-pod gate. When a user picks `zh` on the welcome gate (`globalSettings.language = 'zh'`) and then creates a pod, the new family Automerge doc starts with `settings: null` and `settingsRepository.getDefaultSettings()` returns hard-coded `language: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` (= `'en'`). For `language` and `theme` the revert is invisible — `settingsStore.language` (`settingsStore.ts:32`) and `settingsStore.theme` (line 31) read globalSettings only, so the user's choice still drives the UI. For `textSize` (line 33-35) and `country` (line 92) the family value can override the device value, so a pre-pod choice could appear to revert post-pod for those two.
- Acceptance criterion: in `src/stores/authStore.ts` `signUp` / `buildOwnerDoc`, after `initDoc()`, call `settingsRepo.saveSettings({language, theme, textSize, country})` filtered to the keys actually set in globalSettings. ~10 lines. Held this session because pod-creation paths were heavily hardened on 2026-05-15 and adding code there now carries non-trivial regression risk for low user-visible reward.

**🟡 `#beanies-errors` watch for `storage-migration-*` (post-`3a457e4`, deployed 2026-05-12):**

- `migrateStorage` reports `{surface:'storage-migration-ok', severity:'warning', context:{from,to}}` on success and `{surface:'storage-migration-failed', severity:'error', context:{from,to,step}}` on failure (`step` ∈ `pre-swap`/`install`/`rollback`). The component's failure toasts pass `{silent:true}` so they don't double-report.
- Baseline expectation: occasional `storage-migration-ok` warnings = real adoption (great signal). Zero error-level pings under healthy conditions. A `step:'install'` failure means the move was rolled back cleanly (pod still on the source). A `step:'rollback'` failure means the rollback itself broke — **P1**: the user was told to sign out and back in to recover; check `fileHandleStore.getProviderConfig` state and triage via `/error-review`.

Pattern to watch for: any element with both Tailwind classes AND a long inline `style=""` attribute.

- Investigation paths (when prioritised): (a) reproduce minimally and file an upstream issue at github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss; (b) pin the plugin version in `package.json` to the last known-good if a regression PR landed; (c) add a project-level prettier override that disables the plugin for inline `style` attributes specifically.

**🟡 Silent-refresh diagnostic watch (post-`7a625c4`, deployed 2026-05-14 — SUPERSEDES the previous OAuth-fetch-timeout watch):**

- greg's iPhone 14 PWA fired 3 alerts within 47s today: 2× `cold-start-reconnect-escalation` + 1× `offline-queue-flush:flush rejected after visible`. All `save_failure_level: warning` (unsaved edits in the offline queue when the silent refresh failed) — so the alerts represent real UX friction, not background noise. greg's question: "why does iPhone keep losing connection to Google Drive and why can't it refresh silently?" — the alert today carries only the sentinel `Google access token expired and silent refresh failed` with no signal on **which** failure mode triggered the retry-exhaustion. Could be: (a) Lambda OAuth-proxy cold start (the proxy's been idle for hours, first wake-time request blows the 15s `withTimeout` budget), (b) iOS wake-network race (visibility-change fires before the cellular/wifi stack is fully ready), (c) refresh-token rotation/revocation that isn't classifying as `invalid_grant`, or (d) all three at once.
- **Instrumentation shipped today** (`7a625c4`): `performSilentRefresh` in `googleAuth.ts` now records per-attempt `{attempt, durationMs, classification, errorName, errorMessage}` on every failure (classifications: `permanent` / `timeout` / `network` / `http` / `unknown`), stashes on `lastSilentRefreshDiagnostics`, exposed via `getLastSilentRefreshDiagnostics()`. `syncStore.scheduleColdStartReconnectEscalation` pulls those + a lazy-registered visibility tracker (`page_hidden_for_ms`, `visibility_state`) and attaches them to the `reportError` context. Five new allowlisted context keys in `errorReporter.ts` — all timing + classification labels, zero user-typed content.
- **What the next alert from greg's iPhone PWA will carry**: `silent_refresh_attempts: [{"attempt":1,"durationMs":15001,"classification":"timeout",...}, {...}, {...}]` + `page_hidden_for_ms: N` + `visibility_state: visible|hidden` + `silent_refresh_had_refresh_token: true` + `silent_refresh_consecutive_failures: N`.
- **Decision tree on the next 2-3 captures**:
  - All `timeout` + `page_hidden_for_ms > 60000` → **iOS PWA wake + Lambda cold start**. Fix: warm-up ping on visibility-change, longer first-attempt budget, or provisioned Lambda concurrency.
  - All `network` + short `page_hidden_for_ms` → **wake-time stack race**. Fix: wait for `navigator.onLine && +500ms` before first attempt on visibility-resume.
  - Any `permanent` → **classifier regex too narrow** — revocation slipping past `invalid_grant` matching. Fix: expand the permanent-classification regex.
  - Mixed across captures → multi-pronged structural fix.
- **No code change today beyond instrumentation** — explicitly held back the structural fix until we have the diagnostic data. Captures expected within hours-to-days of greg backgrounding the iPhone PWA.
- Defense-in-depth still in place: `App.vue:512` 20s `Promise.race` wrap on `completeRedirectAuth()` — app init can't wedge even if a future code path adds another awaited fetch.

**🟡 Webkit-CI E2E flake watch — `selectAccountType` poll-for-hint (`5beac12`) + `page.goto('/')` navigation-interrupt (`906ce0e`):**

- **`page.goto('/')` navigation-interrupt (`906ce0e`, 2026-05-11)** — new flake: 8 webkit tests across 6 spec files failed at once in `beforeEach` hooks with `Navigation to "/" is interrupted by another navigation to "/nook"` (SPA router guard redirects `/` on first paint, racing the default `until: 'load'` wait under CI contention). `gh run rerun --failed` passed clean — pure flake. Hardened: new `e2e/helpers/navigation.ts` `gotoRoot(page)` → `page.goto('/', { waitUntil: 'commit' })`; all 18 bare `page.goto('/')` sites across 5 spec files replaced. Watch the next 2-3 webkit-CI runs: if the harden held, retire this bullet; if a different navigation-interrupt shape shows up (e.g. on `page.goto('/settings')` or `page.reload()`), apply the same `waitUntil: 'commit'` treatment there.

**🟢 ActivityCategory type union — sibling latent drift (small cleanup, no urgency):**

- `cc9cb56` aligned the three sources of truth that had drifted (`ACTIVITY_CATEGORIES` runtime list, `ActivityCategory` type union, `activityCategoryToExpenseCategory` map) and added an invariant test that locks all three together.
- However, `src/constants/activityPresets.ts` references activity IDs as `category: ActivityCategory` literals — these are typed but the file isn't covered by the new invariant test. Future drift in presets won't fail CI until either (a) a preset references a non-existent ID (would be caught by tsc immediately, fine), OR (b) a preset references a stale ID that was removed from the union (would be caught immediately, fine). Net: no actual gap — TypeScript covers the cross-file consistency. Deferred this from being a blocker.
- Worth noting only because: if any future helper string-types activity IDs (bypasses the union), it could re-introduce silent drift. Pattern to watch for in code review.

**🟢 Net-worth chart follow-ups (from 2026-04-22 plan, explicitly deferred):**

- **Asset value re-valuations have no history.** Changing `asset.currentValue` today retroactively rewrites every historical chart point for that asset. Per-asset valuation events would fix it; deferred. Documented in the doc-block of `utils/netWorthHistory.ts`.
- **Asset-to-liability `transfer` semantics.** `calculateBalanceAdjustment` increments destination balance by `+amount` for `transfer` type — wrong direction for credit-card payoffs (where dest balance should DECREASE). Needs a UX decision: restrict transfers to same-side accounts, or interpret cross-side transfers differently. Separate plan when prioritised.
- **Daily snapshots architecture.** Long-term, writing a daily `combinedNetWorth` snapshot to its own Automerge collection would obsolete the entire historical-replay module and immune the chart to whole classes of subtle miscount. Not a near-term priority; flagged in the `netWorthHistory.ts` doc-block as the right next step if more replay branches are needed.
- **`convertAmount` silent identity-fallback** when no FX rate path exists. Currently returns `amount` unconverted with no warning. Used app-wide; out of scope for the chart fix. Right fix is to return `undefined` and force callers to decide — bigger surgery.
