**CI health:**

- 🔴 **`lighthouse-ci.yml` has failed on every PR since 2026-07-20** (green through 07-14 — a clean transition, no gradual decay). **ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-21: a genuine homepage performance regression, NOT a build break.** Two error-level assertions on `index.html` only (blog + help pages score 0.99): `categories.performance` 0.88 vs `minScore` 0.90, and `largest-contentful-paint` 3245ms vs `maxNumericValue` 3000ms. **The LCP element is the hero mascot image, which LOADS in 84ms — 83% of its LCP (2707ms) is _render delay_.** Lighthouse attributed 1510ms of savings to two render-blocking stylesheets (`index.css` 10.9KB + `faq.css` 10.3KB); total blocking time was 0ms, so JS was never implicated. Cause: Astro's default `build.inlineStylesheets: 'auto'` only inlines under ~4KB, and the 2026-07-17 "three worlds" beanstalk homepage work (#56, `e77bc9b7` + follow-ups) pushed the homepage CSS past that, adding two blocking round trips to the critical path. **PARTIAL FIX SHIPPED to `main` (`6333c378`) — Lighthouse is STILL RED.** `build.inlineStylesheets: 'always'` (web/astro.config.mjs) removed both render-blocking stylesheets. Measured on `main` after the fix: performance **0.88 → 0.91 (now PASSES)**, render-blocking resources 2 → 0, CLS 0.018, TBT 70ms. **But LCP only moved 3245ms → 3158ms and still fails the 3000ms budget.** Lighthouse's advertised "1510ms of render-blocking savings" did NOT materialise, because inlining relocates the ~21KB of CSS into the HTML document rather than removing it from the critical path — the homepage HTML is now 189KB, and on LHCI's simulated throttling that download/parse is itself the bottleneck. Render delay is still 81% of LCP (2544ms) with FCP at 2.1s, while TBT is only 70ms and DOM is a healthy 717 elements — so this is a _critical-bytes_ problem, not a JS or DOM-complexity problem. **The remaining gap is ~158ms.** Next options (greg's call, not yet actioned): (a) a focused homepage perf pass — defer/lighten the decorative beanstalk section, split the single-page homepage, and take the 70KB `uses-responsive-images` saving; or (b) raise the LCP budget from 3000ms with a documented rationale, on the grounds that LHCI simulated mobile throttling is far harsher than real CloudFront-served traffic. Reverting the inline-CSS change is NOT recommended — it is a genuine improvement on its own merits.
  - ✅ **PR A SHIPPED (`f2b944a4`, 2026-07-21) — the LCP regression is FIXED, but the check now flaps on runner noise.** Per the 4-pass plan `docs/plans/2026-07-21-homepage-lcp-critical-css.md`. Two levers: (1) the hero's two above-the-fold decorative blobs used `filter: blur(100px)`/`blur(80px)` over solid circles — a large-radius blur is rastered on the main thread before first paint, so they were gating LCP. Replaced with pre-baked `radial-gradient`s, geometry derived from the fact that a CSS blur radius IS the Gaussian sigma (box grown to original + 3σ per side, re-anchored on the same centre). (2) `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 3000px` on the beanstalk section, which was ~27% of the homepage DOM and ~19.7KB of CSS that first paint had to style/lay out/paint despite being below the fold and scroll-driven. Also hoisted the LCP image path into one `HERO_MASCOT` const (it was written twice — `lcpImage` and `<img src>` — and drift would silently strip the preload from the LCP image with no failing assertion). **Measured on a quiet runner: LCP 3158ms → 2716ms (budget 3000), performance 0.91 → 0.94, render delay 2544ms → 2006ms, CLS unchanged at 0.018.**
  - ⚠️ **A bug this nearly shipped, caught by plan Pass 4 and worth remembering:** `content-visibility: auto` size-contains the subtree while skipped, so `getBoundingClientRect()` on descendants returns degenerate rects. `dockOffset()` runs during setup and reads rects from `#stage`/`#seedSlot` (both inside the section) to position the docked seed over its slot; it only recomputes on `resize` or a post-launch re-dock, **neither of which fires on a normal cold load**. Shipping (2) alone would have parked the seed in the wrong place on every first visit, silently. Fixed by making `dockOffset()` refuse a degenerate measurement (write nothing rather than garbage) and having `readScroll()` retry once the section is genuinely rendered — browser-agnostic, no tuned constant touched. Verified with Playwright at 412×823 on a cold load with no resize: docked seed centre lands exactly on slot centre (dx=0, dy=0). Hero equivalence verified by headless screenshot diff with `prefers-reduced-motion` forced (max channel diff 7/255, zero pixels >8/255).
  - 🔶 **NEW PROBLEM — the gate flaps on GitHub-runner contention, independent of our code.** The identical commit `f2b944a4` PASSED on its branch (perf 0.80/0.81/0.81, TBT 80ms) and then FAILED twice on `main` minutes later: first on `categories.performance` 0.73/0.61/0.81 **and** `total-blocking-time` 676/436/444ms, then on TBT alone at 1260/340/465ms. TBT on this page measured 70–80ms both before and after the fix, so a 1260ms reading is machine contention, not bytes. Earlier the same day, baseline runs were rock-steady (LCP 3165/3160/3158). **Implication: the LCP fix worked, but the check cannot currently be trusted as a merge gate**, and this is exactly the "thin margin + noisy runner = flapping" risk the plan flagged. **Do NOT land PR D (`push: [main]` trigger) until this is addressed** — it would install a permanently-flapping check on `main`. Options to weigh: raise `numberOfRuns` and set `aggregationMethod: 'median'` explicitly (currently the implicit default is `optimistic`, i.e. best-of-3 — so historical numbers are best-case), relax `total-blocking-time` which is the most contention-sensitive metric, or accept Lighthouse as advisory-only on PRs. PRs B (Caveat scoping) and C (`inlineStylesheets` decision) are unaffected and still shippable.
  - ✅ **B SHIPPED (`9cdc2ac1`)** — Caveat is now imported by `WorldsBeanstalk.astro` (its only consumer) instead of `BaseLayout`, so its `@font-face` rules ship on 1 page rather than 91; matches the existing per-page Fraunces pattern. Also deleted `--font-hand` from `guides/[...slug].astro`, which was declared, never referenced, and listed `'Caveat'` ahead of the name fontsource actually registers (`'Caveat Variable'`) so it would have fallen through to `cursive` anyway. No LCP effect, as predicted — this was a correctness fix.
  - ✅ **C SHIPPED as a comment-only correction (`529ca220`)** — the `astro.config.mjs` comment asserted a 1510ms saving as fact; measured result was 87ms (Lighthouse's render-blocking estimate assumes the bytes disappear, but inlining moves ~112KB of CSS into every page document instead). **The `'auto'` vs `'always'` decision is DEFERRED, not made** — that comparison needs a quiet runner, and consecutive runs of the identical commit gave TBT between 80ms and 1342ms. `content-visibility` skips rendering, not bytes, so the ~112KB inline CSS (and the lost cross-page caching on a 91-page site) is still on the table. Prefer `'auto'` if it holds LCP when re-measured.
  - 🔴 **BLOCKED — D (`push: [main]` Lighthouse trigger) must NOT land until the flakiness is resolved.** Runner contention is now the dominant failure mode, not page performance: across four consecutive dispatches on 2026-07-21 the same tree produced `total-blocking-time` of 80 / 436 / 465 / 1342ms and `categories.performance` of 0.81 / 0.61 / 0.60 / 0.85, on a page whose TBT measures 70–80ms on a quiet runner. LCP — the metric we actually fixed — has stopped appearing in the failures. **Next session's decision, in preference order:** (1) set `aggregationMethod: 'median'` explicitly AND raise `numberOfRuns` from 3 to 5, so one contended run cannot decide the gate (note the current implicit default is `optimistic`/best-of-3, so all historical numbers in this entry are best-case); (2) relax or `warn` the `total-blocking-time` assertion, which is by far the most CPU-contention-sensitive of the budgets; (3) accept Lighthouse as advisory-only on PRs and rely on the `web-vitals` → Plausible RUM already shipping from `BaseLayout` for the durable field signal. Do not simply raise the LCP budget — that metric is now healthy.
  - ⚠️ **CORRECTION — an earlier version of this entry misdiagnosed it** as a build failure (`unified is not a function` from astro's `coerceLegacyMarkdownPlugins`) and blamed a floating `node-version: '24'` pin. That was wrong and was written into this file before being checked. The `unified` error came from sampling a SINGLE Lighthouse run which happened to be PR #289 (astro 5→**7**, a two-major bump that legitimately breaks `astro check`) and generalising it to all PRs. Every other failing run — including a font-bump-only PR and a `workflow_dispatch` run on `main` itself — builds fine and fails on the perf assertions above. **Lesson: sample more than one run before generalising a CI failure, and check WHICH step failed.** The Node-pin hypothesis is withdrawn; nothing supports it.
  - **Why it still matters:** Lighthouse is `pull_request`-only, so `main` is never gated by it, and a permanently-red check trains reviewers to ignore the one signal guarding marketing-site performance.
  - ⚠️ **Open question on the fix:** removing render-blocking CSS makes the page paint sooner, which can trade LCP for **CLS**. Local runs of the fix show homepage CLS 0.109–0.159 against a 0.1 budget — but local numbers are unreliable here (perf swung 0.81–0.92 and LCP 1813–3161ms across three runs of identical code), and CLS was NOT failing in CI. Must be judged on CI numbers, not local.

### App Review demo mode — code-gated demo family, no Google sign-in (2026-08-20, session 2)

> 1 commit (`71da5def`), pushed to `main`. Not deployed to web (deliberately — see below). iOS TestFlight build uploaded green from run `32322420564`. Full suite 4563 passing, type-check clean, 0 lint errors in `src/`.

**The problem.** Store reviewers could not sign in with `beaniesdemo@gmail.com`. Google's risk engine challenges every sign-in from an unfamiliar device + IP + country, which is precisely what a reviewer VM looks like against a young, low-activity account. Disabling 2-Step Verification does not stop it and there is no consumer setting that does. Apple's own App Review Information guidance is to supply a demo mode that needs no third-party sign-in.

**What shipped.** An "App Review Access" button on the welcome screen, rendered only in a deliberately-armed, unexpired build. A correct code seeds a synthetic family in memory and lands on `/nook` — no OAuth, no Drive, no filesystem pod, no network call at all — with a persistent "demo family" banner. Armed only on the two mobile release lanes; a negative parity assertion keeps it off the web bundle permanently.

**Reuse over duplication** (the plan's DRY pass found five would-be duplications and shared them instead):

- `sha256` / `sha256Hex` extracted into `src/utils/encoding.ts`, and the normalize→hash→membership gate into new `src/utils/hashedCodeGate.ts` — now shared with the invite-token gate, which was carrying its own copy. Both **survive retirement**.
- The batch document seeder lifted out of the DEV-only E2E `dataBridge` into `src/services/automerge/seedDocument.ts`; the bridge now delegates. Also survives retirement.
- `withAnalyticsSuppressed()` added to `src/services/analytics/plausible.ts` — the module that already owns the `window.plausible` global, rather than monkey-patching it from a feature module.
- Teardown reuses `authStore.signOutAndClearData`, refresh reuses `syncStore.reloadAllStores`, the banner reuses `ErrorBanner`, and the failure surface reuses `showToast` (which already fires `reportError`).

**Correctness work worth remembering:**

- **A pre-existing session is refused, not merged.** `authStore.signUp` returns `{ success: true }` without doing anything when `currentUser` is set, so seeding on top of a live session would have written ~60 synthetic records into a **real family's Automerge document**. Now a non-destructive `session-exists` precondition that clears nothing.
- `createNewFile` gained ONE option (`suppressRemoteSideEffects`) skipping all **three** of its remote interactions — the pre-write registry lookup, the registry registration, and the pod-created Slack ping. A test pins the DEFAULT so an inverted flag can't silently unregister real families.
- The fixture is authored in **USD** to match `DEFAULT_CURRENCY`. A non-default base currency made the app fetch live exchange rates from a CDN, breaking the no-network guarantee.
- `isDemoSession` is `sessionStorage`-backed (a reload keeps the reviewer in the same pod, so the banner must survive) and cleared from `resetAllAppStores` (sign-out does `router.replace` with no reload, so a memory-only flag would leak the banner onto the next real pod).

**What the browser walkthrough caught that the unit tests could not.** Every unit test passed while the feature was still broken for a reviewer. Driving the real app surfaced three defects: the reviewer landed on the **first-run setup wizard** instead of the demo family (`buildOwnerDoc` sets `onboardingCompleted: false`; now cleared during the seed, verified afterwards because `settingsStore` swallows its own write errors); the seed **made a network call**; and the plan's assumption that a reload ends the session was **wrong**, which had left the banner missing while synthetic data stayed on screen. Worth generalising: for anything a human walks through, drive it end-to-end before calling it done.

**On the `src/utils/reviewDemo.ts` near-miss (recorded because the two sessions' accounts differ).** The first commit attempt staged the test and all four importers but not the module itself, so `main` would briefly have referenced a missing file; it was caught before pushing and fixed with `--amend`. The session-1 wrap attributes this to a concurrent `git reset` unstaging it. The direct evidence from this session points elsewhere: the explicit file list this session built and committed from (`printf`'d to the scratchpad before staging) **did not contain the path at all**, so `git add` never staged it and there was nothing for a reset to drop. Both things may have happened, but the omission alone fully explains the outcome. The broader lesson recorded in memory — don't touch the index while a concurrent session is mid-commit — stands on its own merits regardless. The narrower lesson for this session: when committing by explicit pathspec, diff the list against `git status` rather than trusting a hand-built array.

**Temporary by design.** Every shared-code touchpoint carries a `REVIEW-DEMO:` marker (21 files) and `docs/runbooks/native-store-submission.md` §6 carries the App Review Information text plus a step-by-step retirement checklist. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-08-20-app-review-demo-mode.md` (4-pass; the fresh-eyes pass is what caught the data-safety defect). Prompts: `docs/prompts/2026-08/2026-08-20-app-review-demo-mode.md`.

### Settings "Resume Setup" rewire + timezone test fix + blog copy edit (2026-05-16, evening session)

> 4 commits, 1 Vue prod deploy (`911f50a`). Continuation of the Shaun-in-HK pod-creation hardening thread from morning + a CI failure recovered along the way.

- **Settings "Create New Data File" → "Resume Setup"** (`f9fef9c`, Vue prod `911f50a`) — when a signed-in user reaches Settings → Family Data without a pod configured, the previous button called `syncStore.configureSyncFile` (a misnamed "save-as" path that assumed an in-memory pod already existed). Pre-pod it silently no-op'd — exactly the path Shaun hit. Replaced with "Resume Setup" that routes to `/welcome?resume=setup`, re-using the hardened `ResumePodSetup` flow (createNewFile with verification + structured CreatePodResult failures + `.corrupt-<ts>` rename). Also removed the now-zero-caller `configureSyncFile` from `syncStore` + dead test plumbing in `syncAutoSave.test.ts`. Single creation path, single error model. New `settings.resumeSetup` i18n key (en + beanie + zh); `settings.createOrLoadDataFile` subhead reworded to "Finish setting up your encrypted data file, or load an existing one." Net change: 5 files, 33 insertions, 55 deletions.
- **Timezone-dependent unit test fix** (`911f50a`) — pulling origin/main mid-session pulled in upstream commit `c381807 feat(todo): outlined-glow treatment` which failed CI on 3 unit tests (`todo.test.ts:42`, `todo.test.ts:73`, `TodoItemRow.test.ts:88`) — all asserted "overdue when dueTime is 10:00" but pinned `vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-05-16T07:00:00Z'))` and labeled it "15:00 SGT". That instant is 15:00 only east of UTC; on CI (Ubuntu, UTC) it's 07:00, which makes `07:00 < 10:00 local` and breaks the precedence assertion. Fix: `new Date(2026, 4, 16, 15, 0, 0)` (y, m, d, h) constructor pins 15:00 in the runner's LOCAL time, deterministic in any timezone. Verified with `TZ=UTC vitest run` locally.
- **UI strings — `nook.motto21` rewording** (`deb1e07`, greg's commit) — "First you get the beans, then you get the money, and then you get the women" → "In America, first you get the beans..." (Scarface reference made explicit). Merged into the deploy bundle.

In working-tree-wrap commit.
- **Reuse rule established for future Settings-data-file work** — the "Resume Setup" route is the one true path to a fresh pod from within an authenticated session. Anywhere a user lands at `!syncStore.isConfigured` (Settings, deep-link, weird back-button state), the recovery action is `/welcome?resume=setup`. Never re-introduce a Settings-side `configureSyncFile`-style shortcut.

### Chunk-load recovery saga — iOS Safari self-heal hardened end-to-end after the onboarding overhaul exposed every weak spot (2026-05-13, session 2)

Surfaced by greg testing the just-shipped Drive OAuth flow on his iPhone 14 Safari: after the Google consent screen, the **`Cannot destructure property 'registerGoogleAccountAssertion' from null or undefined value`** reload loop was back. Cleared Safari data, retried, still looping — sometimes 30 seconds, sometimes 4-5 minutes, eventually settling. No Slack alerts during any of the loops. Seven follow-up deploys diagnosed and fixed the recovery flow layer by layer:

- **`af1820f` — regex matches iOS Safari's destructure phrasing + `hardReload` unregisters the SW.** The previous regex (`/Cannot destructure property .+ as it is (?:null|undefined)/i`, shipped 2026-05-10 in `8491e76`) only matched V8/Chrome/Firefox's "as it is null" wording. iOS Safari emits `"Cannot destructure property X from null or undefined value"` — different preposition, no match → `isChunkLoadError` returned false → App.vue's init catch fell through to the error overlay instead of `hardReload`-ing. Broadened to `/Cannot destructure[^.]*\b(?:null|undefined)\b/i` (covers V8 + Safari + future variants, regression tests confirm it still rejects `"Cannot read properties of null"` / `"null is not an object (evaluating …)"`). `hardReload` now also `reg.unregister()`s the SW — `caches.delete(all)` alone doesn't break the precache intercept on iOS WebKit; unregistering removes the SW entirely so the next nav is a fresh network fetch. `main.ts` re-registers on the fresh load → offline support back within ~1s.
- **`2ec88eb` — `LoginPage.onMounted` waits for `authStore.isInitialized`.** Vue mounts children's `onMounted` BEFORE the parent's; LoginPage's `if (route.query.resume === 'setup' && authStore.isAuthenticated)` was racing App.vue's async `authStore.initializeAuth()` and getting the pre-init `false` → resume branch silently skipped → user landed on WelcomeGate while `app.onboardingZombieState` correctly fired.
- **`4b715b5` — setup-level reactive `watchEffect` on `route.query.resume`.** Even with the wait, a SECOND race remained: when a user refreshes `/welcome` bare (no query) in the zombie state, App.vue's `router.replace('/welcome?resume=setup')` lands AFTER LoginPage's `onMounted` already decided activeView. Added a `watchEffect` (auth-init + isAuthenticated + `?resume=setup`) that flips activeView the moment all three hold, plus an early-return in onMounted for the zombie state without `?resume=setup` (keeps spinner up, avoids running family-init on a pod that doesn't exist).
- **`3bcbec8` — the real root cause was CloudFront + S3, not the client.** Diagnosed: `deploy.yml` did `aws s3 sync dist/ ... --delete` (removing old chunks immediately) AND `infrastructure/modules/app-subdomain/main.tf` has `default_ttl=86400` (24h cache on index.html). After every deploy: 1-15 min window where CDN edges serve the OLD `index.html` referencing chunks that `--delete` just wiped → 404 → loop. `hardReload`'s SW unregister couldn't help — browser STILL fetches index.html from CloudFront. Fix: drop `--delete` (old chunks survive the cache-stale window) + re-upload `index.html` with `Cache-Control: no-cache, max-age=0, must-revalidate` so CDN always revalidates. Same commit moved `setOnboardingCompleted(false)` into `buildOwnerDoc` (so the resume path restores the money-wizard flag too — was being silently skipped), and persisted `displayName` on `AuthUser` so the resume screen pre-fills the actual typed name.
- **`e091b47` — REVERTED.** Tried workbox `skipWaiting: true + clientsClaim: true` to close the in-session deploy-gap window. vite-plugin-pwa's docs warn against pairing them with `registerType:'prompt'` (the new SW seizes the current page mid-precache-install → asset-fetch race → null modules), and it made greg's recovery worse (4-5 min loop). Reverted in `f9db1c2`. `cleanupOutdatedCaches:true` (added in same commit, separate concern) kept.
- **`f9db1c2` — bounded retry counter + revert.** Replaced the broken once-guard logic (`router.afterEach` was clearing `CHUNK_RELOAD_FLAG` on EVERY successful nav, including the initial nav that resolves before App.vue's onMounted error throws — so every load was "first attempt", silent hardReloads ran forever, `app.chunkRecoveryFailed` never fired). Now a counter (max 3 silent hardReloads), cleared only after App.vue's post-init health check confirms a successful boot. Reverted skipWaiting/clientsClaim.
- **`d86e797` — closed the last counter leak.** `main.ts`'s `vite:preloadError` handler was still using the old `=== '1'` / `set '1'` boolean logic — actively RESET the counter back to `'1'` every time it fired. With the dynamic-import rejection also routing through App.vue's catch (which increments), the counter cycled `1 → 2 → reset to 1 → 2 → ...` indefinitely, never reached `3`, never escalated. Now matches the App.vue / `router.onError` increment-or-return logic. All three callsites share the counter monotonically; attempt 4 trips the "exhausted" branch (overlay + Slack alert + tappable buttons).

**Verified live on greg's iPhone 14 Safari (iOS 18.7) end-to-end after `d86e797`**: Drive consent → return → 1-2 silent recovery iterations → `<ResumePodSetup>` with the typed name pre-filled → password → finalize → `/nook` → onboarding wizard appears. Single `app.onboardingZombieState` alert per resume round-trip (expected — the safety net). Zero `app.chunkRecoveryFailed` in steady state. The `🫘 New family pod started!` and `🎉 Family pod created!` pings both fire reliably for every storage type.

**Telemetry watches** (in Pending below): `app.chunkRecoveryFailed` (silent in steady state; if it fires for any device class, the layered fix isn't enough for them). `app.onboardingZombieState` (per resume round-trip = fine; same family stuck for hours = nudge them).

### Onboarding hardening — iPhone Drive 400 fix + "logged in but no pod" zombie state killed + every onboarding error pages Slack (2026-05-13)

Triggered by Shaun (HK, iPhone/Chrome-on-iOS, browser — not a PWA): a Google generic 400 mid-Drive-connect during pod creation, then dumped into an empty `/nook` with no `.beanpod`, nothing in `#beanies-errors`. **Shipped to prod `a27cebd` + e2e seed-helper fix `fcdeb64` (deploy.yml runs `25780014229` + `25785600277` respectively, both green); verified end-to-end on greg's iPhone 14 Safari**. Full design: `docs/adr/026-ios-redirect-oauth.md` and `docs/plans/2026-05-13-onboarding-iphone-drive-hardening.md`. Highlights:

- **`shouldUseRedirectAuth()` now true for all iOS/iPadOS WebKit** (UA `iP(hone|od|ad)` or `MacIntel`+touch), not just standalone PWAs — popups/new-tabs on iOS don't reliably postMessage back and the OAuth continuation trips ITP cookie partitioning (the 400). New shared `src/services/sync/connectStorage.ts` (`connectDriveStorage`/`connectLocalStorage`) owns the popup-vs-redirect decision + a `withTimeout` wrap; `CreatePodView` rewired onto it. `waitForAuthCode()` got a 120 s timeout via the new `src/utils/timing.ts:withTimeout` (which also replaced App.vue's ad-hoc `completeRedirectAuth` race).
- **`authStore.podCreated`** (persisted `beanies_pod_created`: `'1'`=pod exists, `'0'`=pending, absent=migration-true) is the durable invariant — `signUp` sets `'0'`, `syncStore.createNewFile` flips `'1'`. Router guard + `App.vue` require `isAuthenticated && podCreated` for `requiresAuth` routes; otherwise → `/welcome?resume=setup` (reports `app.onboardingZombieState`).
- **New `ResumePodSetup.vue`** (reached via `?resume=setup` in `LoginPage`): re-enter owner name+password → `authStore.rehydrateOwnerDoc()` (rebuilds the in-memory doc the redirect destroyed; needed `automergeRepository.createWithId` → `familyMemberRepository.createFamilyMemberWithId` → `familyStore.createMemberWithId`) → finish on the Drive token in hand (or pick Drive/local) → `createNewFile` → `/nook`. "Start over instead" = sign out. **No secrets stashed across the redirect** — password re-entered; token survives in `googleAuth.ts` in-memory state.
- **`🎉 Family pod created!` moved into `syncStore.createNewFile()` on success** — fires for every storage type incl. local (the reported gap) and on the resume path. **Error reporting closed**: `app.redirectAuthCompletion`, `app.postInitNoData`, `app.onboardingZombieState`, `createPod.connectDrive`/`selectLocalFile`/`createNewFile` (error severity unless a genuine cancellation), `resumeSetup.*`. Drive-failure modal now: Try again / Use a local file instead (not just OK). `features.ts` warns loudly in prod builds if `errorReporter` is off while a cloud feature is on. `handleStep2Next`'s `else`-branch now blocks (was: advanced to step 3 with no pod file). `SetupProgressModal` "Continue Anyway" → "Continue" with honest copy (the pod already exists by then; only a background step failed).
- **Out of scope / follow-up**: "Move to Google Drive" migration of an _existing_ pod on iOS (needs the same redirect+re-auth-with-family-key dance) — the Settings → Family Data "Move to Google Drive" row is hidden on iOS/PWAs until then. Also re-validate the Google Picker (load-existing-pod) on iOS under redirect-auth; if it breaks, swap for an in-app `files.list` `.beanpod` chooser on iOS.
- **`BEANIES_ERROR_WEBHOOK_URL` repo variable verified set** — multiple alert categories fired live during 2026-05-13 (`app.onboardingZombieState`, `app.chunkRecoveryFailed`, `🫘 pod started`, `🎉 pod created`), confirming the webhook is wired and the integration is working end-to-end.

### "Someday · Maybe" to-dos — a third lane for the To-Do system (2026-05-12)

> Shipped to prod 2026-05-12 — commits `e5bba2e` (feature) + `b0f5d7e` (Sky-Silk gradient styling), in the `d4cb51c` deploy. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-05-12-someday-maybe-todos.md`.

- **Why** — the To-Do system only had two lanes (open / completed) and every open item, dated or not, was treated as a real commitment (shown in the active list, the planner sidebar, the Nook To-Do widget, the critical-activities briefing). No place for GTD-style "someday / maybe" ideas you'd _like_ to get to but aren't scheduling. This adds an **active / someday · maybe / completed** model behind one optional flag.
- **Data** — `TodoItem.someday?: boolean` (`src/types/models.ts`); optional → no migration; a someday item is, by definition, unscheduled (`setSomeday(id, true)` clears `dueDate`/`dueTime`).
- **`todoStore`** — extracted module-level `byCreatedDesc` / `byCompletedDesc` comparators (used everywhere — _less_ duplication than before); **renamed** `openTodos` → `activeTodos` and `filteredOpenTodos` → `filteredActiveTodos` (now `!completed && !someday`) rather than adding parallel getters (net +2 getters, no dead code; the rename is type-check-safe — a missed consumer is a compile error); added `somedayTodos` / `filteredSomedayTodos`; re-pointed `scheduledTodos` / `undatedTodos` (and the filtered variants) off the active set so they never see someday items; added `setSomeday(id, someday): Promise<TodoItem | null>` = `someday ? updateTodo(id, { someday: true, dueDate: undefined, dueTime: undefined }) : updateTodo(id, { someday: false })` — reuses `updateTodo`'s `wrapAsync` (toast + Slack telemetry on failure; not a silent path; `undefined` keys are `delete`d by `automergeRepository.update()`).
- **`<TodoSection>`** (`src/components/todo/TodoSection.vue`, new) — one renderer for all three To-Do page sections (Open / Someday / Completed): `label`/`emoji`/`labelClass`/`todos`/`collapsible`/`collapsed`(v-model) props, a `#hint` slot, re-emits `toggle`/`view`/`edit`/`delete`/`set-someday`, calls `useSyncHighlight()` internally. A faithful lift of the existing markup — the Open empty-state, the Completed collapse toggle, and the per-row sync highlight are unchanged.
- **`FamilyTodoPage`** — extracted `withMemberFilterAndSort(items)` (page-local member filter + `applySorting`, shared by the Open + Someday lists; the Completed list keeps its own filter that also matches `completedBy`); `displayedOpenTodos` off `filteredActiveTodos`, new `displayedSomedayTodos` off `filteredSomedayTodos`; the three section `<div>`s replaced by three `<TodoSection>`s; `completedCollapsed` ref (was `showCompletedSection`); `handleSetSomeday` → `todoStore.setSomeday`. The "💭 Someday · Maybe" section sits between Open and Completed, **always visible** (not collapsible), with a hint line, hidden only when empty.
- **`TodoItemRow` / `TodoItemCard`** — `isSomeday` computed (reads `todo.someday` directly, no new prop); container styling moved out of the nested `:class` ternary into a `containerClass` computed with early returns (someday → a soft Sky-Silk "daydream" gradient — `bg-gradient-to-br from-[var(--tint-silk-10)] to-[var(--tint-silk-20)]`, brightens to `silk-20→silk-30` on hover — plus a `--tint-silk-20` border: kept light enough to read as quieter than (never louder than) an active white row, but still bright and fully clickable, _not_ the greyed "disabled/done" look; never the overdue-red path since someday items have no date; overdue → red; compact → …; default → white); `checkboxClass` computed (Sky-Silk-300 border on someday); `actionPillStyle` computed so the ✏️/🗑️/💭 hover-pill picks up the silk tint on a someday row; 💭 prefix on the title; the "no date set" filler hidden for someday rows; a new hover-revealed action button (same `h-8 w-8 rounded-[10px]` styling as ✏️/🗑️) — "Move to Someday" 💭 on an active row, "Make active" 📋 on a someday row, `@click.stop="emit('set-someday', todo.id, !isSomeday)"`; `TodoItemCard` re-emits `set-someday`. Flow: row → card → section → page → `todoStore.setSomeday` (same shape as `toggle`/`edit`/`delete`). New `--tint-silk-30` tint token added to `src/style.css` (light 30% / dark 22%, extending the existing `--tint-silk-10`/`-20` scale; used by the someday-row hover state); the `FamilyTodoPage` "💭 Someday · Maybe" section header switched from `--color-text-muted` grey to a readable `text-sky-600 dark:text-sky-400` (matching the purple/green convention of the Open/Completed headers). _(Iterated on greg's feedback: the original ship was a flat grey + dashed-border "parked" look that read as disabled/done → moved to a Sky-Silk wash → added a daydream gradient + deepened it → dialled the gradient back so a someday row never out-pops an active one.)_
- **`TodoViewEditModal`** — a `FrequencyChips` "Track as" 📋 To-do / 💭 Someday · Maybe toggle (reused the existing generic chip control — no new component) before the status badge, `@update:model-value` → `todoStore.setSomeday`; the status badge is now a flat 3-branch `v-if`/`v-else-if`/`v-else` (completed green / someday Sky-Silk "💭 Someday · Maybe" — `text-sky-700 dark:text-sky-300` on `var(--tint-silk-20)` / open purple); the due-date `FormFieldGroup` is `v-if="!todo.someday"` and the due-time group `v-if="!todo.someday && (todo.dueDate || editingField === 'dueDate')"`.
- **"Committed" surfaces** now read `activeTodos` / `filteredActiveTodos` so someday items drop out: `NookTodoWidget`, `TodoPreview`, `ScheduleCards`, `useCriticalItems`, plus `FamilyStatusToast` / `FilterBar` (and the planner calendar views already key off `filteredScheduledTodos`, which is now someday-excluding). `GlobalSearch` (searches all `todos`) and `RecentActivityCard` (completed-only) unchanged.
- **i18n** — 6 new `uiStrings` keys (`todo.someday`, `todo.somedayHint`, `todo.kind`, `todo.kind.todo`, `todo.moveToSomeday`, `todo.makeActive`); `npm run translate` synced `public/translations/zh.json`.
- **Tests** — `src/stores/__tests__/todoStore.test.ts` (new — the store had no prior coverage): the three-lane partition (active / someday / completed; someday excluded from `scheduled`/`undated`/`active`), `setSomeday(true)` calls `updateTodo` with `{ someday: true, dueDate: undefined, dueTime: undefined }`, `setSomeday(false)` with `{ someday: false }`, `toggleComplete` keeps the `someday` flag. `src/components/todo/__tests__/TodoItemRow.test.ts` (new): the active-vs-someday row variants (💭 marker, Sky-Silk daydream gradient wash, no "no date" filler) + the hover button emits `set-someday` with `[id, !isSomeday]`. `npm run validate` green (type-check / lint / format:check / test:run / build); no new E2E (ADR-007 cap).
- **Help Center** — new "Someday · Maybe to-dos" section in the existing **Family To-Do Lists** article (`src/content/help/features.ts`): what it's for, the two ways to mark it (the **Track as** toggle / the **💭** hover button), where someday items show vs. don't, that marking clears the due date, completing/reopening preserves the flag; `readTime` 4→5, `updatedDate` 2026-05-12.
- **Not done** (CLI can't drive a browser): manual smoke of the toggle/move/complete flows + a beanie-mode/zh casing check. Flagged in Pending.

### Storage Provider Migration — move pod between local file and Google Drive (2026-05-12)

- **`3a457e4`** — added `syncStore.migrateStorage(target)` + `isMigratingStorage` ref. Owner-only (the UI action row is `v-if="isOwner"`; the store's own guard rails are `isConfigured` + a non-null `from` + `target !== from`). Returns a discriminated `MigrateStorageResult` (`{outcome:'success',dest}` / `{outcome:'cancelled'}` / `{outcome:'failed',reason}` / `{outcome:'recovery-needed',reason}`); the component renders the toasts (i18n stays in the component layer, the store stays unit-test-friendly). Flow: re-entrancy guard → flush the source one last time (non-forced `syncNow()` so a real cross-device conflict surfaces instead of getting clobbered) → `buildProviderForTarget(target)` (`LocalStorageProvider.fromSavePicker` for local, `GoogleDriveProvider.createNew(name, {forceConsent:false})` for Drive; returns `null` on user-cancel, classified via `isUserCancellation`) → capture the previous provider → `installProvider(newProvider, target)` → on failure, `restorePreviousProvider(previous, from)` re-installs the old one; if that fails too → `recovery-needed`. The encrypted bytes never change (same family key, same envelope, no password prompt); the source file is left intact (we never delete it — recommend keeping it as a backup until the move is confirmed). Telemetry: `reportError({surface:'storage-migration-ok', severity:'warning', context:{from,to}})` on success; `{surface:'storage-migration-failed', severity:'error', context:{from,to,step}}` on failure with `step` ∈ `pre-swap`/`install`/`rollback`; structured `console.error` alongside.
- **DRY refactor** — extracted the duplicated 6-step "make this provider the active one" sequence out of `configureSyncFile` + `configureSyncFileGoogleDrive` into a shared private `installProvider(provider, type)` (`needsPermission=false` → `provider.persist(familyId)` → `syncService.setProvider` → `syncNow()` _throws if it returns false_ → `settingsRepo.saveSettings` (the syncNow+saveSettings pair wrapped in `isReloading=true…finally false` to keep the file-poll reload check from racing) → `registerCurrentFamily` → `setupTokenExpiryHandler()` for Drive else `setupAutoSync()`). `configureSyncFile` is now `selectSyncFile() → installProvider(getProvider()!, 'local')` (the re-`persist`/`setProvider` is idempotent; `selectSyncFile` kept untouched since `CreatePodView` also calls it); `configureSyncFileGoogleDrive` is `createNew(name) → installProvider(p, 'google_drive')`. Side benefit: `configureSyncFile`'s old bare `await syncNow()` (return value ignored) is now a thrown error — closes a silent-failure path.
- **`isUserCancellation(e)`** extracted into `googleAuth.ts` (matches `AbortError` by `.name` + `/cancel|dismiss|popup_closed|user_cancel/i` on the message); `handleSwitchGoogleAccount` in `SettingsPage.vue` rewired onto it (dropped its inline copy of the regex).
- **`GoogleDriveProvider.createNew(fileName, opts: { forceConsent?: boolean } = {})`** — `forceConsent` defaults `true`; only the migration's Drive path passes `false`. Why it matters: `prompt=consent` forces the redirect-auth path on a standalone PWA _even when a token is cached_, so the post-redirect retry of a local→Drive move would redirect again, looping. With `forceConsent:false` the retry reuses the cached token and completes. The earlier-drafted standalone pre-flight `requestAccessToken()` was dropped during implementation in favour of this — one fewer cancellation site, since `buildProviderForTarget`'s try/catch already handles a cancelled `createNew`.
- **UI** — owner-gated "Move to Google Drive" / "Move to a local file" action row in the Family Data modal (`SettingsPage.vue`), between the "Load another data file" row and the error display; `useConfirm` with `variant:'info'` (Heritage Orange — routine, not destructive); `handleMigrateStorage` does the `confirm()` then switches on the result, with the error toasts passed `{silent:true}` (the store already `reportError`s the failure with full `{from,to,step}` context — letting the toast auto-report too would double-ping).
- **i18n** — 18 new `uiStrings` keys under `settings.familyData.migrate.*` (move labels + descs, confirm titles/bodies for each direction, confirm action, cancelled/success/failed/recovery-needed titles+bodies) plus `action.move`; `npm run translate` synced Chinese cleanly.
- **Help Center** (per the updated `/beanies-plan` skill, which now folds Help coverage into plans) — new how-to article `moving-your-pod-storage` in `src/content/help/getting-started.ts` (why you'd move; owner-only; old file stays as a backup; other devices must re-load from the new location; no password prompt; what to do if it says "sign out and back in to recover"); cross-reference paragraph + `updatedDate` bump on `connecting-google-drive`; `beanies-help-docs` SKILL.md inventory bumped 4→6 (also adds the previously-missing `install-as-app`).
- **`/beanies-plan` skill update** — defaults to direct implementation (no GitHub issue unless explicitly requested — one-dev project); Phase 2 gains a Help Center coverage assessment with concrete yes/no rules; the plan template gains a `## Help Center Coverage` section; Rules updated to match.
- **Tests** — new `src/stores/__tests__/syncStore.migrate.test.ts` (10 tests: local→Drive happy path, Drive→local happy path, save-picker cancel, Google-chooser cancel, pre-swap flush failure, install-failure-with-rollback, rollback-failure→recovery-needed, guard rails + re-entrancy, plus two `configureSyncFileGoogleDrive` tests exercising the shared `installProvider`). `isUserCancellation` cases added to `googleAuth.test.ts`. 2123→2136 unit tests passing; type-check + lint + build + translate clean. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-05-12-storage-provider-migration.md`.

### Share-channel "couldn't open" false-positive fix (2026-05-11, session 2)

- **`d5ddc46`** — `ShareChannelGrid.handleChannel` did `const opened = window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener'); if (opened === null) throw 'popup blocker'` — but `window.open` with the `noopener` feature returns `null` by spec even on success, so the error toast fired on _every_ share-channel tap (WhatsApp/Telegram/SMS/Messenger/Email) despite the link being handed off correctly — landing in the first-run onboarding invite step. Dropped the bogus check: `https:` channels open in a new tab, `mailto:`/`sms:`/`fb-messenger://` navigate via `window.location.href`, and the remaining `try/catch` (a genuine `window.open` throw) now shows a `{ silent: true }` toast so it no longer pages `#beanies-errors`. Added `src/components/family/__tests__/ShareChannelGrid.test.ts` (4 tests — component had no prior coverage). Found via `/error-review` of a Slack alert from the Ritterbusch family on desktop Edge. Deployed to prod (`gh run 25670810417`).

### Photo Attachments — Foundation Shipped (2026-04-19)

General-purpose reusable capability for attaching photos to any beanies entity. Delivers the plumbing only; integration into activities, family avatars, and other entities happens in follow-up plans. See `docs/plans/2026-04-18-photos-general-capability.md` and [ADR-021](adr/021-photo-storage.md).

- **Storage model:** photo bytes in the user's Google Drive inside the shared `beanies.family` app folder; only metadata in Automerge (new `photos: Record<UUID, PhotoAttachment>` collection). Not encrypted — matches the existing trust the user already places in Drive for every other file.
- **Multi-member access:** invite flow now shares the app folder alongside `.beanpod`. One-time migration sweep back-fills folder shares for existing families when `syncStore.driveFileId` becomes available.
- **Rendering:** Drive's native `thumbnailLink?sz=w{N}` CDN serves both thumbnails (`=s400`) and full-size (`=s2048`) directly as `<img src>`. No IndexedDB full-size cache; no client-side thumbnail generation.
- **Offline:** IndexedDB `beanies-photo-queue-{familyId}` queues compressed uploads; drains on the `online` event; cleared on sign-out alongside the Automerge cache.
- **Missing-photo UX:** 404/403 from Drive flips a runtime `unresolved` flag; thumbnail shows a broken-image tile; viewer surfaces Replace (swap `driveFileId`, keep UUID stable so entity references survive) / Remove (tombstone) actions.
- **Deletion:** tombstones + 24h-grace GC sweep. Zero-reference cascade gated on integration plans registering their collection via `registerPhotoCollection(name)` so the foundation doesn't auto-delete photos before any entity points to them.
- **DRY refactors shipped alongside:** `driveService.createFile` generalized to accept `string | Blob | Uint8Array` with optional mime (default preserves existing `.beanpod` behavior); drag-drop extracted from `JoinPodView.vue` into a reusable `useFileDrop` composable; `useFilePicker` composable wraps the `<input type="file">` pattern; new `DriveFileNotFoundError` subclass cleanly distinguishes 404/403 from other Drive errors.
- **New modules:** `src/services/photos/photoCompression.ts`, `src/services/sync/photoUploadQueue.ts`, `src/stores/photoStore.ts`, `src/composables/{useFileDrop,useFilePicker,usePhotos}.ts`, `src/components/media/{PhotoThumbnail,PhotoViewer,PhotoAttachments}.vue`.
- **Tests:** 74 new unit tests (compression, queue, store, composables) — all 1060 existing + new tests green.

**Family Scrapbook redesign — `/pod/scrapbook` becomes a tabbed scrapbook of spreads:**

- Old: flat 3-column CSS-columns masonry of mixed favorites + sayings + notes across the whole family, with chip filters and Load More pagination.
- New: a horizontal `<ScrapbookSpine>` strip at the top pages between an **Everyone** overview and each bean's individual magazine-style spread. Page-flip transition between spreads (3D rotateY pivot — leaves on left edge, enters from right for forward; mirrored for backward; ~530ms total; opacity fade under `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- `<ScrapbookEntryCard>` is the single source for `entry.type` → renderer dispatch (saying → `<StickyNote>`; favorite → kraft card with category emoji; milestone → taped kraft card with `<MilestoneThumb>` OR polaroid hero when `:emphasize-photo` and photos exist; note → ripped paper card; unknown → reports once-per-session via `reportError`, renders nothing).
- `<EveryoneSpread>` cover layout: family-name inscription header (Caveat) → "What's happening lately" hero block (most recent moment, photo-emphasized as polaroid when available, supporting cluster of next 4 items densely packed via `grid-auto-flow: dense` with photo cards spanning 2x2 cells) → per-bean clusters (each bean with items gets a header link + avatar polaroid + their 4 most recent items) → "Family moments" footer (family-wide milestones with `memberId: null`).
- `<BeanSpread>` per-bean magazine layout: bean header band → optional polaroid hero from `avatarPhotoId` → sectioned spread driven by a single `SECTIONS` config array (sayings cap 4, favorites 6, milestones 4, notes 3) with "see all →" links into the bean's pod tab.
- **Pets are first-class** in the spine and per-bean clusters (uses `familyStore.sortedMembers`, not `sortedHumans`). Clicking a pet's avatar opens their personal spread.
- Decoration is CSS-only, no images: `.scrapbook-paper` (kraft warm-cream + radial Heritage-Orange/Sky-Silk wash + inline-SVG fractalNoise overlay), `.scrap-taped` (white kraft card + colored tape strip pseudo-element), `.scrap-ripped` (kraft card with subtle torn-edge feel), `.scrap-washi` (small colored rectangle at slight rotation with frayed-end pseudo-elements). All four are self-contained re positioning so parents don't fight them.
- Stable per-id rotations (–2.5° to +2.5°, hashed from entry.id) so cards never reshuffle when new entries arrive at the top of the feed.
- Activeguard `watch` on `familyStore.sortedMembers` — if the active bean is removed mid-spread (delete / family change), bounces back to Everyone with a backward page-turn animation.

**Caveat font cascade-layer fix:**

- Discovered during visual review that "Our family scrapbook" `<h2>` was rendering as Outfit despite using `font-caveat`. Three-layer diagnosis: (1) Google Fonts URL only loaded Caveat at weights 500+700 — added `400` to the `Caveat:wght@` segment in `index.html`. (2) Even with the URL fix, the title still rendered Outfit because `src/style.css:421-425` had a global `h1, h2, h3 { font-family: Outfit, sans-serif }` rule **outside** any `@layer`. In CSS cascade-layer ordering, unlayered styles beat layered styles regardless of selector specificity, so the unlayered element rule won over Tailwind v4's `@layer utilities` `.font-caveat { ... }`. Wrapped the heading rule in `@layer base { ... }` so utility classes can override per element. (3) Defense-in-depth: added explicit `font-medium` on title h2, family-name subtitle, page-header subtitle, and bean-polaroid caption — weight 500 was already loaded so renders correctly even on PWA-cached old assets.

### WebKit Overlay Fixes & E2E Hardening (2026-04-13)

- **Onboarding overlay stuck on Safari/iOS (#153)**: Vue's `<Transition>` inside `<Teleport>` was stalling the leave transition on WebKit, leaving an invisible click-blocking overlay on top of the app after onboarding completion. Replaced the outer fade `<Transition>` with a deterministic class toggle (`ob-overlay-hidden`) + `setTimeout`-driven unmount. Visual behaviour identical, no Vue-transition dependency. Inner step `<Transition>` untouched (never the issue).
- **Global E2E reduced-motion**: `playwright.config.ts` now sets `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` on the shared `use` block. `src/style.css` extends the `prefers-reduced-motion` block with a universal `*, *::before, *::after { animation-iteration-count: 1; animation-duration: 0.01ms }` rule that disables all infinite keyframe animations at once — resolved WebKit "waiting for element to be stable" stalls caused by HomePage decorative float animations. Real users with the accessibility preference also benefit.
- **App loading overlay defused**: The init spinner in `App.vue` (`z-[300]` full-screen div in a `<Transition>`) was getting stuck at `opacity: 0` on WebKit and blocking all clicks. Added `pointer-events-none` — the overlay only holds a spinner, nothing clickable, so this is always the correct behaviour.
- **E2E workflow consolidation**: Deleted the duplicate `e2e-tests` job from `main-ci.yml`. `e2e.yml` is now the single source of truth, with an event-aware matrix: push to `main` → Chromium only (temporarily, pending #155), `run-e2e` PR label → Chromium + WebKit on demand, weekly → full 3-browser sweep. Playwright browser cache added.
- **Follow-up #155** tracks 10 remaining WebKit-only timeouts (Account Institution combobox, planner recurring flows, financial data dashboard) — unrelated to overlays; look like CI perf / timing or genuine WebKit-specific app behaviour. Chromium + Firefox still green.

### WebKit E2E Restored to Main-Push CI (2026-04-13 — later)

- **#155 resolved (PR #156)**: reduced-motion rule now zeroes out `transition-duration` globally (not just `animation-*`), so Vue modal/drawer enter transitions no longer keep dialog buttons "unstable" on webkit. Page-object `goto()` uses `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` to fix the `/transactions` navigation hang on webkit's `load` event. Webkit Playwright project gets its own 40s test timeout for headroom.
- **Webkit flakiness hardened (PR #165)**: a duplicate parallel PR run exposed residual flakiness on identical SHAs — webkit timeout raised to 60s and webkit retries to 2 (CI only) to absorb transient "WebKit encountered an internal error" crashes on page.goto. Also hardened `google-drive.spec.ts` "Create Pod step 2" with an explicit `waitFor` before the Create click — previously raced the WelcomeGate → CreatePodView transition.
- **CI cleanup (PR #166)**: (a) duplicate E2E runs fixed — `e2e.yml` now gates on `github.event.label.name == 'run-e2e'` so only the actual `run-e2e` label add triggers a run (previously every label added to a PR with `run-e2e` fired another run on the same SHA). (b) Webkit is back on every main-push alongside chromium — Safari/iOS is a large share of our users. ADR-007 updated.
- **Current matrix**: PR (opt-in `run-e2e`) → chromium + webkit; push to main → chromium + webkit; weekly schedule → chromium + firefox + webkit.
- **ADR-007 updated** to reflect the new browser-coverage policy.

- **Suite reduction**: 87 → 21 tests (76%), 15 → 7 spec files (53%)

- **Three-Gate Filter**: Every E2E test must pass business-critical outcome, full-stack integration, and deterministic gates

### Multi-Family Architecture (Stage 1)

- Per-family database architecture: each family gets its own IndexedDB (`beanies-data-{familyId}`)
- Registry database (`beanies-registry`): stores families, user mappings, global settings
- Family context orchestrator (`familyContext.ts`) and Pinia store (`familyContextStore.ts`)
- Legacy migration service: auto-migrates single-DB data to per-family DB on first boot
- Global settings split from per-family settings (theme, language, exchange rates are device-level)
- Sync file format v2.0: includes `familyId` and `familyName` (backward-compatible with v1.0)
- Per-family file handle storage for sync
- New types: `Family`, `UserFamilyMapping`, `GlobalSettings`
- All existing repositories work unchanged (transparent multi-tenancy via `getDatabase()`)
- E2E test helpers updated for dynamic per-family DB discovery

### File-Based Authentication (replacing Cognito)

- **Password service** (`src/services/auth/passwordService.ts`): PBKDF2 hashing (100k iterations, SHA-256, 16-byte salt, 32-byte hash) with constant-time verification
- **Auth store** (`src/stores/authStore.ts`): complete rewrite — signIn (member picker + password), signUp (owner creates pod), setPassword (joiner onboarding), signOut
- **Login flow**: WelcomeGate → LoadPodView (file picker + decrypt modal) → PickBeanView (member picker + password) / CreatePodView (3-step wizard) / JoinPodView (family code entry)
- **Data model**: `passwordHash` and `requiresPassword` fields on `FamilyMember`
- Route guards: all app routes have `requiresAuth: true`, login route exempt
- App.vue bootstrap simplified: global settings → auth init → family resolution → data load
- ADR-014 (file-based auth decision), supersedes ADR-010 and ADR-013

### Passkey / Biometric Authentication (Issue #16)

- `passkeyCrypto.ts`: PRF helpers, HKDF key derivation, AES-KW DEK wrapping/unwrapping
- `passkeyService.ts`: Full WebAuthn registration + assertion with PRF and non-PRF paths
- `passkeyRepository.ts`: IndexedDB CRUD for passkey registrations (registry DB v3)
- Dual-path strategy: PRF (true passwordless) + cached password fallback (Firefox)
- `BiometricLoginView.vue`: One-tap biometric login on returning devices
- `PasskeyPromptModal.vue`: Post-sign-in prompt to enable biometric login
- `PasskeySettings.vue`: Full management UI (register, list, remove passkeys)
- Password change invalidates PRF-wrapped DEKs, updates cached passwords
- ADR-015 documents the architectural decision
- `PasskeySettings.vue` component: lists registered passkeys, register new, remove existing
- Requires server-side challenge generation for full flow (deferred)

### Cognito Removal

- Deleted: `src/config/cognito.ts`, `src/services/auth/cognitoService.ts`, `src/services/auth/tokenManager.ts`, `src/services/auth/index.ts`, `src/services/api/adminApi.ts`
- Deleted: `src/pages/MagicLinkCallbackPage.vue`, `src/components/login/VerificationCodeForm.vue`, `src/components/family/CreateMemberAccountModal.vue`
- Deleted: `infrastructure/modules/auth/` (Cognito User Pool), `infrastructure/modules/api/` (Lambda + API Gateway), `infrastructure/scripts/cognito-sync-check.sh`
- Removed `amazon-cognito-identity-js` package (~165KB bundle reduction)
- Removed `cachedSessions` object store from registry database (v1 → v2 migration)
- Removed `CachedAuthSession` type, `isLocalOnly` from `UserFamilyMapping`, `isLocalOnlyMode` from `GlobalSettings`
- Removed Cognito env vars from `.env.example`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `vite.config.ts`

### File-First Architecture

- Encrypted data file is the source of truth; IndexedDB is a temporary cache deleted on sign-out
- Sign-out cleanup: `deleteFamilyDatabase()`, `resetState()` on all data stores, file handle preserved
- App startup always loads from data file when configured; IndexedDB fallback only when file permission not yet granted
- Auto-sync always on when file is configured (no toggle)
- Setup wizard adds Step 3 "Secure Your Data": requires file creation with encryption password
- Default `encryptionEnabled` changed to `true`
- Settings renamed "File Sync" → "Family Data Options"; removed Sync Now, Disconnect, Auto-sync toggle
- Encryption toggle warns before disabling
- SyncStatusIndicator: "Syncing..." → "Saving...", "Synced to..." → "Data saved to..."
- Login page: three security benefit bullet points (encrypted file, no server storage, cloud backup via folder)
- ADR-011: file-first architecture decision record

### Encryption Pipeline Security Hardening (Issue #84) — Closed

- **Critical security fix**: 7 bugs in the sync pipeline could cause encrypted `.beanpod` files to be silently written in plaintext
- **`syncService.ts`**: Added `setEncryptionRequiredCallback()` — `triggerDebouncedSave()`, `flushPendingSave()`, and `save()` now refuse to write when encryption is required but no password is available (defense-in-depth)
- **`syncStore.ts`**: Removed hardcoded `encryptionEnabled: false` from `loadFromFile()`, `loadFromNewFile()`, and `disconnect()` — encryption setting now persists correctly across file operations
- **`syncStore.ts`**: `requestPermission()` no longer arms auto-sync before password is available; `decryptPendingFile()` sets password and encryption flag before reloading stores, then arms auto-sync
- **`MobileHamburgerMenu.vue`**: Fixed sign-out order — `signOut()` now flushes pending saves before `resetAllStores()` clears the session password (matching AppHeader pattern)
- **`fileSync.ts`**: `exportToFile()` now respects encryption settings; `importSyncFileData()` preserves local `encryptionEnabled` value instead of importing from file

### Cross-Device Sync (Issue #103) — Closed

- **`syncStore.ts` — `reloadIfFileChanged()`**: Lightweight `getFileTimestamp()` check, full reload only when file is newer. Handles encrypted files via session password → session DEK → cached password fallback chain
- **`syncStore.ts` — `startFilePolling()` / `stopFilePolling()`**: 10-second interval polling for external file changes, auto-started by `setupAutoSync()`, stopped on sign-out/disconnect
- **`App.vue` — visibility change handling**: `reloadIfFileChanged()` on tab/app resume; `syncStore.syncNow(true)` force save on `hidden` to prevent data loss on quick reload
- **Data loss fix**: `flushPendingSave()` + `syncNow(true)` on `visibilityState: hidden` ensures debounced saves are flushed before page reload
- Cloud relay for near-instant sync planned as follow-up (#118, supersedes #104)

### Projected Recurring Transactions (2026-03-03)

- **Projected transactions** — Future recurring transactions now appear as projections in the transactions list for any future month, giving users visibility into upcoming expenses/income
- **Deferred side effects** — Clicking a projected transaction offers scope selection (this only / this and future / all). Side effects (materializing a transaction or splitting a recurring item) are deferred until the user saves, preventing orphaned records on cancel
- **RecurringEditScopeModal** — Shared global modal for scope selection, registered in `App.vue`
- **`useProjectedTransactions` composable** — Generates ephemeral projected `DisplayTransaction` entries from active recurring items for the selected month
- **startDate → dayOfMonth sync** — Changing a recurring item's start date now auto-syncs the `dayOfMonth` field (clamped to 28) so that `syncLinkedTransactions` picks up the new day. Also syncs `monthOfYear` for yearly items
- **dayOfMonth field repositioned** — Moved between start date and end date in the recurring editor for better discoverability
- **Store immutability fixes** — Replaced all 19 in-place array mutations (`.push()`, `array[index]=`) with immutable patterns (spread, `.map()`) across 9 stores (accounts, family, goals, assets, todo, activity, budget, familyContext, tombstone). Prevents Vue 3.4+ computed reference-equality optimization from skipping re-evaluation
- **Today button on MonthNavigator** — Heritage Orange pill button appears next to month arrows when viewing a non-current month; clicking it jumps back to the current month
- 5 new TDD tests for startDate→dayOfMonth sync, all 659 tests passing

- **Scope modal moved to save time** — "This only / This & all future / All occurrences" modal now appears after the user clicks Save (not before opening the edit modal). Applies to both recurring activities and projected transactions. Users can see what they're changing before deciding scope.

### Google Drive Resilience Fixes (2026-03-09)

- **5xx retry with exponential backoff** — `GoogleDriveProvider` now retries on 503/5xx errors up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s). After exhausting retries on write, queues to offline flush instead of throwing unhandled.
- **Init file polling suppression** — `deferPolling()` / `startDeferredPolling()` prevents `setupAutoSync` from starting file polling until after `processRecurringItems` completes, breaking the init mutation → file poll → reload → more mutations cascade.
- **30-second init timeout** — If `loadFamilyData` takes longer than 30s (due to Drive API issues), the spinner is dismissed so the app is usable. Data continues loading in the background.

### Recent Fixes

- **Join flow cross-browser decrypt fix** — When a new member joined via invite link and created a password, the `joinFamily()` flow only stored a `passwordHash` in the Automerge doc but never created a `wrappedKey` entry in the V4 envelope. This meant password-based file decryption failed on different browsers/devices (e.g. Safari PWA after joining via Chrome on iOS, where storage is completely isolated). Fix: added `wrapFamilyKeyForMember()` to syncStore that derives an AES-KW wrapping key from the password and wraps the family key, called from `JoinPodView.handleCreatePassword()` before syncing.
- **Envelope merge race condition fix** — `fetchAndMergeRemote()` in `doSave()` was doing wholesale `currentEnvelope = remoteEnvelope` replacement, which could overwrite locally-added `inviteKeys`, `wrappedKeys`, and `passkeyWrappedKeys` when a prior auto-save wrote a version without them. Fix: merge local keys into remote envelope before assignment.
- **Family key cache on join fix** — `cacheFamilyKey()` silently returned when device was not trusted, causing data loss after page refresh or PWA install following a successful join. Fix: added `force` option to `cacheFamilyKey()` and force-cache during join/decrypt flows. Also fixed `App.vue` to redirect to `/welcome` when auto-decrypt fails instead of falling through to an empty Automerge doc.
- **Google Picker API for join flow** — When `drive.file` scope can't read a file shared by another user (returns 404), the join flow now shows a Google Picker button to let the invitee select the shared `.beanpod` file from their Drive (grants `drive.file` access). Includes `drivePicker.ts` service, `google-picker.d.ts` type declarations, and picker fallback UI in `JoinPodView.vue`. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-03-05-google-picker-invite-email-sharing.md`.
- **Email sharing in invite modal** — Optional email field in the invite modal (`FamilyPage.vue`) lets the pod owner share the `.beanpod` file with a family member's Google account directly via the Drive Permissions API. Uses `shareFileWithEmail()` in `driveService.ts`.
- **Google OAuth re-consent loop fix** — Three-layer fix preventing PWA users from being forced to re-consent on every page refresh:
  1. `getValidToken()` and 401 fallbacks in `googleDriveProvider.ts` now pass `forceConsent: true` when no refresh token exists (Google only issues refresh tokens with `prompt=consent`)
  2. `App.vue` requests `navigator.storage.persist()` on startup to prevent browser eviction of IndexedDB
  3. Refresh tokens dual-written to IndexedDB + localStorage as defense-in-depth against storage eviction (iOS Safari 7-day policy, PWA storage pressure)
  - New `hasRefreshToken()` export in `googleAuth.ts` for cross-module access
  - Plan: `docs/plans/2026-03-04-fix-oauth-reconsent-loop.md`
- **Multi-family isolation hardening** — Fixed cross-family data leakage when authenticated user's familyId could not be resolved:
  - Added cached session familyId as 4th fallback in auth resolution chain (JWT → getUserAttributes → registry → cached session)
  - Authenticated users no longer fall back to `lastActiveFamilyId` (which could belong to a different user)
  - Placeholder family creation now uses auth-resolved ID instead of random UUID (`createFamilyWithId()`)
  - Sync service refuses to load sync file whose `familyId` doesn't match the active family (in `loadAndImport`, `openAndLoadFile`, `decryptAndImport`)
  - Sync service skips initialization when no active family is set (prevents legacy key fallback)
  - Sync service `reset()` clears stale file handles and session passwords on family switch
  - Sync service tracks `currentFileHandleFamilyId` — `save()` blocks writes if handle belongs to a different family
  - Added `closeDatabase()` before loading family data to ensure clean DB connection
  - 22 multi-family isolation tests (up from 19)
- **BaseModal scroll fix** — Modal body now uses `flex-1 overflow-y-auto` with `max-h-[calc(100vh-2rem)]` so tall content scrolls instead of overflowing below the viewport (discovered via asset loan form E2E tests)
- Restored ReportsPage that was wiped during bulk ESLint/Prettier formatting
- Added data-testid attributes to transaction items and account cards for E2E tests
- Fixed E2E tests to switch to transactions tab before interacting with elements
- Switched from idb library to native IndexedDB APIs

## v6 UI Framework Proposal

A v6 UI framework proposal has been uploaded to `docs/brand/beanies-ui-framework-proposal-v6.html`, superseding v5 with detailed login flow screens for the new file-based authentication model. The v3 proposal was previously removed as obsolete.

v6 introduces a **six-screen authentication flow** built around the Pod concept (encrypted `.beanpod` data files):

- **00a: Welcome Gate** — Three paths: sign in, create pod, join pod
- **00b: Load Your Pod** — File picker + drag-drop zone + cloud storage connectors (Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud)
- **00b-2: Unlock Your Pod** — Decrypt loaded file with pod password
- **00b-3: Pick Your Bean** — Family member selection with 88px avatars and onboarding status indicators
- **00c: Create a New Pod** — 3-step wizard (name/password → storage → invite)
- **00d: Join an Existing Pod** — Family code or magic link entry

Additionally, v6 includes all previous v4/v5 screens: Dashboard, Accounts (card + list), Budgets, Transactions, Onboarding, Family Hub, Mobile (4 phone mockups), Landing Page, and Settings.

## v7 UI Framework Proposal

A v7 UI framework proposal has been uploaded to `docs/brand/beanies-ui-framework-proposal-v7.html`, introducing a major structural reorganisation: the app shifts from finance-first to **family-first**, with three new pages and a collapsible accordion sidebar.

### Key Changes in v7

1. **Sidebar accordion restructure** — Flat nav replaced with two collapsible sections:
   - **The Piggy Bank 🐷** (finance): Overview, Accounts, Budgets, Transactions

2. **Family Nook 🏡** — New home screen after login (replaces finance dashboard as entry point). Shows today's schedule, events, milestones, activity feed, shared to-do widget, and Piggy Bank quick-access card

3. **Family Planner 📅** — Calendar and scheduling hub absorbing the old Family Hub calendar. Month/week/day/agenda views, event categorisation, family member filtering

4. **Family To-Do ✅** — Standalone task management page at `/todo`. Quick-add, assignees, date integration with calendar. Purple (#9B59B6) accent colour for to-do elements

5. **Updated mobile bottom tab bar** — 5 tabs: 🏡 Nook, 📅 Planner, 🐷 Piggy Bank, 📋 Budget, 👨‍👩‍👦 Pod

6. **Family Hub updated** — Calendar removed (→ Family Planner), now focused on personal member activity and milestones

7. **Budget page enhancements** — 3 transaction entry methods (Quick Add, Batch Add, CSV Upload), time-position marker, motivational emoji messages, category spending bars

8. **Transactions ledger** — Recurring/one-time type pills, summary pills, enhanced add modal with recurring toggle

## Known Issues

- **Single-family re-login shows LoadPodView instead of auto-decrypting:** When a single family exists and the user clicks "Sign In" after sign-out, `tryAutoDecrypt` fails because `cacheFamilyKey()` only stores the key on trusted devices (`isTrustedDevice === true`). On non-trusted devices, the cached family key is empty, so auto-decrypt falls through to the LoadPodView password form. Needs investigation: either always cache the family key after explicit password entry, or prompt for trusted device earlier in the flow.
- ~~**Data loss after tab idle/sleep — saves fail silently:** After waking from sleep and visiting Settings to check last-saved timestamp, all subsequent saves failed with "no family key or envelope". Data created after visiting Settings was lost on refresh.~~ **Fixed 2026-03-10** — Root cause: `SettingsPage.vue` called `syncStore.initialize()` on mount, which called `syncService.reset()` clearing the encryption key from the sync service (but not the Vue ref). Four-layer fix: (1) removed redundant init from SettingsPage, (2) `syncService.initialize()` skips destructive re-init when already active for same family, (3) `loadFromFile()` now calls `setFamilyKey()` instead of `setEnvelope()` to restore key on every file poll, (4) save-on-hide/unload handlers recover the key from the store ref before saving.
- ~~**Google Drive new account registration fails:** Two errors: (1) "authorization scope was not enough" — granular consent lets users deselect scopes, (2) "File not found" — global folder cache reuses a previous account's folder ID.~~ **Fixed 2026-03-04** — clear folder cache + force consent in `createNew()`, validate `drive.file` scope after token exchange, clear cache on auth failure.
